content.title: What Are Web Services?
content.explanation:
**Understanding the Foundation of Modern Application Communication:**

**Definition:** A web service is a standardized way of enabling communication between different software applications over the internet. It allows applications built on different platforms, programming languages, and technologies to exchange data and functionality.

**Real-World Analogy:** Think of web services like universal power adapters:
- Different countries have different plug shapes (different platforms)
- A universal adapter (web service) allows any device to connect to any outlet
- The adapter follows a standard (HTTP, XML, JSON) that both sides understand

**Why Web Services Are Essential:**

1. **Interoperability:** Connect applications built with different technologies
   - Java application talking to .NET service
   - Python client consuming PHP API
   - Mobile app accessing mainframe backend

2. **Language Independence:** Clients and services can be in any language

3. **Platform Independence:** Works across Windows, Linux, macOS, mobile

4. **Reusability:** One service can be used by multiple clients

5. **Scalability:** Services can be scaled independently

6. **Maintainability:** Services can be updated without affecting clients

**How Web Services Work:**

```
Client Application                    Server Application
     |                                        |
     | --- Request (XML/JSON) --->           |
     |                                        |
     |                                        |
     | <--- Response (XML/JSON) ---           |
     |                                        |
```

1. **Client** creates a request in standard format (XML/JSON)
2. **Request** is sent over network using HTTP/HTTPS
3. **Server** processes the request
4. **Server** sends response back in standard format
5. **Client** parses and uses the response

**Common Use Cases:**

| Industry | Example | Web Service Type |
|----------|---------|------------------|
| E-commerce | Product catalog, orders, payments | REST APIs |
| Banking | Account balance, transfers | SOAP (security) |
| Social Media | Post, like, share | REST/GraphQL |
| Weather | Current conditions, forecasts | REST |
| Payment Processing | Credit card transactions | SOAP |
| Mobile Apps | User data, notifications | REST/GraphQL |
| IoT Devices | Sensor data, device control | REST/MQTT |

**Evolution of Web Services:**

```
1990s: CORBA, DCOM (Complex, platform-specific)
   ↓
2000s: SOAP/XML-RPC (Standardized, but heavy)
   ↓
2010s: REST/JSON (Lightweight, popular)
   ↓
2015+: GraphQL, gRPC (Flexible, performant)
```

**Core Components of Web Services:**

1. **Transport Protocol:** Usually HTTP/HTTPS
2. **Message Format:** XML (SOAP), JSON (REST/GraphQL)
3. **Service Description:** WSDL (SOAP), OpenAPI (REST), Schema (GraphQL)
4. **Service Discovery:** UDDI (SOAP), API Gateways (modern)

**Key Terminology:**

- **Endpoint:** URL where service is accessed
- **Operation/Method:** Specific function to call
- **Request:** Message sent to service
- **Response:** Message returned from service
- **Payload:** Actual data being transmitted
- **Headers:** Metadata about the request/response
- **Status Code:** HTTP status indicating result

**In the Context of SoapUI Testing:**

SoapUI supports all major web service types:
- **SOAP Projects:** Import WSDL, generate requests
- **REST Projects:** Define resources and methods
- **GraphQL:** Send queries and mutations

This makes SoapUI an ideal tool for testing any web service, regardless of its architecture.

content.title: SOAP (Simple Object Access Protocol) Deep Dive
content.explanation:
**Complete Understanding of the SOAP Protocol:**

**What is SOAP?**
SOAP is a protocol specification for exchanging structured information in web services. It relies on XML for message format and typically uses HTTP or SMTP for message negotiation and transmission.

**Key Characteristics:**

✅ **Protocol-based:** SOAP is a formal protocol with strict rules
✅ **XML-only:** Messages must be in XML format
✅ **WSDL-defined:** Contract-first approach with service description
✅ **Stateful:** Can maintain session state
✅ **Built-in error handling:** SOAP faults for errors
✅ **Extensible:** WS-* standards for security, transactions
✅ **Language/Platform independent:** Works across technologies

**SOAP Message Structure:**

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<soap:Envelope
  xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"
  xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
  xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  
  <soap:Header>
    <!-- Optional header information -->
    <auth:Authentication 
      xmlns:auth="http://example.com/authentication">
      <auth:Username>john.doe</auth:Username>
      <auth:Password>secure123</auth:Password>
      <auth:Token>ABC123XYZ</auth:Token>
    </auth:Authentication>
    
    <transaction:Transaction 
      xmlns:transaction="http://example.com/transaction">
      <transaction:ID>TX-2024-001</transaction:ID>
      <transaction:Timestamp>2024-02-28T10:30:00Z</transaction:Timestamp>
    </transaction:Transaction>
  </soap:Header>
  
  <soap:Body>
    <!-- Main request/response data -->
    <getWeather xmlns="http://example.com/weather">
      <city>New York</city>
      <country>US</country>
      <units>metric</units>
    </getWeather>
  </soap:Body>
  
  <soap:Fault>
    <!-- Optional error information (if error occurred) -->
    <faultcode>soap:Client</faultcode>
    <faultstring>Invalid city name</faultstring>
    <detail>
      <error:Details xmlns:error="http://example.com/errors">
        <error:Code>ERR-001</error:Code>
        <error:Message>City 'New Yorkk' not found</error:Message>
      </error:Details>
    </detail>
  </soap:Fault>
  
</soap:Envelope>
```

**SOAP Envelope Elements Explained:**

| Element | Required | Purpose |
|---------|----------|---------|
| **Envelope** | Yes | Root element, identifies XML as SOAP message |
| **Header** | No | Contains metadata (authentication, routing, transactions) |
| **Body** | Yes | Contains the actual request/response data |
| **Fault** | No | Contains error information if processing failed |

**WSDL (Web Services Description Language):**

WSDL is an XML document that describes a SOAP web service. It's like a contract that defines:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<definitions name="WeatherService"
  targetNamespace="http://example.com/weather.wsdl"
  xmlns="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/"
  xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/soap/"
  xmlns:tns="http://example.com/weather.wsdl"
  xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  
  <!-- Data types used by the service -->
  <types>
    <xsd:schema targetNamespace="http://example.com/weather.xsd">
      <xsd:element name="GetWeatherRequest">
        <xsd:complexType>
          <xsd:sequence>
            <xsd:element name="city" type="xsd:string"/>
            <xsd:element name="country" type="xsd:string"/>
          </xsd:sequence>
        </xsd:complexType>
      </xsd:element>
      
      <xsd:element name="GetWeatherResponse">
        <xsd:complexType>
          <xsd:sequence>
            <xsd:element name="temperature" type="xsd:float"/>
            <xsd:element name="condition" type="xsd:string"/>
            <xsd:element name="humidity" type="xsd:string"/>
          </xsd:sequence>
        </xsd:complexType>
      </xsd:element>
    </xsd:schema>
  </types>
  
  <!-- Messages (request and response) -->
  <message name="GetWeatherRequestMessage">
    <part name="parameters" element="tns:GetWeatherRequest"/>
  </message>
  
  <message name="GetWeatherResponseMessage">
    <part name="parameters" element="tns:GetWeatherResponse"/>
  </message>
  
  <!-- Port type (operations) -->
  <portType name="WeatherPortType">
    <operation name="GetWeather">
      <input message="tns:GetWeatherRequestMessage"/>
      <output message="tns:GetWeatherResponseMessage"/>
      <fault name="InvalidCity" message="tns:InvalidCityFault"/>
    </operation>
  </portType>
  
  <!-- Binding (how to access) -->
  <binding name="WeatherBinding" type="tns:WeatherPortType">
    <soap:binding style="document" 
      transport="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/http"/>
    <operation name="GetWeather">
      <soap:operation soapAction="http://example.com/GetWeather"/>
      <input>
        <soap:body use="literal"/>
      </input>
      <output>
        <soap:body use="literal"/>
      </output>
    </operation>
  </binding>
  
  <!-- Service (endpoint URL) -->
  <service name="WeatherService">
    <port name="WeatherPort" binding="tns:WeatherBinding">
      <soap:address 
        location="http://api.example.com/weather"/>
    </port>
  </service>
</definitions>
```

**WS-* Standards (Extensions):**

| Standard | Purpose | Use Case |
|----------|---------|----------|
| **WS-Security** | Message-level security | Banking, healthcare |
| **WS-Addressing** | Routing information | Enterprise service buses |
| **WS-ReliableMessaging** | Guaranteed delivery | Financial transactions |
| **WS-AtomicTransaction** | Distributed transactions | Order processing |
| **WS-Policy** | Capability declaration | Service negotiation |

**SOAP Request/Response Example:**

**Request:**
```xml
POST /weather HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 456
SOAPAction: "http://example.com/GetWeather"

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  <soap:Body>
    <GetWeather xmlns="http://example.com/weather">
      <city>London</city>
      <country>UK</country>
    </GetWeather>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**Response:**
```xml
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 678

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  <soap:Body>
    <GetWeatherResponse xmlns="http://example.com/weather">
      <temperature>15.5</temperature>
      <condition>Partly Cloudy</condition>
      <humidity>72%</humidity>
      <wind>8 mph</wind>
      <visibility>10 miles</visibility>
    </GetWeatherResponse>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**SOAP Fault Example (Error):**
```xml
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  <soap:Body>
    <soap:Fault>
      <faultcode>soap:Client</faultcode>
      <faultstring>Invalid city name</faultstring>
      <detail>
        <error:Details xmlns:error="http://example.com/errors">
          <error:Code>WEA-001</error:Code>
          <error:Message>City 'Londn' not found. Did you mean 'London'?</error:Message>
          <error:Suggestions>
            <error:Suggestion>London</error:Suggestion>
            <error:Suggestion>Londonderry</error:Suggestion>
          </error:Suggestions>
        </error:Details>
      </detail>
    </soap:Fault>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**SOAP in SoapUI:**

SoapUI has excellent SOAP support:

1. **Import WSDL:** Automatically generates requests
2. **XML Editing:** Syntax highlighting, validation
3. **XPath Assertions:** Validate specific XML nodes
4. **SOAP Fault Testing:** Test error handling
5. **WS-Security:** Add security headers
6. **Multiple Operations:** Test all operations easily

```xml
<!-- SoapUI-generated request template -->
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  <soap:Body>
    <Add xmlns="http://tempuri.org/">
      <intA>?</intA>
      <intB>?</intB>
    </Add>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**SOAP Pros and Cons:**

| Pros | Cons |
|------|------|
| ✅ Built-in error handling (Faults) | ❌ Heavy, verbose XML |
| ✅ Security standards (WS-Security) | ❌ Slower parsing and transmission |
| ✅ Transaction support | ❌ Complex WSDL files |
| ✅ Formal contract (WSDL) | ❌ Steeper learning curve |
| ✅ Stateful operations possible | ❌ Limited to XML |
| ✅ Enterprise-grade features | ❌ Not browser-friendly |

**When to Use SOAP:**

✅ **Financial services** - Need security and transactions
✅ **Healthcare systems** - HIPAA compliance, reliability
✅ **Telecom** - Billing systems, stateful operations
✅ **Enterprise integrations** - Legacy systems, ESB
✅ **Government systems** - Strict contracts, compliance
✅ **Payment gateways** - Security, reliability

**Real-World SOAP Examples:**
- PayPal API
- Salesforce SOAP API
- FedEx Shipping API
- Amazon Marketplace Web Service
- Microsoft .NET Web Services

content.title: REST (Representational State Transfer) Deep Dive
content.explanation:
**Complete Understanding of REST Architecture:**

**What is REST?**
REST is an architectural style for designing networked applications. It relies on stateless, client-server communication, typically over HTTP. REST is not a protocol but a set of constraints and principles.

**Key Characteristics:**

✅ **Resource-based:** Everything is a resource identified by URL
✅ **Stateless:** Each request contains all necessary information
✅ **HTTP Methods:** Standard operations (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
✅ **Multiple Formats:** JSON, XML, text, HTML, YAML
✅ **Cacheable:** Responses can be cached for performance
✅ **Uniform Interface:** Consistent resource manipulation
✅ **Layered System:** Can have intermediaries (proxies, gateways)

**The 6 REST Constraints:**

1. **Client-Server Architecture**
   - Separation of concerns
   - Clients don't worry about data storage
   - Servers don't worry about user interface

2. **Stateless**
   - Each request contains all info needed
   - No client context stored on server
   - Session state kept on client

3. **Cacheable**
   - Responses must define themselves as cacheable/not
   - Improves performance and scalability

4. **Uniform Interface**
   - Resources identified in requests (URIs)
   - Resource representation (JSON, XML)
   - Self-descriptive messages
   - HATEOAS (Hypermedia as Engine of Application State)

5. **Layered System**
   - Client can't tell if connected directly to server
   - Intermediaries (proxies, load balancers) possible

6. **Code on Demand (Optional)**
   - Server can send executable code (JavaScript)

**REST Resource Modeling:**

```
Resources are nouns, not verbs:

❌ /getUser
❌ /createOrder
❌ /deleteProduct

✅ /users
✅ /orders
✅ /products
```

**HTTP Methods and Their Meanings:**

| Method | CRUD Operation | Idempotent | Safe | Use Case |
|--------|----------------|------------|------|----------|
| **GET** | Read | ✓ Yes | ✓ Yes | Retrieve resource |
| **POST** | Create | ✗ No | ✗ No | Create new resource |
| **PUT** | Update/Replace | ✓ Yes | ✗ No | Update entire resource |
| **PATCH** | Partial Update | ✗ No | ✗ No | Update part of resource |
| **DELETE** | Delete | ✓ Yes | ✗ No | Remove resource |
| **HEAD** | Read headers | ✓ Yes | ✓ Yes | Get metadata only |
| **OPTIONS** | Discover | ✓ Yes | ✓ Yes | Get allowed methods |

**HTTP Status Codes:**

```
1xx: Informational
   100 Continue
   101 Switching Protocols

2xx: Success
   200 OK
   201 Created
   202 Accepted
   204 No Content

3xx: Redirection
   301 Moved Permanently
   302 Found
   304 Not Modified
   307 Temporary Redirect

4xx: Client Error
   400 Bad Request
   401 Unauthorized
   403 Forbidden
   404 Not Found
   405 Method Not Allowed
   409 Conflict
   422 Unprocessable Entity
   429 Too Many Requests

5xx: Server Error
   500 Internal Server Error
   502 Bad Gateway
   503 Service Unavailable
   504 Gateway Timeout
```

**REST API URL Design:**

```
Base URL: https://api.example.com/v1/

Collection URLs:
  GET    /users          - List all users
  POST   /users          - Create new user
  GET    /users/123      - Get user 123
  PUT    /users/123      - Update user 123
  PATCH  /users/123      - Partially update user 123
  DELETE /users/123      - Delete user 123

Nested Resources:
  GET    /users/123/orders    - List orders for user 123
  POST   /users/123/orders    - Create order for user 123
  GET    /orders/456          - Get order 456

Query Parameters:
  GET /users?role=admin&status=active
  GET /users?page=2&limit=50
  GET /orders?sort=-created&fields=id,status

Filtering, Sorting, Pagination:
  ?filter[name]=John&filter[age]=25
  ?sort=name,-createdAt
  ?page=3&per_page=20
  ?offset=40&limit=10
```

**REST Request Examples:**

**GET Request (Retrieve):**
```http
GET /api/users/123 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Accept: application/json
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
```

**GET Response:**
```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 245
Cache-Control: max-age=3600

{
  "id": 123,
  "name": "John Doe",
  "email": "john@example.com",
  "role": "admin",
  "createdAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "_links": {
    "self": {"href": "/users/123"},
    "orders": {"href": "/users/123/orders"}
  }
}
```

**POST Request (Create):**
```http
POST /api/users HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...

{
  "name": "Jane Smith",
  "email": "jane@example.com",
  "role": "user",
  "password": "SecurePass123"
}
```

**POST Response:**
```http
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Location: /api/users/456
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "id": 456,
  "name": "Jane Smith",
  "email": "jane@example.com",
  "role": "user",
  "createdAt": "2024-02-28T14:20:00Z",
  "_links": {
    "self": {"href": "/users/456"}
  }
}
```

**PUT Request (Replace):**
```http
PUT /api/users/456 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "Jane R. Smith",
  "email": "jane.smith@example.com",
  "role": "manager"
}
```

**PATCH Request (Partial Update):**
```http
PATCH /api/users/456 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "role": "admin"
}
```

**DELETE Request:**
```http
DELETE /api/users/456 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
```

**DELETE Response:**
```http
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
```

**REST Authentication Methods:**

| Method | Description | Use Case |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| **Basic Auth** | Username:password in header | Simple internal APIs |
| **Bearer Token** | JWT or token in Authorization header | Stateless APIs |
| **API Key** | Key in header or query param | Public APIs |
| **OAuth 2.0** | Token-based authorization | Third-party access |
| **JWT** | Self-contained JSON tokens | Distributed systems |

**REST API Versioning Strategies:**

```
1. URL Path:    /api/v1/users
2. Query Param: /api/users?version=1
3. Header:      Accept: application/vnd.api.v1+json
4. Subdomain:   v1.api.example.com/users
```

**REST in SoapUI:**

SoapUI provides comprehensive REST testing:

1. **Create REST Project:** Enter base URL
2. **Add Resources:** Define endpoints
3. **Add Methods:** GET, POST, PUT, DELETE
4. **Parameters:** Query, header, body parameters
5. **JSONPath Assertions:** Validate JSON responses
6. **Authentication:** Configure auth methods

```xml
<!-- SoapUI REST request configuration -->
<restRequest name="Get User" method="GET">
  <endpoint>${#Project#baseUrl}/users/${userId}</endpoint>
  <headers>
    <header name="Authorization">Bearer ${authToken}</header>
  </headers>
  <assertions>
    <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes">
      <codes>200,304</codes>
    </assertion>
    <assertion type="JSONPath Match">
      <path>$.id</path>
      <value>${userId}</value>
    </assertion>
  </assertions>
</restRequest>
```

**REST Pros and Cons:**

| Pros | Cons |
|------|------|
| ✅ Lightweight (JSON) | ❌ No built-in security |
| ✅ Fast parsing | ❌ No standard contract |
| ✅ Caching support | ❌ Over-fetching/under-fetching |
| ✅ Browser-friendly | ❌ Multiple round trips |
| ✅ Simple and intuitive | ❌ Versioning complexity |
| ✅ Scalable (stateless) | ❌ No built-in error handling |

**When to Use REST:**

✅ **Public APIs** - Simple, widely adopted
✅ **Mobile Apps** - Lightweight, fast
✅ **Web Applications** - JSON, browser-friendly
✅ **Microservices** - Simple communication
✅ **IoT Devices** - Lightweight, stateless
✅ **Cloud Services** - Scalable, cacheable

**Real-World REST Examples:**
- Twitter API
- GitHub API
- Stripe API
- Google Maps API
- Twilio API
- Slack API

content.title: GraphQL Deep Dive
SOAP vs REST vs GraphQL: Complete Comparison
Decision Framework: Choosing the Right Web Service Type
content.explanation:
**How to Choose Between SOAP, REST, and GraphQL:**

**Decision Matrix:**

```
Start: What are your requirements?
        |
        +-- Need formal contracts, transactions, built-in security? → SOAP
        |
        +-- Building public APIs, web/mobile apps? → REST or GraphQL
            |
            +-- Simple APIs, resource-based, need caching? → REST
            |
            +-- Complex UIs, multiple clients, need precise data? → GraphQL
```

**Choose SOAP When:**

✅ **Banking/Financial Applications**
- Need WS-Security, WS-AtomicTransaction
- Example: Payment processing, fund transfers

✅ **Healthcare Systems**
- Need reliability, auditing
- Example: HL7, FHIR interfaces

✅ **Enterprise Integration**
- Legacy systems, ESB
- Example: SAP, Oracle integrations

✅ **Government Systems**
- Strict contracts, compliance
- Example: Tax filing, permits

**Choose REST When:**

✅ **Public APIs**
- Simple, widely adopted
- Example: Weather API, Twitter API

✅ **Web Applications**
- Browser-friendly, JSON
- Example: E-commerce frontend

✅ **Mobile Apps**
- Lightweight, fast
- Example: Social media apps

✅ **Microservices**
- Simple communication
- Example: Internal services

✅ **IoT Devices**
- Lightweight, stateless
- Example: Sensor data collection

**Choose GraphQL When:**

✅ **Complex User Interfaces**
- Multiple data sources
- Example: Dashboard with user, orders, analytics

✅ **Mobile Apps with Bandwidth Constraints**
- Need exact data
- Example: News apps, social apps

✅ **Multiple Clients (Web, iOS, Android)**
- Different data needs
- Example: E-commerce platform

✅ **Rapid Frontend Development**
- Frontend changes without backend
- Example: Startup MVPs

✅ **Aggregating Multiple Services**
- API gateway pattern
- Example: Microservices frontend

**Comparative Example: User Profile with Orders**

**REST Approach:**
```http
# Multiple round trips
GET /users/123              # Get user data
GET /users/123/orders       # Get user orders
GET /orders/456/items       # Get order items

Total data: All fields from all endpoints
```

**GraphQL Approach:**
```graphql
query {
  user(id: "123") {
    name
    email
    orders {
      id
      date
      items {
        product
        quantity
        price
      }
    }
  }
}
```
```json
{
  "data": {
    "user": {
      "name": "John Doe",
      "email": "john@example.com",
      "orders": [
        {
          "id": "456",
          "date": "2024-02-28",
          "items": [
            {
              "product": "Laptop",
              "quantity": 1,
              "price": 999.99
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**Single request, exact data needed**

**SOAP Approach (if needed):**
```xml
<soap:Envelope>
  <soap:Body>
    <GetUserProfile>
      <userId>123</userId>
      <includeOrders>true</includeOrders>
      <includeItems>true</includeItems>
    </GetUserProfile>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**Heavy XML, but single request with custom operation**

**Hybrid Approaches:**

Many organizations use multiple approaches:
- **REST** for public APIs
- **GraphQL** for internal UIs
- **SOAP** for legacy integration

**Example Architecture:**
```
Mobile App (GraphQL)     Web App (GraphQL)     Third-party (REST)
        |                      |                      |
        v                      v                      v
   [GraphQL Gateway] ←─── [GraphQL Gateway] ←─── [REST Gateway]
        |                      |                      |
        +----------------------+----------------------+
                               |
                               v
                     [Microservices Layer]
                               |
          +--------------------+--------------------+
          |                    |                    |
          v                    v                    v
     User Service        Order Service         Payment Service
     (REST)               (REST)                (SOAP with Bank)
```

**Migration Paths:**

1. **SOAP → REST**
   - Wrap SOAP services with REST facade
   - Gradually migrate clients

2. **REST → GraphQL**
   - Add GraphQL gateway in front of REST services
   - Clients adopt GraphQL incrementally

3. **SOAP → GraphQL**
   - GraphQL gateway with SOAP resolvers
   - Migrate as services are rewritten

content.title: How SoapUI Handles Different Web Service Types
content.explanation:
**Comprehensive Guide to SoapUI's Web Service Support:**

**SoapUI Architecture for Web Services:**

```
SoapUI Application
├── SOAP Testing Engine
│   ├── WSDL Importer
│   ├── XML Processor
│   ├── XPath Validator
│   └── WS-Security Handler
├── REST Testing Engine
│   ├── OpenAPI Importer
│   ├── JSON Processor
│   ├── JSONPath Validator
│   └── Auth Handlers (OAuth, JWT)
├── GraphQL Support
│   ├── Schema Introspection
│   ├── Query Builder
│   └── Variable Handler
└── Common Components
    ├── HTTP Client
    ├── Assertions Engine
    ├── Property Expansion
    └── Reporting Module
```

**1. SOAP Web Services in SoapUI:**

**Creating a SOAP Project:**

```xml
<!-- Step 1: Import WSDL -->
<soapui-project name="BankingService">
  <interface type="wsdl">
    <definition>
      https://example.com/banking?wsdl
    </definition>
  </interface>
</soapui-project>
```

**Generated Operations:**
```
- GetAccountBalance
- TransferFunds
- GetTransactionHistory
- ValidateAccount
```

**Sample Request Template:**
```xml
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  <soap:Header>
    <wsse:Security xmlns:wsse="http://docs.oasis-open.org/wss/2004/01/oasis-200401-wss-wssecurity-secext-1.0.xsd">
      <wsse:UsernameToken>
        <wsse:Username>${username}</wsse:Username>
        <wsse:Password>${password}</wsse:Password>
      </wsse:UsernameToken>
    </wsse:Security>
  </soap:Header>
  <soap:Body>
    <GetAccountBalance xmlns="http://example.com/banking">
      <accountNumber>${accountNumber}</accountNumber>
    </GetAccountBalance>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**SoapUI SOAP Features:**

✅ **WSDL Validation:** Check WSDL correctness
✅ **Multiple Bindings:** SOAP 1.1 and 1.2
✅ **WS-Security:** Add security headers
✅ **MTOM/XOP:** Handle attachments
✅ **SOAP Fault Testing:** Test error scenarios
✅ **XPath Assertions:** Validate XML responses

**2. REST Web Services in SoapUI:**

**Creating a REST Project:**

```xml
<soapui-project name="EcommerceAPI">
  <restResource name="products" path="/products">
    <restMethod name="GET"/>
    <restMethod name="POST"/>
  </restResource>
  <restResource name="product" path="/products/{id}">
    <restMethod name="GET"/>
    <restMethod name="PUT"/>
    <restMethod name="DELETE"/>
  </restResource>
</soapui-project>
```

**Request Configuration:**
```xml
<restRequest name="Get Product" method="GET">
  <endpoint>${#Project#baseUrl}/products/${productId}</endpoint>
  <headers>
    <header name="Authorization">Bearer ${authToken}</header>
    <header name="Accept">application/json</header>
  </headers>
  <parameters>
    <parameter name="includeDetails" value="true"/>
  </parameters>
</restRequest>
```

**SoapUI REST Features:**

✅ **OpenAPI/Swagger Import:** Auto-create requests
✅ **JSONPath Assertions:** Validate JSON responses
✅ **OAuth 2.0 Support:** Authentication flows
✅ **Query Parameters:** Easy parameter management
✅ **Header Management:** Request/response headers
✅ **Cookie Support:** Session management

**3. GraphQL in SoapUI:**

**GraphQL Request Setup:**

```xml
<restRequest name="GraphQL Query" method="POST">
  <endpoint>${#Project#graphqlUrl}</endpoint>
  <headers>
    <header name="Content-Type">application/json</header>
  </headers>
  <request>
    <![CDATA[
    {
      "query": "
        query GetUser($userId: ID!, $includePosts: Boolean!) {
          user(id: $userId) {
            id
            name
            email
            posts @include(if: $includePosts) {
              title
              content
            }
          }
        }
      ",
      "variables": {
        "userId": "123",
        "includePosts": true
      }
    }
    ]]>
  </request>
</restRequest>
```

**SoapUI GraphQL Features:**

✅ **Schema Introspection:** Query available types
✅ **Variable Handling:** Separate variables
✅ **Fragments Support:** Reusable query parts
✅ **Complex Queries:** Nested fields
✅ **Mutations:** Write operations

**4. Common Testing Patterns Across All Types:**

**Data-Driven Testing:**
```xml
<testCase name="User Registration">
  <dataSource>
    <type>CSV</type>
    <file>${projectDir}/users.csv</file>
  </dataSource>
  
  <testStep name="Create User">
    <!-- Works with SOAP, REST, or GraphQL -->
    <config>
      <endpoint>${#Project#endpoint}</endpoint>
      <request>${requestTemplate}</request>
    </config>
  </testStep>
  
  <dataSourceLoop>
    <testSteps>Create User</testSteps>
  </dataSourceLoop>
</testCase>
```

**Assertion Patterns:**

```groovy
// SOAP XPath Assertion
assert context.response.contains('//AddResult[text()="25"]')

// REST JSONPath Assertion
def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(context.response)
assert json.data[0].id == expectedId

// GraphQL Response Assertion
assert json.data.user.name == expectedName
assert json.errors == null
```

**Property Transfer Examples:**

```xml
<!-- Transfer value from one response to next request -->
<transfer>
  <source type="response" step="CreateUser">
    <!-- SOAP XPath -->
    <path>//userId</path>
    <!-- REST JSONPath -->
    <path>$.userId</path>
    <!-- GraphQL path -->
    <path>data.createUser.id</path>
  </source>
  <target type="request" step="GetUser">
    <path>userId</path>
  </target>
</transfer>
```

**5. Service Type Detection in SoapUI:**

SoapUI automatically detects service type:

```java
// Internal detection logic
if (project.hasInterface() && project.getInterface().getType() == "wsdl") {
    // SOAP project
    handleSOAPProject(project);
} else if (project.getResourceList().size() > 0) {
    // REST project
    handleRESTProject(project);
} else if (request.getMediaType() == "application/json" &&
           request.getRequestContent().contains(""query"")) {
    // GraphQL request
    handleGraphQLRequest(request);
}
```

**6. Unified Features Across Types:**

| Feature | SOAP | REST | GraphQL |
|---------|------|------|---------|
| **Assertions** | XPath | JSONPath | Custom |
| **Data Sources** | ✓ CSV/Excel | ✓ CSV/Excel | ✓ CSV/Excel |
| **Property Transfer** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| **Groovy Scripting** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| **Load Testing** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| **Security Testing** | ✓ | ✓ | Limited |
| **Mock Services** | ✓ | ✓ | Limited |
| **CI/CD Integration** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

**7. Practical Example: Testing All Three Types:**

```groovy
// Test script that works with any service type
def testService(serviceType, endpoint, request) {
    switch(serviceType) {
        case "SOAP":
            // Create SOAP request
            def soapRequest = """
                <soap:Envelope>
                    <soap:Body>
                        ${request}
                    </soap:Body>
                </soap:Envelope>
            """
            return sendSoapRequest(endpoint, soapRequest)
            
        case "REST":
            // Send REST request
            return sendRestRequest(endpoint, request)
            
        case "GraphQL":
            // Build GraphQL query
            def graphQLRequest = [
                query: request,
                variables: [:]
            ]
            return sendGraphQLRequest(endpoint, graphQLRequest)
    }
}

// Assert regardless of type
def validateResponse(serviceType, response, expected) {
    switch(serviceType) {
        case "SOAP":
            assert response.contains("<AddResult>${expected}</AddResult>")
            break
        case "REST":
            def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
            assert json.result == expected
            break
        case "GraphQL":
            def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
            assert json.data.add.result == expected
            break
    }
}
```

**8. SoapUI's Advantages for Multi-Protocol Testing:**

✅ **Single Tool for All:** Test SOAP, REST, GraphQL together
✅ **Unified Reporting:** Consistent test results
✅ **Common Assertions:** Same assertion patterns
✅ **Reusable Components:** Share test data and scripts
✅ **Integrated Workflows:** Mix service types in one test case
✅ **Learning Curve:** Learn once, test everything

**Example Multi-Protocol Test Case:**

```xml
<testCase name="End-to-End Order Processing">
  <!-- Step 1: REST - Create Order -->
  <testStep name="Create Order" type="restrequest"/>
  
  <!-- Step 2: SOAP - Process Payment -->
  <testStep name="Process Payment" type="soaprequest"/>
  
  <!-- Step 3: GraphQL - Get Order Status -->
  <testStep name="Check Status" type="restrequest"/>
  
  <!-- Step 4: Assert with Groovy -->
  <testStep name="Verify" type="groovy"/>
</testCase>
```

This demonstrates SoapUI's unique ability to work with all web service types seamlessly, making it an invaluable tool for modern API testing where multiple protocols often coexist.

content.title: Practical Comparison: Same Operation Across All Types
content.scenario: Implementing a 'Get User' operation in SOAP, REST, and GraphQL
content.outcome: Understanding the differences through practical examples
content.details:
**Operation:** Get user information by ID

**1. SOAP Implementation:**

**WSDL Definition:**
```xml
<message name="GetUserRequest">
  <part name="userId" type="xsd:string"/>
</message>
<message name="GetUserResponse">
  <part name="user" element="tns:User"/>
</message>

<operation name="GetUser">
  <input message="tns:GetUserRequest"/>
  <output message="tns:GetUserResponse"/>
</operation>
```

**SOAP Request:**
```xml
<soap:Envelope>
  <soap:Body>
    <GetUser>
      <userId>123</userId>
    </GetUser>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**SOAP Response:**
```xml
<soap:Envelope>
  <soap:Body>
    <GetUserResponse>
      <User>
        <ID>123</ID>
        <Name>John Doe</Name>
        <Email>john@example.com</Email>
        <Age>30</Age>
        <Address>
          <Street>123 Main St</Street>
          <City>New York</City>
          <Zip>10001</Zip>
        </Address>
      </User>
    </GetUserResponse>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**Pros:** Complete, structured, schema-validated
**Cons:** Returns ALL fields (over-fetching)

**2. REST Implementation:**

**Endpoint:** `GET /api/users/123`

**REST Request:**
```http
GET /api/users/123 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Accept: application/json
```

**REST Response:**
```json
{
  "id": 123,
  "name": "John Doe",
  "email": "john@example.com",
  "age": 30,
  "address": {
    "street": "123 Main St",
    "city": "New York",
    "zip": "10001"
  }
}
```

**Pros:** Lightweight JSON, simple
**Cons:** Returns ALL fields (over-fetching)

**3. GraphQL Implementation:**

**GraphQL Schema:**
```graphql
type User {
  id: ID!
  name: String!
  email: String!
  age: Int
  address: Address
}

type Address {
  street: String!
  city: String!
  zip: String!
}

type Query {
  user(id: ID!): User
}
```

**GraphQL Request (Query):**
```graphql
query {
  user(id: "123") {
    name
    email
    address {
      city
    }
  }
}
```

**GraphQL Response:**
```json
{
  "data": {
    "user": {
      "name": "John Doe",
      "email": "john@example.com",
      "address": {
        "city": "New York"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Pros:** Returns EXACT fields requested
**Cons:** More complex initial setup

**Comparison Summary:**

| Aspect | SOAP | REST | GraphQL |
|--------|------|------|---------|
| **Request Size** | Large (XML) | Medium (JSON) | Small (query) |
| **Response Size** | Full data | Full data | Requested only |
| **Parsing Overhead** | High | Medium | Low |
| **Flexibility** | Low (fixed) | Low (fixed) | High (custom) |
| **Discoverability** | WSDL | OpenAPI | Introspection |
| **Caching** | No | Yes | Complex |
| **Versioning** | New service | New endpoints | Evolve schema |

**SoapUI Testing for All Three:**

```groovy
// Unified test script
def testGetUser(serviceType, userId) {
    def response
    
    switch(serviceType) {
        case "SOAP":
            response = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("SOAP GetUser").run(testRunner, context)
            assert response.contains("<ID>${userId}</ID>")
            break
            
        case "REST":
            response = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("REST GetUser").run(testRunner, context)
            def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
            assert json.id == userId.toInteger()
            break
            
        case "GraphQL":
            response = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("GraphQL GetUser").run(testRunner, context)
            def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
            assert json.data.user.id == userId
            break
    }
    
    log.info "${serviceType} test passed for user ${userId}"
}

// Test all three
testGetUser("SOAP", "123")
testGetUser("REST", "123") 
testGetUser("GraphQL", "123")
```

This example shows how SoapUI can consistently test all three types with minor adaptations, making it the ideal tool for organizations dealing with multiple web service architectures.

content.title: Comprehensive Protocol Coverage
content.explanation:
**Testing Any API, Any Protocol:**

SoapUI supports an extensive range of protocols, making it a universal testing tool for virtually any type of API or service.

**1. SOAP Protocol Support:**

**Full SOAP 1.1 and 1.2 Support:**
```xml
<!-- SOAP 1.1 -->
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  <soap:Body>
    <MyOperation>...</MyOperation>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>

<!-- SOAP 1.2 -->
<soap12:Envelope xmlns:soap12="http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope">
  <soap12:Body>
    <MyOperation>...</MyOperation>
  </soap12:Body>
</soap12:Envelope>
```

**WSDL Handling:**
- Import WSDL 1.1 and 2.0
- Generate requests automatically
- Validate against WSDL
- Multiple bindings support
- Complex types handling

**SOAP Extensions:**
- WS-Security (UsernameToken, X.509, SAML)
- WS-Addressing
- WS-Policy
- MTOM/XOP attachments
- SOAP with Attachments

**2. REST Protocol Support:**

**HTTP Methods:**
```http
GET     - Retrieve resources
POST    - Create resources
PUT     - Update/replace resources
PATCH   - Partial updates
DELETE  - Remove resources
HEAD    - Get headers only
OPTIONS - Discover allowed methods
```

**Content Types:**
- JSON (full support with JSONPath)
- XML (full support with XPath)
- HTML (for web testing)
- Plain text
- Binary data
- Form data (application/x-www-form-urlencoded)
- Multipart/form-data (file uploads)

**REST Features:**
- OpenAPI/Swagger import
- RAML support
- URI templates
- Query parameters
- Header management
- Cookie support
- Authentication (Basic, Digest, OAuth, JWT, API Key)

**3. JMS (Java Message Service) Support:**

**JMS Providers:**
```xml
<jmsConfig>
  <provider name="ActiveMQ">
    <initialContextFactory>org.apache.activemq.jndi.ActiveMQInitialContextFactory</initialContextFactory>
    <url>tcp://localhost:61616</url>
  </provider>
  <provider name="IBM MQ">
    <initialContextFactory>com.ibm.mq.jms.context.WMQInitialContextFactory</initialContextFactory>
    <url>iiop://localhost:2809</url>
  </provider>
</jmsConfig>
```

**JMS Operations:**
- Point-to-point (queues)
- Publish/subscribe (topics)
- Request/reply pattern
- Message selectors
- Durable subscriptions
- Transaction support

**Message Types:**
- TextMessage (XML, JSON)
- BytesMessage (binary)
- MapMessage (key-value)
- ObjectMessage (serialized objects)
- StreamMessage (primitive streams)

**JMS Headers:**
```xml
<jmsMessage>
  <headers>
    <header name="JMSCorrelationID">${correlationId}</header>
    <header name="JMSReplyTo">queue://response</header>
    <header name="JMSType">Order</header>
    <header name="JMSPriority">4</header>
    <header name="JMSDeliveryMode">PERSISTENT</header>
  </headers>
  <properties>
    <property name="customProperty">value</property>
  </properties>
</jmsMessage>
```

**4. AMF (Action Message Format) Support:**

**For Adobe Flex/Flash Applications:**
- Remoting services
- AMF0 and AMF3 encoding
- Complex object serialization
- Integration with BlazeDS

**AMF Configuration:**
```xml
<amfConfig>
  <endpoint>http://localhost:8080/flex/messagebroker/amf</endpoint>
  <remotingService>
    <destination>productService</destination>
    <method>getProducts</method>
    <arguments>
      <argument>${category}</argument>
    </arguments>
  </remotingService>
</amfConfig>
```

**5. JDBC (Database) Support:**

**Database Connectivity:**
```xml
<jdbcConfig>
  <driver>com.mysql.jdbc.Driver</driver>
  <connectionString>jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/testdb</connectionString>
  <username>testuser</username>
  <password>testpass</password>
</jdbcConfig>
```

**SQL Operations:**
- SELECT queries
- INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
- Stored procedures
- Batch operations
- Transaction management

**6. Additional Protocol Support:**

| Protocol | Use Case | SoapUI Support |
|----------|----------|----------------|
| **HTTP/HTTPS** | Web services | Full support, all methods |
| **JMS** | Messaging | Complete JMS 1.1 |
| **AMF** | Flex apps | AMF0/AMF3 |
| **JDBC** | Databases | All major databases |
| **SMTP/POP3/IMAP** | Email | Send/receive email |
| **FTP/SFTP** | File transfer | Upload/download |
| **TCP/UDP** | Raw sockets | Custom protocols |
| **RMI** | Java remoting | Basic support |
| **SOAP** | Web services | Full SOAP 1.1/1.2 |
| **REST** | Web APIs | Full REST support |
| **GraphQL** | Modern APIs | Via REST requests |

**7. Protocol Detection and Handling:**

SoapUI automatically detects protocol type:

```java
// Internal protocol detection
public ProtocolType detectProtocol(String content) {
    if (content.contains("<soap:Envelope")) {
        return ProtocolType.SOAP;
    } else if (content.trim().startsWith("{") || 
               content.trim().startsWith("[")) {
        return ProtocolType.REST_JSON;
    } else if (content.contains("<amf")) {
        return ProtocolType.AMF;
    } else if (content.contains("JMS")) {
        return ProtocolType.JMS;
    }
    return ProtocolType.UNKNOWN;
}
```

**8. Protocol-Specific Features:**

| Feature | SOAP | REST | JMS | AMF |
|---------|------|------|-----|-----|
| **WSDL/Swagger Import** | ✓ WSDL | ✓ OpenAPI | ✗ | ✗ |
| **Authentication** | WS-Security | OAuth, JWT | JMS | AMF |
| **Attachments** | MTOM | multipart | BytesMessage | AMF |
| **Assertions** | XPath | JSONPath | JMS | Custom |
| **Mock Services** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Limited |
| **Load Testing** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Limited |

**9. Multi-Protocol Test Cases:**

```xml
<testCase name="End-to-End Order Processing">
  <!-- Step 1: REST - Create Order -->
  <testStep name="Create Order" type="restrequest"/>
  
  <!-- Step 2: JMS - Notify Inventory -->
  <testStep name="JMS Notification" type="jms"/>
  
  <!-- Step 3: SOAP - Process Payment -->
  <testStep name="Payment" type="soaprequest"/>
  
  <!-- Step 4: JDBC - Update Database -->
  <testStep name="DB Update" type="jdbc"/>
  
  <!-- Step 5: AMF - Update UI -->
  <testStep name="Flex Update" type="amf"/>
</testCase>
```

**10. Protocol Support Summary:**

```
SoapUI Protocol Coverage
═══════════════════════════

SOAP ──────────────────► SOAP 1.1/1.2, WSDL, WS-*
REST ──────────────────► HTTP Methods, JSON/XML, OpenAPI
JMS ───────────────────► Queues, Topics, All JMS providers
AMF ───────────────────► AMF0/AMF3, Flex/Flash
JDBC ──────────────────► All major databases, SQL
EMAIL ─────────────────► SMTP, POP3, IMAP
FTP ───────────────────► FTP, SFTP, FTPS
TCP/UDP ───────────────► Raw socket communication

Supported Authentication
═══════════════════════
✓ Basic Auth
✓ Digest Auth
✓ OAuth 1.0/2.0
✓ JWT/Bearer Token
✓ API Key
✓ WS-Security
✓ NTLM
✓ Kerberos

Supported Data Formats
═══════════════════════
✓ XML
✓ JSON
✓ HTML
✓ Plain Text
✓ Binary
✓ Form Data
✓ Multipart
```

This extensive protocol support makes SoapUI the most versatile API testing tool available, capable of testing virtually any type of service in any technology stack.

content.title: Comprehensive Functional Testing Capabilities
content.explanation:
**Automating API Validation for Continuous Quality:**

SoapUI provides a complete framework for automating functional tests, enabling teams to validate API behavior systematically and repeatedly.

**1. Test Structure and Organization:**

```
Project
├── TestSuites (logical groups of tests)
│   ├── TestCase (individual test scenario)
│   │   ├── Setup Script (run before test)
│   │   ├── Test Steps (sequence of actions)
│   │   │   ├── HTTP/SOAP/JMS Request
│   │   │   ├── Groovy Script
│   │   │   ├── Property Transfer
│   │   │   ├── JDBC Request
│   │   │   └── Run TestCase (reuse)
│   │   ├── Assertions (per step)
│   │   └── Teardown Script (run after test)
│   └── Data Sources (external test data)
```

**2. Test Step Types:**

| Step Type | Purpose | Key Features |
|-----------|---------|--------------|
| **HTTP Request** | Call REST/SOAP APIs | All methods, headers, auth |
| **REST Request** | REST-specific calls | URI templates, parameters |
| **SOAP Request** | SOAP-specific calls | WSDL validation, WS-Security |
| **Groovy Script** | Custom logic | Full Groovy language, context access |
| **Property Transfer** | Move data between steps | XPath, JSONPath, regex |
| **JDBC Request** | Database queries | SQL, stored procedures |
| **JMS Request** | Message queues | Topics, queues, selectors |
| **Run TestCase** | Reuse other test cases | Modular test design |
| **Delay** | Pause execution | Wait conditions |
| **Conditional GoTo** | Branching logic | Based on conditions |

**3. Assertion Library (50+ Types):**

**Content Assertions:**
```xml
<assertions>
  <!-- Text-based -->
  <assertion type="Contains">
    <token>success</token>
    <ignoreCase>true</ignoreCase>
  </assertion>
  
  <assertion type="Not Contains">
    <token>error</token>
  </assertion>
  
  <assertion type="XPath Match">
    <xpath>//result/status</xpath>
    <expected>SUCCESS</expected>
  </assertion>
  
  <assertion type="JSONPath Match">
    <path>$.data[0].id</path>
    <expected>${expectedId}</expected>
  </assertion>
</assertions>
```

**Protocol Assertions:**
```xml
<assertions>
  <!-- HTTP Status -->
  <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes">
    <codes>200,201,202</codes>
  </assertion>
  
  <!-- Response Headers -->
  <assertion type="Response Headers">
    <header>Content-Type</header>
    <value>application/json</value>
  </assertion>
  
  <!-- SOAP Fault -->
  <assertion type="SOAP Fault">
    <faultType>Client</faultType>
  </assertion>
</assertions>
```

**Performance Assertions:**
```xml
<assertions>
  <!-- Response Time -->
  <assertion type="Response SLA">
    <time>2000</time>
  </assertion>
  
  <!-- Size Validation -->
  <assertion type="Size Assertion">
    <min>100</min>
    <max>10000</max>
  </assertion>
</assertions>
```

**Script Assertions:**
```groovy
// Custom script assertion
assert context.response.contains("success") : "Missing success flag"

def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(context.response)
assert json.data.size() > 0 : "Empty data array"
assert json.data.every { it.id != null } : "Missing IDs"
assert json.metadata.timestamp > System.currentTimeMillis() - 60000
```

**4. Data-Driven Testing:**

**CSV Data Source:**
```xml
<dataSource>
  <type>CSV</type>
  <file>${projectDir}/data/testdata.csv</file>
  <firstRow>header</firstRow>
  <delimiter>,</delimiter>
</dataSource>

<dataSourceLoop>
  <testSteps>
    <testStep name="Create User"/>
    <testStep name="Verify User"/>
  </testSteps>
</dataSourceLoop>
```

**Excel Data Source:**
```xml
<dataSource>
  <type>Excel</type>
  <file>${projectDir}/data/testdata.xlsx</file>
  <sheet>Sheet1</sheet>
</dataSource>
```

**Database Data Source:**
```xml
<dataSource>
  <type>JDBC</type>
  <driver>com.mysql.jdbc.Driver</driver>
  <connection>jdbc:mysql://localhost/testdb</connection>
  <query>SELECT * FROM test_users WHERE active = 1</query>
</dataSource>
```

**5. Property Handling:**

**Property Scopes:**
```groovy
// Project scope
def projectProp = context.expand('${#Project#baseUrl}')

// TestSuite scope
def suiteProp = context.expand('${#TestSuite#timeout}')

// TestCase scope
def caseProp = context.expand('${#TestCase#userId}')

// System properties
def javaHome = context.expand('${#System#java.home}')

// Environment variables
def apiKey = context.expand('${#Env#API_KEY}')

// Set properties
testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('result', 'PASSED')
context.setProperty('timestamp', new Date().time)
```

**Property Transfer Examples:**

```xml
<transfer>
  <!-- Extract ID from response -->
  <source type="response" step="CreateUser">
    <path>$.id</path>
  </source>
  <target type="request" step="GetUser">
    <path>userId</path>
  </target>
</transfer>

<!-- Extract token from header -->
<transfer>
  <source type="responseHeader" step="Login">
    <header>Authorization</header>
  </source>
  <target type="header" step="GetUser">
    <header>Authorization</header>
  </target>
</transfer>
```

**6. Groovy Scripting Capabilities:**

```groovy
// Pre-request script
def generateRequest() {
    def request = [
        timestamp: new Date().time,
        randomId: new Random().nextInt(10000),
        username: "user_${System.currentTimeMillis()}"
    ]
    return new groovy.json.JsonBuilder(request).toPrettyString()
}

messageExchange.setRequestContent(generateRequest())

// Post-request script
def response = messageExchange.responseContent
if (response) {
    def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
    testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('createdId', json.id.toString())
    log.info "Created ID: ${json.id}"
}

// Conditional logic
if (context.expand('${#TestCase#userRole}') == 'admin') {
    testRunner.runTestStepByName('AdminCheck')
} else {
    testRunner.runTestStepByName('UserCheck')
}

// Error handling
try {
    // Risky operation
    def result = riskyOperation()
    assert result == expected
} catch (Exception e) {
    log.error "Test failed: ${e.message}"
    testRunner.fail(e.message)
}
```

**7. Test Execution Options:**

| Execution Mode | Description | Use Case |
|----------------|-------------|----------|
| **Single Step** | Run one test step | Debugging |
| **TestCase** | Run complete test case | Development |
| **TestSuite** | Run all cases in suite | Regression |
| **Project** | Run all tests | Full validation |
| **Data-Driven** | Run with multiple data sets | Data validation |
| **Parallel** | Run tests concurrently | Speed optimization |

**8. Test Reports:**

```xml
<testReport>
  <summary>
    <testSuite name="UserAPI">
      <testCase name="CreateUser">
        <result>PASSED</result>
        <time>1.234s</time>
        <assertions>
          <total>5</total>
          <passed>5</passed>
        </assertions>
        <steps>
          <step name="Authenticate" status="PASSED" time="0.345s"/>
          <step name="CreateUser" status="PASSED" time="0.567s"/>
          <step name="VerifyUser" status="PASSED" time="0.322s"/>
        </steps>
      </testCase>
    </testSuite>
  </summary>
</testReport>
```

**9. CI/CD Integration:**

```bash
# Command-line execution
testrunner.sh -s "UserAPI TestSuite" \
              -f reports \
              -j -r \
              -PbaseUrl=${API_URL} \
              -PauthToken=${TOKEN} \
              project.xml

# Maven integration
mvn soapui:test -Dsoapui.project=project.xml \
                -Dsoapui.testsuite="UserAPI"

# Jenkins pipeline
stage('API Tests') {
    steps {
        sh 'testrunner.sh -f reports -j project.xml'
    }
    post {
        always {
            junit 'reports/*.xml'
        }
    }
}
```

**10. Functional Testing Benefits Summary:**

| Benefit | Impact |
|---------|--------|
| **Automation** | 90% reduction in manual testing time |
| **Reusability** | 60% faster test creation |
| **Coverage** | 5x more scenarios tested |
| **Consistency** | 100% repeatable execution |
| **Early Detection** | Bugs caught 70% earlier |
| **Regression** | Instant feedback on changes |
| **Documentation** | Tests document expected behavior |

**11. Best Practices for Functional Testing:**

✅ **Modular Design:** Create reusable test components
✅ **Data-Driven:** Separate test logic from data
✅ **Independent Tests:** No test depends on others
✅ **Clean Up:** Always restore test environment
✅ **Meaningful Assertions:** Validate what matters
✅ **Version Control:** Store tests with code
✅ **Regular Review:** Update tests with API changes

**12. Example: Complete Functional Test Case**

```xml
<testCase name="Complete User Registration Flow">
  <setupScript>
    <![CDATA[
      // Generate unique test data
      def username = "user_${System.currentTimeMillis()}"
      testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('testUsername', username)
      testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('testEmail', "${username}@test.com")
    ]]>
  </setupScript>
  
  <testSteps>
    <!-- Step 1: Register user -->
    <testStep name="RegisterUser" type="restrequest">
      <config>
        <endpoint>${#Project#apiUrl}/users</endpoint>
        <method>POST</method>
        <request>
          <![CDATA[
          {
            "username": "${testUsername}",
            "email": "${testEmail}",
            "password": "Test@123"
          }
          ]]>
        </request>
      </config>
      <assertions>
        <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>201</codes></assertion>
        <assertion type="JSONPath Match"><path>$.username</path><value>${testUsername}</value></assertion>
      </assertions>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 2: Extract user ID -->
    <testStep name="ExtractUserId" type="groovy">
      <script>
        <![CDATA[
          def response = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("RegisterUser")
              .getPropertyValue("response")
          def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
          testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('userId', json.id.toString())
        ]]>
      </script>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 3: Login with new user -->
    <testStep name="Login" type="restrequest">
      <config>
        <endpoint>${#Project#apiUrl}/auth/login</endpoint>
        <method>POST</method>
        <request>
          <![CDATA[
          {
            "username": "${testUsername}",
            "password": "Test@123"
          }
          ]]>
        </request>
      </config>
      <assertions>
        <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>200</codes></assertion>
        <assertion type="JSONPath Existence"><path>$.token</path></assertion>
      </assertions>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 4: Get user profile -->
    <testStep name="GetProfile" type="restrequest">
      <config>
        <endpoint>${#Project#apiUrl}/users/${userId}</endpoint>
        <method>GET</method>
      </config>
      <assertions>
        <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>200</codes></assertion>
        <assertion type="JSONPath Match"><path>$.username</path><value>${testUsername}</value></assertion>
        <assertion type="Response SLA"><time>2000</time></assertion>
      </assertions>
    </testStep>
  </testSteps>
  
  <tearDownScript>
    <![CDATA[
      // Clean up test user
      def userId = context.expand('${#TestCase#userId}')
      if (userId) {
        def deleteRequest = new com.eviware.soapui.impl.wsdl.teststeps.RestTestRequestStep()
        deleteRequest.setEndpoint("${#Project#apiUrl}/users/${userId}")
        deleteRequest.setMethod("DELETE")
        deleteRequest.run(testRunner, context)
      }
    ]]>
  </tearDownScript>
</testCase>
```

content.title: Performance and Load Testing with SoapUI
content.explanation:
**Validating API Performance Under Load:**

SoapUI provides comprehensive load testing capabilities to ensure your APIs can handle expected traffic volumes and perform reliably under stress.

**1. Load Testing Overview:**

```
Load Test Types
├── Load Testing
│   ├── Expected user load
│   ├── Normal operating conditions
│   └── Performance validation
├── Stress Testing
│   ├── Beyond expected load
│   ├── Breaking point identification
│   └── Recovery testing
├── Soak Testing
│   ├── Extended duration
│   ├── Memory leak detection
│   └── Resource exhaustion
├── Spike Testing
│   ├── Sudden load increases
│   ├── Burst handling
│   └── Auto-scaling validation
└── Endurance Testing
    ├── Long-term stability
    ├── Degradation detection
    └── SLA compliance
```

**2. Load Test Configuration:**

```xml
<loadTest name="User API Load Test">
  <!-- Basic Configuration -->
  <configuration>
    <threads>
      <min>10</min>
      <max>100</max>
      <increment>5</increment>
    </threads>
    
    <duration>
      <rampUp>60</rampUp>     <!-- seconds -->
      <steady>300</steady>    <!-- seconds -->
      <rampDown>60</rampDown> <!-- seconds -->
    </duration>
    
    <limits>
      <maxAssertionErrors>100</maxAssertionErrors>
      <maxTotalErrors>200</maxTotalErrors>
      <threadTimeout>30000</threadTimeout>
    </limits>
  </configuration>
  
  <!-- Load Strategy -->
  <strategy type="Simple">
    <startThreads>10</startThreads>
    <endThreads>100</endThreads>
    <duration>300</duration>
  </strategy>
  
  <!-- Test Steps to Include -->
  <testSteps>
    <testStep name="Get Users" weight="2"/>
    <testStep name="Create User" weight="1"/>
    <testStep name="Update User" weight="1"/>
    <testStep name="Delete User" weight="1"/>
  </testSteps>
</loadTest>
```

**3. Load Strategies:**

```xml
<!-- Simple Strategy - Linear increase -->
<strategy type="Simple">
  <startThreads>10</startThreads>
  <endThreads>100</endThreads>
  <duration>300</duration>
</strategy>

<!-- Variance Strategy - Random fluctuations -->
<strategy type="Variance">
  <minThreads>20</minThreads>
  <maxThreads>80</maxThreads>
  <duration>600</duration>
  <seed>12345</seed>
</strategy>

<!-- Burst Strategy - Periodic spikes -->
<strategy type="Burst">
  <baseThreads>20</baseThreads>
  <burstThreads>100</burstThreads>
  <burstDuration>30</burstDuration>
  <interval>120</interval>
</strategy>

<!-- Grid Strategy - Custom schedule -->
<strategy type="Grid">
  <schedule>
    <point time="0" threads="10"/>
    <point time="60" threads="50"/>
    <point time="120" threads="100"/>
    <point time="180" threads="50"/>
    <point time="240" threads="10"/>
  </schedule>
</strategy>

<!-- Thread Strategy - Gradual thread changes -->
<strategy type="Thread">
  <threads>
    <thread time="0" count="10"/>
    <thread time="60" count="20"/>
    <thread time="120" count="40"/>
    <thread time="180" count="80"/>
    <thread time="240" count="100"/>
  </threads>
</strategy>
```

**4. Performance Metrics Collection:**

```xml
<metrics>
  <!-- Response Time Metrics -->
  <metric name="avgResponseTime"/>
  <metric name="minResponseTime"/>
  <metric name="maxResponseTime"/>
  <metric name="medianResponseTime"/>
  <metric name="percentile90"/>
  <metric name="percentile95"/>
  <metric name="percentile99"/>
  
  <!-- Throughput Metrics -->
  <metric name="requestsPerSecond"/>
  <metric name="transactionsPerSecond"/>
  <metric name="bytesPerSecond"/>
  
  <!-- Error Metrics -->
  <metric name="errorCount"/>
  <metric name="errorRate"/>
  <metric name="assertionErrors"/>
  
  <!-- Thread Metrics -->
  <metric name="activeThreads"/>
  <metric name="finishedThreads"/>
  <metric name="totalThreads"/>
  
  <!-- Timing Metrics -->
  <metric name="latency"/>
  <metric name="connectTime"/>
  <metric name="processingTime"/>
</metrics>
```

**5. SLA (Service Level Agreement) Thresholds:**

```xml
<sla>
  <!-- Response Time SLAs -->

    <warning>1000</warning>

  </threshold>
  
  <threshold name="percentile95">
    <warning>2000</warning>

  </threshold>
  
  <!-- Error Rate SLAs -->

  </threshold>
  
  <!-- Throughput SLAs -->

  </threshold>
</sla>
```

**6. Real-Time Monitoring:**

```groovy
// Real-time monitoring script
def monitor = context.getProperty("monitor")
if (!monitor) {
    monitor = new HashMap()
    context.setProperty("monitor", monitor)
}

// Track metrics per thread
def threadId = Thread.currentThread().getId()
def stepName = context.expand('${testStep#name}')
def startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()

// Store after execution
context.setProperty("monitor.${threadId}.${stepName}", [
    start: startTime,
    end: System.currentTimeMillis()
])

// Aggregate metrics periodically
if (threadId == 1) {
    // Calculate statistics
    def metrics = context.getProperty("monitor")
    def totalTime = 0
    def count = 0
    
    metrics.each { key, value ->
        if (value instanceof Map && value.containsKey('duration')) {
            totalTime += value.duration
            count++
        }
    }
    
    if (count > 0) {
        log.info "Average response time: ${totalTime/count}ms"
    }
}
```

**8. Distributed Load Testing:**

**9. Load Test Data Management:**

<loadTestData>

**10. Load Test Assertions:**

```xml
<loadTestAssertions>

```

**11. Load Testing Best Practices:**

✅ **Realistic Scenarios:** Model actual user behavior
✅ **Think Time:** Include realistic delays
✅ **Data Variation:** Use diverse test data
✅ **Warm-up Period:** Allow system to stabilize
✅ **Monitor Resources:** Track server metrics
✅ **Test in Staging:** Never on production
✅ **Gradual Load:** Ramp up slowly
✅ **Multiple Runs:** Average results over runs
✅ **Baseline First:** Know normal performance
✅ **Correlate Metrics:** Connect client and server metrics

**12. Performance Bottleneck Identification:**

```groovy
// Analyze load test results
def analyzeBottlenecks(results) {
    def bottlenecks = []
    
    // Check response time degradation
    results.timeline.eachWithIndex { point, index ->
        if (index > 0) {
            def prev = results.timeline[index - 1]
            def increase = ((point.avgResponse - prev.avgResponse) / prev.avgResponse) * 100
            
            if (increase > 50) {  // 50% increase
                bottlenecks.add([
                    time: point.time,
                    threads: point.threads,
                    increase: increase,
                    suspected: "Response time spike at ${point.threads} users"
                ])
            }
        }
    }
    
    // Check error rate spikes
    results.steps.each { step ->
        if (step.errorRate > 5) {  // 5% error rate
            bottlenecks.add([
                step: step.name,
                errorRate: step.errorRate,
                suspected: "High error rate in ${step.name}"
            ])
        }
    }
    
    return bottlenecks
}
```

**13. Load Testing Example:**

```xml
<loadTest name="E-commerce API Peak Load">
  <configuration>
    <threads min="10" max="200" increment="10"/>
    <duration rampUp="120" steady="600" rampDown="120"/>
  </configuration>
  
  <strategy type="Simple">
    <startThreads>10</startThreads>
    <endThreads>200</endThreads>

      <file>data/products.csv</file>
    </dataSource>
    <dataSource name="users">
      <type>CSV</type>
      <file>data/users.csv</file>
      <uniquePerThread>true</uniquePerThread>
    </dataSource>
  </data>
  
  <sla>
    <threshold name="avgResponseTime" warning="1000" critical="2000"/>
    <threshold name="errorRate" warning="1" critical="5"/>
    <threshold name="requestsPerSecond" warning="100" critical="50"/>
  </sla>
</loadTest>
```

**14. Load Test Results Analysis:**

```
Load Test Results Analysis
═══════════════════════════

Peak Performance: 200 concurrent users
Saturation Point: 150 users (response time spikes)
Max Throughput: 850 req/sec
Error Rate at Peak: 2.3%

Bottlenecks Identified:
• Checkout API - response time degrades after 100 users
• Database connection pool exhausted at 150 users
• Redis cache miss rate increases significantly

Recommendations:
• Scale database connection pool
• Add caching for product catalog
• Optimize checkout transaction
• Consider read replicas for scaling
```

**15. Load Testing Benefits Summary:**

| Benefit | Impact |
|---------|--------|
| **Capacity Planning** | Right-size infrastructure |
| **Bottleneck Detection** | Identify performance issues early |
| **SLA Validation** | Ensure performance meets requirements |
| **Cost Optimization** | Avoid over-provisioning |
| **User Experience** | Prevent slowdowns during peak |
| **Confidence** | Deploy with performance certainty |
| **Regression Prevention** | Catch performance degradation |

content.title: Creating and Using Mock Services
content.explanation:
**Simulating APIs for Isolated Testing:**

Mock services allow you to simulate API behavior without having the actual service running. This is invaluable for development, testing, and demos.

**1. Mock Services Overview:**

```
Mock Service Use Cases
├── Development
│   ├── Frontend development before API ready
│   ├── Parallel development
│   └── Testing error scenarios
├── Testing
│   ├── Isolated component testing
│   ├── Simulate third-party APIs
│   └── Test edge cases
├── Demos
│   ├── Product demonstrations
│   ├── Training environments
│   └── Proof of concepts
└── CI/CD
    ├── Automated testing
    ├── Contract testing
    └── Integration testing
```

**2. Creating a Mock Service:**

```xml
<!-- Mock Service Definition -->
<mockService name="Product API Mock" port="8080" path="/api">
  <!-- Mock Operations -->
  <mockOperation name="GET /products" method="GET" path="/products">
    <mockResponse name="Success Response">
      <httpStatus>200</httpStatus>
      <contentType>application/json</contentType>
      <response>
        <![CDATA[
        [
          {
            "id": 1,
            "name": "Product 1",
            "price": 99.99,
            "inStock": true
          },
          {
            "id": 2,
            "name": "Product 2",
            "price": 149.99,
            "inStock": true
          }
        ]
        ]]>
      </response>
    </mockResponse>
    
    <mockResponse name="Empty Response">
      <httpStatus>200</httpStatus>
      <response>[]</response>
    </mockResponse>
  </mockOperation>
  
  <mockOperation name="GET /products/{id}" method="GET" path="/products/{id}">
    <mockResponse name="Found">
      <httpStatus>200</httpStatus>
      <response>
        <![CDATA[
        {
          "id": "${id}",
          "name": "Product ${id}",
          "price": 99.99,
          "inStock": true
        }
        ]]>
      </response>
    </mockResponse>
    
    <mockResponse name="Not Found">
      <httpStatus>404</httpStatus>
      <response>
        {"error": "Product not found"}
      </response>
    </mockResponse>
  </mockOperation>
</mockService>
```

**3. Dynamic Mock Responses:**

```groovy
// Scripted mock response
def request = mockRequest.getRequest()
def method = mockRequest.getMethod()
def path = mockRequest.getPath()

log.info "Received ${method} request to ${path}"

// Parse request if needed
if (method == "POST" && request) {
    def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(request)
    log.info "Request body: ${json}"
}

// Generate dynamic response
def response = [:]
response.timestamp = new Date().time
response.randomValue = new Random().nextInt(1000)

// Conditional logic
if (path.contains("error")) {
    mockResponse.setHttpResponseCode(500)
    response.error = "Internal Server Error"
} else if (path.contains("timeout")) {
    Thread.sleep(5000)
    response.status = "delayed"
} else {
    mockResponse.setHttpResponseCode(200)
    response.status = "success"
    response.data = generateData(path)
}

// Set response content
mockResponse.setContent(new groovy.json.JsonBuilder(response).toPrettyString())
mockResponse.setContentType("application/json")

// Add custom headers
mockResponse.setHeader("X-Custom-Header", "mock-value")
mockResponse.setHeader("X-Request-ID", requestId)
```

**4. Response Dispatch Strategies:**

```xml
<!-- Sequence Strategy - Cycle through responses -->
<mockOperation dispatchStyle="SEQUENCE">
  <mockResponse name="Response 1"/>
  <mockResponse name="Response 2"/>
  <mockResponse name="Response 3"/>
</mockOperation>

<!-- Random Strategy - Random selection -->
<mockOperation dispatchStyle="RANDOM">
  <mockResponse name="Success" weight="70"/>
  <mockResponse name="Error" weight="20"/>
  <mockResponse name="Timeout" weight="10"/>
</mockOperation>

<!-- Query Match - Based on parameters -->
<mockOperation dispatchStyle="QUERY_MATCH">
  <match>
    <parameter name="status">
      <value match="active">Active Response</value>
      <value match="inactive">Inactive Response</value>
      <default>Default Response</default>
    </parameter>
  </match>
</mockOperation>

<!-- XPath Match - Based on XML content -->
<mockOperation dispatchStyle="XQUERY">
  <match>
    <xpath>/request/type</xpath>
    <value match="standard">Standard Response</value>
    <value match="premium">Premium Response</value>
  </match>
</mockOperation>

<!-- Script Dispatch - Custom logic -->
<mockOperation dispatchStyle="SCRIPT">
  <script>
    <![CDATA[
      if (mockRequest.getHeader("X-User-Role") == "admin") {
        return "Admin Response"
      } else if (mockRequest.getMethod() == "POST") {
        return "Create Response"
      } else {
        return "Default Response"
      }
    ]]>
  </script>
</mockOperation>
```

**5. Simulating Delays and Faults:**

```xml
<!-- Response Delays -->
<mockResponse name="Slow Response">
  <delay>2000</delay>  <!-- 2 second delay -->
  <response>...</response>
</mockResponse>

<!-- Variable Delay -->
<mockResponse name="Variable Delay">
  <delayScript>
    <![CDATA[
      // Random delay between 1-5 seconds
      return (Math.random() * 4000 + 1000) as int
    ]]>
  </delayScript>
  <response>...</response>
</mockResponse>

<!-- Fault Simulation -->
<mockResponse name="Internal Error">
  <httpStatus>500</httpStatus>
  <response>
    {
      "error": "Internal Server Error",
      "code": 500,
      "timestamp": "${new Date().time}"
    }
  </response>
</mockResponse>

<!-- Timeout Simulation -->
<mockResponse name="Timeout">
  <delay>30000</delay>  <!-- 30 seconds -->
  <response>...</response>
</mockResponse>
```

**6. Stateful Mock Services:**

```groovy
// Stateful mock with in-memory storage
def storage = context.getProperty("mockStorage")
if (!storage) {
    storage = [
        users: [:],
        products: [:],
        counters: [:]
    ]
    context.setProperty("mockStorage", storage)
}

// Handle different operations
switch(mockRequest.getMethod()) {
    case "GET":
        // Retrieve data
        def id = extractId(mockRequest.getPath())
        def data = storage.users[id]
        if (data) {
            return createResponse(200, data)
        } else {
            return createResponse(404, [error: "Not found"])
        }
        break
        
    case "POST":
        // Create new resource
        def newData = parseRequest(mockRequest)
        def id = generateId()
        storage.users[id] = newData
        storage.counters.created = storage.counters.created + 1
        return createResponse(201, [id: id, ...newData])
        break
        
    case "DELETE":
        // Delete resource
        def id = extractId(mockRequest.getPath())
        if (storage.users.remove(id)) {
            return createResponse(204, null)
        } else {
            return createResponse(404, [error: "Not found"])
        }
        break
}
```

**7. Mock Service Logging:**

```xml
<!-- Enable detailed logging -->
<mockService name="Logging Mock" logActivity="true">
  <log>
    <requestHeaders>true</requestHeaders>
    <requestContent>true</requestContent>
    <responseHeaders>true</responseHeaders>
    <responseContent>true</responseContent>
    <timing>true</timing>
  </log>
  
  <logFile>
    <path>${projectDir}/logs/mock.log</path>

  </logFile>
</mockService>
```

**8. Mock Service Validation:**

```xml
<!-- Request validation rules -->
<mockOperation name="Create User">
  <validation>
    <!-- Required headers -->
    <header name="Content-Type" required="true">
      <value>application/json</value>
    </header>
    
    <header name="Authorization" required="true">
      <pattern>^Bearer .+$</pattern>
    </header>
    
    <!-- Request body validation -->
    <body validation="JSON">
      <schema>user-schema.json</schema>
      <requiredFields>username,email</requiredFields>
    </body>
    
    <!-- Parameter validation -->
    <parameter name="id" required="false">
      <type>integer</type>
      <min>1</min>
      <max>9999</max>
    </parameter>
  </validation>
  
  <!-- Validation error response -->
  <validationError>
    <httpStatus>400</httpStatus>
    <response>
      {
        "error": "Validation failed",
        "details": "${validationErrors}"
      }
    </response>
  </validationError>
</mockOperation>
```

**9. Mock Service Statistics:**

```xml
<mockService name="Statistics Mock">
  <statistics>
    <!-- Track request counts -->
    <counter name="totalRequests"/>
    <counter name="successfulRequests"/>
    <counter name="errorRequests"/>
    
    <!-- Response time tracking -->
    <timer name="responseTime">
      <avg/>
      <min/>
      <max/>
      <percentile95/>
    </timer>
    
    <!-- Per-endpoint stats -->
    <endpoint name="/products">
      <counter name="requests"/>
      <timer name="responseTime"/>
    </endpoint>
  </statistics>
  
  <!-- Statistics endpoint -->
  <mockOperation name="GET /stats" method="GET" path="/stats">
    <mockResponse name="Statistics">
      <response>
        <![CDATA[
        {
          "totalRequests": ${statistics.totalRequests},
          "avgResponseTime": ${statistics.avgResponseTime},
          "endpoints": {
            "/products": {
              "requests": ${statistics.endpoints['/products'].requests},
              "avgTime": ${statistics.endpoints['/products'].avgTime}
            }
          }
        }
        ]]>
      </response>
    </mockResponse>
  </mockOperation>
</mockService>
```

**10. Mock Service Examples:**

```xml
<!-- Example: Payment Gateway Mock -->
