**11. Mock Service Benefits:**

| Benefit | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Parallel Development** | Frontend/backend teams work simultaneously |
| **Cost Reduction** | No need for paid third-party APIs |
| **Reliability** | No dependencies on external services |
| **Edge Cases** | Simulate rare or error conditions |
| **Performance** | Fast, predictable responses |
| **Controlled Testing** | Complete control over behavior |
| **Offline Development** | Work without internet connection |
| **Training** | Safe environment for learning |

**12. Best Practices for Mock Services:**

✅ **Realistic Responses:** Match real API as closely as possible
✅ **Include Errors:** Simulate error conditions
✅ **State Management:** Use stateful mocks for complex scenarios
✅ **Logging:** Enable logging for debugging
✅ **Validation:** Validate incoming requests
✅ **Versioning:** Maintain multiple versions if needed
✅ **Documentation:** Document mock behavior
✅ **Performance:** Keep responses fast
✅ **Cleanup:** Reset state between test runs

**13. Complete Mock Service Example:**

```xml
<mockService name="E-commerce API Mock" port="8080" path="/api/v1">
  <!-- State management -->
  <script>
    <![CDATA[
      def storage = context.getProperty("storage")
      if (!storage) {
        storage = [
          products: [
            [id: 1, name: "Laptop", price: 999.99, stock: 10],
            [id: 2, name: "Mouse", price: 29.99, stock: 50],
            [id: 3, name: "Keyboard", price: 79.99, stock: 25]
          ],
          orders: [:],
          nextOrderId: 1000
        ]
        context.setProperty("storage", storage)
      }
    ]]>
  </script>
  
  <!-- Get all products -->
  <mockOperation name="GET /products" method="GET" path="/products">
    <mockResponse name="Product List">
      <script>
        <![CDATA[
          def storage = context.getProperty("storage")
          def products = storage.products.collect { p ->
            [
              id: p.id,
              name: p.name,
              price: p.price,
              inStock: p.stock > 0
            ]
          }
          mockResponse.setContent(new groovy.json.JsonBuilder(products).toPrettyString())
        ]]>
      </script>
    </mockResponse>
  </mockOperation>
  
  <!-- Get product by ID -->
  <mockOperation name="GET /products/{id}" method="GET" path="/products/{id}">
    <mockResponse name="Found">
      <script>
        <![CDATA[
          def storage = context.getProperty("storage")
          def id = mockRequest.getPath().split('/').last().toInteger()
          def product = storage.products.find { it.id == id }
          
          if (product) {
            mockResponse.setHttpResponseCode(200)
            mockResponse.setContent(new groovy.json.JsonBuilder([
              id: product.id,
              name: product.name,
              price: product.price,
              stock: product.stock,
              inStock: product.stock > 0
            ]).toPrettyString())
          } else {
            mockResponse.setHttpResponseCode(404)
            mockResponse.setContent('{"error": "Product not found"}')
          }
        ]]>
      </script>
    </mockResponse>
  </mockOperation>
  
  <!-- Create order -->
  <mockOperation name="POST /orders" method="POST" path="/orders">
    <mockResponse name="Order Created">
      <script>
        <![CDATA[
          def storage = context.getProperty("storage")
          def request = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(mockRequest.getRequest())
          
          // Validate products and stock
          def valid = true
          def errors = []
          
          request.items.each { item ->
            def product = storage.products.find { it.id == item.productId }
            if (!product) {
              valid = false
              errors.add("Product ${item.productId} not found")
            } else if (product.stock < item.quantity) {
              valid = false
              errors.add("Insufficient stock for product ${product.name}")
            }
          }
          
          if (valid) {
            // Create order
            def orderId = storage.nextOrderId++
            def order = [
              id: orderId,
              items: request.items,
              total: calculateTotal(request.items),
              status: "confirmed",
              createdAt: new Date().time
            ]
            storage.orders[orderId] = order
            
            // Update stock
            request.items.each { item ->
              def product = storage.products.find { it.id == item.productId }
              product.stock -= item.quantity
            }
            
            mockResponse.setHttpResponseCode(201)
            mockResponse.setContent(new groovy.json.JsonBuilder([
              orderId: orderId,
              status: "confirmed",
              total: order.total
            ]).toPrettyString())
          } else {
            mockResponse.setHttpResponseCode(400)
            mockResponse.setContent(new groovy.json.JsonBuilder([
              error: "Invalid order",
              details: errors
            ]).toPrettyString())
          }
        ]]>
      </script>
    </mockResponse>
  </mockOperation>
  
  <!-- Get order -->
  <mockOperation name="GET /orders/{id}" method="GET" path="/orders/{id}">
    <mockResponse name="Order Details">
      <script>
        <![CDATA[
          def storage = context.getProperty("storage")
          def id = mockRequest.getPath().split('/').last().toInteger()
          def order = storage.orders[id]
          
          if (order) {
            mockResponse.setContent(new groovy.json.JsonBuilder(order).toPrettyString())
          } else {
            mockResponse.setHttpResponseCode(404)
            mockResponse.setContent('{"error": "Order not found"}')
          }
        ]]>
      </script>
    </mockResponse>
  </mockOperation>
  
  <!-- Helper function -->
  <script>
    <![CDATA[
      def calculateTotal(items) {
        def storage = context.getProperty("storage")
        def total = 0
        items.each { item ->
          def product = storage.products.find { it.id == item.productId }
          total += product.price * item.quantity
        }
        return total
      }
    ]]>
  </script>
</mockService>
```

content.title: Understanding Test Cases in SoapUI
content.explanation:
**What is a Test Case and Why It Matters:**

A test case in SoapUI is a collection of test steps that together validate a specific scenario or functionality of your API. Think of it as a script that automates a sequence of actions and verifies the results.

**Test Case Anatomy:**

```
Test Case: "User Registration Flow"
├── Setup Script (runs once before all steps)
├── Test Steps (executed in order)
│   ├── Step 1: Generate unique user data (Groovy script)
│   ├── Step 2: Register user (POST /users)
│   ├── Step 3: Verify registration (assertions)
│   ├── Step 4: Login with new user (POST /auth/login)
│   ├── Step 5: Verify login token (assertions)
│   ├── Step 6: Get user profile (GET /users/{id})
│   └── Step 7: Verify profile data (assertions)
├── Teardown Script (runs once after all steps)
└── Properties (shared data across steps)
```

**Why Test Cases Are Essential:**

✅ **Automation:** Run complex scenarios without manual intervention
✅ **Reusability:** Use same test case with different data
✅ **Consistency:** Same validation every time
✅ **Documentation:** Tests document expected behavior
✅ **Regression:** Catch issues when API changes
✅ **Debugging:** Isolate and identify problems

**Test Case Hierarchy:**

```
Project (e.g., "E-commerce API")
├── TestSuite 1 (e.g., "User Management")
│   ├── TestCase 1: "Register User"
│   ├── TestCase 2: "Login User"
│   ├── TestCase 3: "Update Profile"
│   └── TestCase 4: "Delete User"
├── TestSuite 2 (e.g., "Product Catalog")
│   ├── TestCase 1: "Get Products"
│   ├── TestCase 2: "Search Products"
│   └── TestCase 3: "Get Product Details"
└── TestSuite 3 (e.g., "Order Processing")
    ├── TestCase 1: "Create Order"
    ├── TestCase 2: "Get Order"
    └── TestCase 3: "Cancel Order"
```

**Test Case Components:**

| Component | Purpose | Example |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| **Name** | Identify the test case | "TC-001-Valid-Login" |
| **Description** | Document purpose | "Test login with valid credentials" |
| **Setup Script** | Prepare test environment | Generate test data, authenticate |
| **Test Steps** | Sequence of actions | HTTP requests, scripts, assertions |
| **Properties** | Shared variables | ${userId}, ${authToken} |
| **Assertions** | Validation rules | Status code, content checks |
| **Teardown Script** | Clean up after test | Delete test data, close connections |
| **Tags** | Categorize tests | @smoke @regression @critical |

**Test Case Lifecycle:**

```
1. Create → 2. Configure → 3. Add Steps → 4. Add Assertions → 5. Run → 6. Analyze → 7. Refine
     ↑                                                                           ↓
     └─────────────────── 8. Maintain (as API changes) ──────────────────────────┘
```

content.title: Complete Test Case Example with Multiple Steps
content.scenario: Testing complete user lifecycle with data flow between steps
content.outcome: End-to-end validation of user operations
content.details:
**Test Case: Complete User Lifecycle**

**Setup Script - Generate Test Data:**
```groovy
// Generate unique test data
def timestamp = System.currentTimeMillis()
def username = "testuser_${timestamp}"
def email = "${username}@test.com"

// Store in test case properties
testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('testUsername', username)
testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('testEmail', email)
testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('testPassword', 'Test@123')

testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('timestamp', timestamp.toString())

log.info "Generated test user: ${username}"
```

**Step 1: Create User**
```xml
<testStep name="Create User" type="restrequest">
  <config>
    <endpoint>${#Project#apiUrl}/users</endpoint>
    <method>POST</method>
    <request>
      <![CDATA[
      {
        "name": "${testUsername}",
        "email": "${testEmail}",
        "password": "${testPassword}"
      }
      ]]>
    </request>
  </config>
  <assertions>
    <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>201</codes></assertion>
    <assertion type="JSONPath Existence"><path>$.id</path></assertion>
    <assertion type="JSONPath Match"><path>$.email</path><value>${testEmail}</value></assertion>
  </assertions>
</testStep>
```

**Step 2: Extract User ID**
```groovy
<testStep name="Extract User ID" type="groovy">
  <script>
    <![CDATA[
      def response = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("Create User")
          .getPropertyValue("response")
      def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
      def userId = json.id.toString()
      testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('userId', userId)
      log.info "Extracted user ID: ${userId}"
    ]]>
  </script>
</testStep>
```

**Step 3: Login**
```xml
<testStep name="Login" type="restrequest">
  <config>
    <endpoint>${#Project#apiUrl}/auth/login</endpoint>
    <method>POST</method>
    <request>
      <![CDATA[
      {
        "username": "${testUsername}",
        "password": "${testPassword}"
      }
      ]]>
    </request>
  </config>
  <assertions>
    <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>200</codes></assertion>
    <assertion type="JSONPath Existence"><path>$.token</path></assertion>
  </assertions>
</testStep>
```

**Step 4: Extract Token**
```groovy
<testStep name="Extract Token" type="groovy">
  <script>
    <![CDATA[
      def response = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("Login")
          .getPropertyValue("response")
      def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
      def token = json.token
      testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('authToken', token)
      log.info "Extracted auth token"
    ]]>
  </script>
</testStep>
```

**Step 5: Get User Profile**
```xml
<testStep name="Get User Profile" type="restrequest">
  <config>
    <endpoint>${#Project#apiUrl}/users/${userId}</endpoint>
    <method>GET</method>
    <headers>
      <header name="Authorization">Bearer ${authToken}</header>
    </headers>
  </config>
  <assertions>
    <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>200</codes></assertion>
    <assertion type="JSONPath Match"><path>$.id</path><value>${userId}</value></assertion>
    <assertion type="JSONPath Match"><path>$.email</path><value>${testEmail}</value></assertion>
    <assertion type="Response SLA"><time>2000</time></assertion>
  </assertions>
</testStep>
```

**Step 6: Update User**

<testStep name="Update User" type="restrequest">

    <endpoint>${#Project#apiUrl}/users/${userId}</endpoint>

```groovy

    <![CDATA[

      def getStep = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("Get User Profile")
      getStep.run(testRunner, context)
      
      def response = getStep.getPropertyValue("response")
      def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
      
      assert json.name == "${testUsername} Updated" : "Name not updated correctly"
      log.info "Update verified successfully"
    ]]>

</testStep>
```

content.title: Adding Test Suites and Organizing Tests
Test Suite Organization Strategies
content.explanation:
**Structuring Tests for Maintainability and Scalability:**

Test suites are containers that group related test cases together. Proper organization is crucial for managing large test collections.

**Test Suite Organization Patterns:**

**1. By Feature/Module:**
```
TestSuite: "User Management"
├── TestCase: "Create User"
├── TestCase: "Login User"
├── TestCase: "Update Profile"
├── TestCase: "Change Password"
└── TestCase: "Delete User"

TestSuite: "Product Catalog"
├── TestCase: "List Products"
├── TestCase: "Search Products"
├── TestCase: "Get Product Details"
└── TestCase: "Filter Products"
```

**2. By Test Type:**
```
TestSuite: "Smoke Tests"
├── TestCase: "Health Check"
├── TestCase: "Basic Auth"
└── TestCase: "Critical Path"

TestSuite: "Regression Tests"
├── TestCase: "All User Tests"
├── TestCase: "All Product Tests"
└── TestCase: "All Order Tests"

TestSuite: "Integration Tests"
├── TestCase: "Payment Flow"
├── TestCase: "Email Service"
└── TestCase: "Third-party API"
```

**3. By Priority/Risk:**
```
TestSuite: "Critical Tests"
├── TestCase: "Authentication"
├── TestCase: "Payment Processing"
└── TestCase: "Data Integrity"

TestSuite: "High Priority"
├── TestCase: "Core Features"
└── TestCase: "Major Workflows"

TestSuite: "Low Priority"
├── TestCase: "Edge Cases"
└── TestCase: "Rare Scenarios"
```

**Creating and Managing Test Suites:**

```xml
<!-- TestSuite with shared properties -->
<testSuite name="User API Tests">
  <properties>
    <property name="baseUrl" value="${#Project#apiUrl}/users"/>
    <property name="timeout" value="5000"/>
    <property name="testUser" value=""/>
  </properties>
  
  <!-- Setup script runs before any test in suite -->
  <setupScript>
    <![CDATA[
      log.info "Starting User API test suite"
      def startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
      context.setProperty('suiteStartTime', startTime)
    ]]>
  </setupScript>
  
  <!-- Test cases go here -->
  
  <!-- Teardown script runs after all tests -->
  <tearDownScript>
    <![CDATA[
      def endTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
      def duration = endTime - context.getProperty('suiteStartTime')
      log.info "User API test suite completed in ${duration}ms"
    ]]>
  </tearDownScript>
</testSuite>
```

**Test Suite-Level Assertions:**

```xml
<testSuite name="Performance Tests">
  <assertions>
    <!-- Suite-level performance requirements -->
    <assertion type="MaxDuration">
      <time>300000</time> <!-- 5 minutes max for entire suite -->
    </assertion>
    <assertion type="MaxFailures">
      <count>5</count>
    </assertion>
  </assertions>
</testSuite>
```

**Running Test Suites:**

```bash
# Run entire suite from command line
testrunner.sh -s "User API Tests" project.xml

# Run multiple suites
testrunner.sh -s "User API Tests" -s "Product API Tests" project.xml

# Run with specific properties
testrunner.sh -s "User API Tests" \
              -PbaseUrl=https://staging-api.example.com \
              -PauthToken=${TOKEN} \
              project.xml
```

**Best Practices for Test Organization:**

✅ **Consistent Naming:** Use clear, descriptive names
✅ **Logical Grouping:** Group related tests together
✅ **Shared Setup:** Use suite-level setup for common tasks
✅ **Independent Tests:** Tests should run in any order
✅ **Hierarchical Structure:** Use folders for large suites
✅ **Documentation:** Document suite purpose and dependencies

**Test Suite Metrics:**

| Metric | Description | Target |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| **Test Count** | Number of test cases | 10-50 per suite |
| **Execution Time** | Total suite duration | < 10 minutes |
| **Pass Rate** | Percentage passing | > 95% |
| **Coverage** | Feature coverage | > 80% |
| **Maintenance** | Time to update | < 1 hour/week |

content.title: Test Execution Strategies and Options
content.explanation:
**Different Ways to Execute Tests in SoapUI:**

SoapUI provides multiple execution modes to suit different testing scenarios.

**1. Execution Levels:**

```
Single Test Step
      ↓
  Test Case
      ↓
 Test Suite
      ↓
  Project
      ↓
Multiple Projects
```

**2. Execution Methods:**

| Method | How to Run | Use Case |
|--------|------------|----------|
| **Single Step** | Right-click step > Run | Debugging, development |
| **TestCase** | Right-click case > Run TestCase | Validate specific scenario |
| **TestSuite** | Right-click suite > Run TestSuite | Regression testing |
| **Project** | Right-click project > Run All | Full validation |
| **Multiple Selection** | Select items > Run | Custom test sets |

**3. Execution Modes:**

```xml
<!-- Normal Mode - Run all steps sequentially -->
<testCase name="Test" runMode="SEQUENTIAL"/>

<!-- Parallel Mode - Run steps concurrently -->
<testCase name="Performance Test" runMode="PARALLEL">
  <threadCount>5</threadCount>
</testCase>

<!-- Data-Driven Mode - Run with multiple data sets -->
<testCase name="DataDrivenTest" runMode="DATA_DRIVEN">
  <dataSource>
    <type>CSV</type>
    <file>data.csv</file>
  </dataSource>
</testCase>
```

**4. Command-Line Execution:**

```bash
# Basic execution
testrunner.sh project.xml

# Run specific test suite
testrunner.sh -s "User API Tests" project.xml

# Run specific test case
testrunner.sh -s "User API Tests" -c "Create User" project.xml

# Run with properties
testrunner.sh -PbaseUrl=https://api.example.com \
              -PauthToken=${TOKEN} \
              project.xml

# Generate reports
testrunner.sh -f reports -j -r project.xml
```

**5. Test Runner Interface:**

```
Test Runner
├── Progress Bar (overall completion)
├── Test Case List
│   ├── Test Case 1 [RUNNING]  ◄── Current status
│   ├── Test Case 2 [PASSED]   ✓

**6. Execution Options:**

```xml
<executionOptions>

  <stepDelay>0</stepDelay>

content.title: Comprehensive Assertion Strategies
content.explanation:
**Validating API Responses Thoroughly:**

Assertions are the heart of test validation. They verify that actual results match expected outcomes.

**Assertion Categories:**

```
Assertions
├── Protocol Level
│   ├── HTTP Status Codes
│   ├── Response Headers
│   └── SOAP Faults
├── Content Level
│   ├── Contains/Not Contains
│   ├── XPath Match (XML)
│   ├── JSONPath Match (JSON)
│   └── Schema Compliance
├── Performance Level
│   ├── Response SLA
│   ├── Size Assertion
│   └── Throughput
└── Custom Level
    ├── Script Assertion
    ├── JDBC Assertion
    └── Property Assertion
```

**Common Assertion Types Explained:**

| Assertion Type | What It Checks | Example |
|----------------|----------------|---------|
| **Valid HTTP Status Codes** | Response code is in allowed list | 200,201,202 |
| **Contains** | Text appears in response | "success" |
| **Not Contains** | Text does NOT appear | "error" |
| **XPath Match** | XML element matches value | //status = "active" |
| **JSONPath Match** | JSON value matches | $.user.id = 123 |
| **JSONPath Existence** | JSON path exists | $.user.email |
| **Response SLA** | Response time within limit | < 2000ms |
| **Size Assertion** | Response size in range | 100-1000 bytes |
| **Schema Compliance** | Validates against schema | matches XSD/JSON schema |
| **SOAP Fault** | Checks for/against SOAP errors | fault should/should not exist |

**Assertion Examples:**

```xml
<!-- Status Code Assertion -->
<assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes">
  <codes>200,201,202</codes>
</assertion>

<!-- Contains Assertion -->
<assertion type="Contains">
  <token>success</token>
  <ignoreCase>true</ignoreCase>
</assertion>

<!-- JSONPath Match -->
<assertion type="JSONPath Match">
  <path>$.data[0].id</path>
  <expected>${expectedId}</expected>
</assertion>

<!-- XPath Match with Namespace -->
<assertion type="XPath Match">
  <xpath>declare namespace ns='http://example.com'; //ns:result</xpath>
  <expected>25</expected>
</assertion>

<!-- Response SLA -->
<assertion type="Response SLA">
  <time>2000</time>
</assertion>

<!-- Script Assertion -->
<assertion type="Script">
  <script>
    <![CDATA[
      def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(messageExchange.responseContent)
      assert json.items.size() > 0 : "Empty items list"
      assert json.items.every { it.price > 0 } : "Invalid prices"
    ]]>
  </script>
</assertion>
```

**Assertion Best Practices:**

✅ **Layer Assertions:** Start with protocol, then content, then business logic
✅ **Be Specific:** Test exact values, not just existence
✅ **Use Dynamic Values:** Reference properties, not hardcoded
✅ **Include Performance:** Always add SLA assertions
✅ **Fail Fast:** Order assertions from most to least likely to fail
✅ **Meaningful Messages:** Add custom messages for clarity

**Assertion Layers Example:**

```xml
<testStep name="Get User">
  <!-- Layer 1: Protocol -->
  <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>200</codes></assertion>
  
  <!-- Layer 2: Structure -->
  <assertion type="JSONPath Existence"><path>$.id</path></assertion>
  <assertion type="JSONPath Existence"><path>$.name</path></assertion>
  
  <!-- Layer 3: Content -->
  <assertion type="JSONPath Match"><path>$.id</path><value>${userId}</value></assertion>
  <assertion type="JSONPath Match"><path>$.email</path><value>${email}</value></assertion>
  
  <!-- Layer 4: Business Logic -->
  <assertion type="Script">
    <script>
      def json = ...
      assert json.createdDate < new Date().time
      assert json.status in ['active', 'pending']
    </script>
  </assertion>
  
  <!-- Layer 5: Performance -->
  <assertion type="Response SLA"><time>2000</time></assertion>
</testStep>
```

**Assertion Result Interpretation:**

```
Assertion Results
══════════════════

✓ Valid HTTP Status Codes: Status 200 found in [200]
✓ JSONPath Existence: Path '$.id' exists with value '123'
✓ JSONPath Match: Path '$.name' = 'John Doe' ✓
✗ JSONPath Match: Path '$.email' expected 'john@test.com' but got 'johndoe@test.com'
✓ Response SLA: Response time 234ms < 2000ms
```

content.title: Advanced Test Execution Strategies
content.explanation:
**Optimizing Test Execution for Different Scenarios:**

**1. Parallel Execution:**

```xml
<!-- Run test cases in parallel -->
<testSuite name="Parallel Tests" parallel="true">
  <threadCount>5</threadCount>
  <testCase name="Test1"/>
  <testCase name="Test2"/>
  <testCase name="Test3"/>
  <testCase name="Test4"/>
  <testCase name="Test5"/>
</testSuite>

<!-- Run steps in parallel within test case -->
<testCase name="Performance Test" parallelSteps="true">
  <threadCount>3</threadCount>
  <testStep name="Step1"/>
  <testStep name="Step2"/>
  <testStep name="Step3"/>
</testCase>
```

**2. Conditional Execution:**

```groovy
// Conditional step execution
if (context.expand('${#TestCase#environment}') == 'production') {
    // Skip destructive tests in production
    testRunner.cancel("Skipping destructive tests in production")
}

// Run based on previous step result
if (testRunner.getResults().last().getStatus() == Status.FAILED) {
    log.warn "Previous step failed, running diagnostic step"
    testRunner.runTestStepByName("Diagnostic Step")
}
```

**3. Retry Strategy:**

```groovy
// Retry failed steps
int maxRetries = 3
int retryCount = 0
boolean success = false

while (!success && retryCount < maxRetries) {
    try {
        testRunner.runTestStepByName("Flaky Step")
        success = true
    } catch (Exception e) {
        retryCount++
        log.warn "Attempt ${retryCount} failed: ${e.message}"
        if (retryCount >= maxRetries) {
            throw e
        }
        Thread.sleep(1000 * retryCount) // Exponential backoff
    }
}
```

**4. Data-Driven Execution:**

```xml
<testCase name="DataDrivenTest">
  <dataSource>
    <type>CSV</type>
    <file>data.csv</file>
  </dataSource>
  
  <!-- Control loop behavior -->
  <dataSourceLoop>
    <strategy>SEQUENTIAL</strategy> <!-- or RANDOM, UNIQUE -->
    <testSteps>
      <testStep name="Test Step"/>
    </testSteps>
  </dataSourceLoop>
</testCase>
```

**5. Scheduled Execution:**

```bash
# Cron job for nightly tests
0 2 * * * /opt/soapui/bin/testrunner.sh -f /reports project.xml

# Jenkins scheduled build
H 2 * * * % cd %WORKSPACE && testrunner.sh -f reports project.xml
```

**6. Test Dependency Management:**

```xml
<testCase name="Login Test" dependsOn="Setup Test">
  <!-- Only runs if Setup Test passed -->
</testCase>

<testCase name="Checkout Test" dependsOn="Login Test, Cart Test">
  <!-- Requires both dependencies -->
</testCase>
```

**7. Execution Strategies Summary:**

| Strategy | When to Use | Benefits | Trade-offs |
|----------|-------------|----------|------------|
| **Sequential** | Simple tests, dependencies | Predictable, easy debugging | Slow for many tests |
| **Parallel** | Independent tests, performance | Fast execution | Resource contention |
| **Data-Driven** | Same logic, multiple inputs | Comprehensive coverage | Complex setup |
| **Conditional** | Environment-specific | Flexible, safe | Harder to maintain |
| **Retry** | Flaky tests, unreliable services | Improved stability | Slower overall |
| **Scheduled** | Regular validation | Automated testing | Requires infrastructure |
| **Dependency** | Complex workflows | Logical flow | Can't run tests independently |

**8. Execution Metrics and Optimization:**

```groovy
// Track execution metrics
def metrics = [:]

testRunner.results.each { result ->
    def stepName = result.testStep.name
    metrics[stepName] = [
        time: result.timeTaken,
        status: result.status,
        assertions: result.assertionResults.size()
    ]
}

// Identify slow steps
def slowSteps = metrics.findAll { it.value.time > 2000 }
log.warn "Slow steps: ${slowSteps.keySet()}"

// Calculate pass rate
def passed = metrics.count { it.value.status.toString() == 'PASSED' }
def total = metrics.size()
log.info "Pass rate: ${(passed/total)*100}%"
```

**9. Execution Best Practices:**

✅ **Start Simple:** Sequential first, then optimize
✅ **Isolate Tests:** No test should depend on others
✅ **Use Retries Wisely:** Only for known flaky tests
✅ **Monitor Resources:** Don't overload test machines
✅ **Balance Load:** Distribute parallel tests evenly
✅ **Track Performance:** Monitor execution times over time
✅ **Fail Fast:** Stop on critical failures
✅ **Clean Up:** Always restore test environment

  </testSuite>
  
  <!-- Performance tests - scheduled separately -->
  <testSuite name="Performance Tests">
    <testCase name="Load Test" runMode="PARALLEL">
      <threadCount>50</threadCount>
      <duration>300</duration>
    </testCase>
  </testSuite>
</testSuite>
```

**Execution Configuration:**

```groovy
// Global execution strategy
def executionStrategy = [
    environments: ['dev', 'staging', 'prod'],

    maxRetries: 3,

]

}

content.title: Test Case Design Best Practices
content.explanation:
**Creating Maintainable, Reliable, and Effective Tests:**

**1. Naming Conventions:**

```
✅ Good Names:
TC001_CreateUser_ValidData
TC002_CreateUser_InvalidEmail
TC003_Login_ValidCredentials
TC004_Login_WrongPassword

❌ Bad Names:
Test1
NewTest
CopyOfTest
TestFinal
```

**2. Test Independence:**

```groovy
// GOOD: Self-contained test
@setup
void setup() {
    // Create test data just for this test
    def testUser = createTestUser()
    testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('testUserId', testUser.id)
}

@teardown
void teardown() {
    // Clean up only what this test created
    deleteTestUser(testRunner.testCase.getPropertyValue('testUserId'))
}

// BAD: Depends on other tests
// Assumes user already exists from previous test
```

**3. Data-Driven Design:**

```xml
<!-- GOOD: Separate test logic from data -->
<testCase name="Login Tests">
  <dataSource>
    <type>CSV</type>
    <file>login-test-data.csv</file>
  </dataSource>
  <dataSourceLoop>
    <testSteps>
      <testStep name="Login"/>
    </testSteps>
  </dataSourceLoop>
</testCase>

<!-- BAD: Hardcoded data in test -->
<testStep name="Login">
  <request>{"username":"admin","password":"admin123"}</request>
</testStep>
```

**4. Assertion Completeness:**

```xml
<!-- GOOD: Multiple layers of assertions -->
<testStep name="Get User">
  <assertions>
    <!-- Protocol -->
    <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>200</codes></assertion>
    
    <!-- Structure -->
    <assertion type="JSONPath Existence"><path>$.id</path></assertion>
    <assertion type="JSONPath Existence"><path>$.email</path></assertion>
    
    <!-- Content -->
    <assertion type="JSONPath Match"><path>$.id</path><value>${userId}</value></assertion>
    
    <!-- Business Logic -->
    <assertion type="Script">
      <script>assert json.createdDate < now()</script>
    </assertion>
    
    <!-- Performance -->
    <assertion type="Response SLA"><time>2000</time></assertion>
  </assertions>
</testStep>

<!-- BAD: Single assertion -->
<assertion type="Contains"><token>success</token></assertion>
```

**5. Property Management:**

```xml
<!-- GOOD: Use properties hierarchy -->
<project>
  <properties>
    <property name="baseUrl" value="https://api.example.com"/>
  </properties>
  
  <testSuite>
    <properties>
      <property name="testDataDir" value="${projectDir}/data"/>
    </properties>
    
    <testCase>
      <properties>
        <property name="userId" value=""/>
        <property name="authToken" value=""/>
      </properties>
    </testCase>
  </testSuite>
</project>

<!-- Usage -->
<endpoint>${#Project#baseUrl}/users/${#TestCase#userId}</endpoint>
```

**6. Error Handling:**

```groovy
// GOOD: Handle errors gracefully
try {
    testRunner.runTestStepByName("Critical Step")
} catch (Exception e) {
    log.error "Critical step failed: ${e.message}"
    // Take screenshot, log details, notify team
    testRunner.fail("Test failed: ${e.message}")
} finally {
    // Always clean up
    cleanup()
}

// BAD: Let exceptions bubble up unhandled
```

**7. Test Documentation:**

```xml
<!-- GOOD: Document test purpose and expectations -->
<testCase name="TC001_CreateUser_ValidData">
  <description>
    Create a new user with valid data
    
    Preconditions:
    - API is accessible
    - No existing user with same email
    
    Test Data:
    - Username: testuser_${timestamp}
    - Email: test@example.com
    - Password: Test@123
    
    Expected Results:
    - HTTP 201 Created
    - Response contains user ID
    - All fields match input
    - User is created in database
    
    Tags: @smoke @user @regression
  </description>
  
  <tags>
    <tag>smoke</tag>
    <tag>user-management</tag>
  </tags>
</testCase>
```

**8. Maintainability Checklist:**

✅ **DRY Principle:** Don't Repeat Yourself - use shared scripts
✅ **Single Responsibility:** One test case, one scenario
✅ **Clear Names:** Names explain purpose
✅ **No Magic Numbers:** Use named constants/properties
✅ **Comments:** Explain WHY, not WHAT
✅ **Version Control:** Store tests with code
✅ **Regular Review:** Update tests when API changes

**9. Test Design Patterns:**

```
Pattern: Arrange-Act-Assert
├── Arrange: Setup test data and conditions
├── Act: Execute the test (API call)
└── Assert: Verify results

Pattern: Given-When-Then (BDD)
├── Given: Preconditions
├── When: Action performed
└── Then: Expected outcome

Pattern: Setup-Exercise-Verify-Teardown
├── Setup: Prepare environment
├── Exercise: Run test
├── Verify: Check results
└── Teardown: Clean up
```

**10. Quality Metrics for Test Cases:**

| Metric | Target | How to Measure |
|--------|--------|----------------|
| **Pass Rate** | > 95% | (Passed/Total) × 100 |
| **Execution Time** | < 5s per test | Average duration |
| **Flakiness** | < 2% | Failures over multiple runs |
| **Coverage** | > 80% | Requirements traced |
| **Maintenance Time** | < 1h/week | Time spent updating |
| **Assertions per Test** | 5-10 | Count of assertions |
| **Documentation** | 100% | All tests described |

**11. Common Pitfalls to Avoid:**

❌ **Hardcoded Values:** Use properties
❌ **Tight Coupling:** Tests depend on each other
❌ **Missing Cleanup:** Leftover test data
❌ **Over-asserting:** Testing too much in one step
❌ **Under-asserting:** Missing important checks
❌ **Ignoring Failures:** Not investigating flaky tests
❌ **No Version Control:** Tests not tracked
❌ **Poor Naming:** Unclear test purpose

**12. Test Case Template:**

```xml
<!-- Template for new test cases -->
<testCase name="TCXXX_Feature_Scenario">
  <description>
    [Brief description of test]
    
    Preconditions:
    - [List prerequisites]
    
    Test Data:
    - [List input data]
    
    Expected Results:
    - [List expected outcomes]
    
    Tags: [@smoke @regression @feature]
  </description>
  
  <properties>
    <!-- Test-specific properties -->
  </properties>
  
  <setupScript>
    <![CDATA[
      // Initialize test data
    ]]>
  </setupScript>
  
  <testSteps>
    <!-- Add steps here -->
  </testSteps>
  
  <tearDownScript>
    <![CDATA[
      // Clean up
    ]]>
  </tearDownScript>
</testCase>
```

content.title: Understanding SOAP Message Structure
content.explanation: **Complete Anatomy of a SOAP Message:** A SOAP message is an XML document with a specific structure that all SOAP-compliant services must follow. **Basic SOAP Message Structure:** ```xml ``` **SOAP Envelope Elements Explained:** | Element | Required | Purpose | Content | |---------|----------|---------|---------| | **Envelope** | Yes | Root element that identifies the XML as a SOAP message | Contains Header and Body | | **Header** | No | Contains application-specific information like authentication, routing, transaction IDs | Metadata elements | | **Body** | Yes | Contains the actual request or response data | Operation name and parameters | | **Fault** | No | Contains error and status information (only present when an error occurs) | Fault code, string, actor, detail | **SOAP Request Example (Calculator Service):** ```xml testuser testpass ABC123XYZ TX-2024-001 2024-03-12T10:30:00Z 15 10 ``` **SOAP Response Example (Success):** ```xml 25 ``` **SOAP Fault Example (Error):** ```xml soap:Client Server was unable to process request ERR-1001 Division by zero is not allowed ``` **SOAP Fault Components:** | Fault Element | Description | Example | |---------------|-------------|---------| | **faultcode** | Identifies the fault type | soap:Client, soap:Server, soap:VersionMismatch, soap:MustUnderstand | | **faultstring** | Human-readable error description | "Division by zero" | | **faultactor** | URI of the source of the fault (optional) | "http://example.com/calculator" | | **detail** | Application-specific error details (optional) | `1001` | **SOAP 1.1 vs SOAP 1.2 Comparison:** | Feature | SOAP 1.1 | SOAP 1.2 | |---------|----------|----------| | **Namespace** | http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/ | http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope | | **Fault Structure** | ``, ``, etc. | ``, ``, etc. | | **HTTP Binding** | Uses SOAPAction header | No SOAPAction header required | | **Content-Type** | text/xml | application/soap+xml | **SOAP 1.2 Fault Example:** ```xml soap12:Sender InvalidParameter Invalid parameter value intB 0 Cannot divide by zero ``` **WSDL (Web Services Description Language):** WSDL is an XML document that describes a SOAP web service. It defines: - **Types:** Data types used by the service - **Messages:** The messages exchanged - **Operations:** Functions the service provides - **Port Types:** Groups of operations - **Bindings:** How to access the service (SOAP over HTTP, etc.) - **Service:** The endpoint URL **WSDL Structure:** ```xml ``` **How SoapUI Uses WSDL:** When you create a SOAP project with a WSDL, SoapUI: 1. Parses the WSDL to discover all operations 2. Generates sample requests for each operation 3. Validates requests against the WSDL schema 4. Uses the endpoint from WSDL (can be overridden) 5. Applies SOAP bindings (SOAP 1.1 vs 1.2) **WSDL Import in SoapUI:** ```xml http://www.dneonline.com/calculator.asmx?WSDL ```
