content.title: Advanced SOAP Request Configuration
content.explanation:
**Customizing SOAP Requests Beyond Basic Templates:**

**1. Setting Request Properties:**

```xml
<!-- In SoapUI, you can set request properties -->
<soapui:request>
  <properties>
    <property name="timeout" value="30000"/>
    <property name="prettyPrint" value="true"/>
    <property name="dumpFile" value="${projectDir}/logs/request.xml"/>
  </properties>
</soapui:request>
```

**2. Configuring HTTP Headers:**

```xml
<!-- Custom HTTP headers for SOAP requests -->
<soapui:request>
  <headers>
    <header name="SOAPAction">http://tempuri.org/Add</header>
    <header name="User-Agent">SoapUI/5.7.2</header>
    <header name="Accept-Encoding">gzip,deflate</header>
    <header name="Connection">Keep-Alive</header>
    <header name="Authorization">Basic dGVzdHVzZXI6dGVzdHBhc3M=</header>
  </headers>
</soapui:request>
```

**3. Using Properties in Requests:**

```xml
<!-- Replace hardcoded values with properties -->
<soap:Envelope>
  <soap:Body>
    <tem:Add>
      <tem:intA>${#Project#defaultIntA}</tem:intA>
      <tem:intB>${#TestCase#testIntB}</tem:intB>
    </tem:Add>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**4. Setting Timeout Values:**

```xml
<!-- Configure timeouts in request -->
<soapui:request>
  <timeout>30000</timeout>  <!-- 30 seconds -->
  <connectionTimeout>10000</connectionTimeout>  <!-- 10 seconds -->
  <maxResponseSize>1048576</maxResponseSize>  <!-- 1 MB -->
</soapui:request>
```

**5. Working with Multiple SOAP Versions:**

```xml
<!-- SOAP 1.1 -->
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  ...
</soap:Envelope>

<!-- SOAP 1.2 -->
<soap12:Envelope xmlns:soap12="http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope">
  ...
</soap12:Envelope>
```

**6. Adding WS-Security Headers:**

```xml
<!-- UsernameToken security -->
<soapenv:Header>
  <wsse:Security xmlns:wsse="http://docs.oasis-open.org/wss/2004/01/oasis-200401-wss-wssecurity-secext-1.0.xsd">
    <wsse:UsernameToken>
      <wsse:Username>${username}</wsse:Username>
      <wsse:Password Type="http://docs.oasis-open.org/wss/2004/01/oasis-200401-wss-username-token-profile-1.0#PasswordText">${password}</wsse:Password>
    </wsse:UsernameToken>
  </wsse:Security>
</soapenv:Header>
```

**7. SOAP Request with Attachments (SwA):**

```xml
<!-- SOAP with Attachments - multipart message -->
Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary="MIME_boundary"; type="text/xml"

--MIME_boundary
Content-Type: text/xml; charset=UTF-8

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<soap:Envelope>
  <soap:Body>
    <UploadDocument>
      <fileName>contract.pdf</fileName>
      <fileContent>cid:contract123</fileContent>
    </UploadDocument>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>

--MIME_boundary
Content-Type: application/pdf
Content-ID: <contract123>
Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64

[base64-encoded PDF content]

--MIME_boundary--
```

**8. MTOM (Message Transmission Optimization Mechanism):**

```xml
<!-- MTOM for optimized binary transmission -->
<soap:Envelope>
  <soap:Body>
    <UploadDocument>
      <fileName>contract.pdf</fileName>
      <fileContent>
        <xop:Include xmlns:xop="http://www.w3.org/2004/08/xop/include" href="cid:contract123"/>
      </fileContent>
    </UploadDocument>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**9. SOAP Request with MustUnderstand Headers:**

```xml
<soapenv:Header>
  <Transaction xmlns="http://example.com/transaction" soapenv:mustUnderstand="1">
    <ID>TX-2024-001</ID>
  </Transaction>
</soapenv:Header>
```

**10. Using Multiple Operations in One Request:**

```xml
<!-- Some services support multiple operations in one body -->
<soap:Body>
  <GetUser>
    <UserId>123</UserId>
  </GetUser>
  <GetOrders>
    <UserId>123</UserId>
  </GetOrders>
</soap:Body>
```

content.title: Comprehensive SOAP Response Handling
content.explanation:
**Understanding and Processing SOAP Responses:** **1. Response Structure:** A SOAP response follows the same envelope structure as requests, with the operation result in the body. **Success Response:** ```xml 25 ``` **2. SOAP Fault Response (Error):** ```xml soap:Server Server Error 500 Internal server error ``` **3. Response Headers:** ```http HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8 Content-Length: 567 Server: Microsoft-IIS/10.0 X-Powered-By: ASP.NET Date: Tue, 12 Mar 2024 10:30:45 GMT ``` **4. Parsing SOAP Responses in SoapUI:** SoapUI automatically parses SOAP responses and provides several views: - **XML View:** Raw XML response with syntax highlighting - **Raw View:** Complete raw response including headers - **Pretty Print:** Formatted XML for readability - **Tree View:** Expandable tree structure of the XML **5. Extracting Data from Responses:** ```groovy // Groovy script to extract response data def response = messageExchange.responseContent def xml = new XmlSlurper().parseText(response) // Extract using GPath (Groovy's path language) def result = xml.Body.AddResponse.AddResult.text() log.info "Add result: ${result}" // Extract with namespace handling def envelope = new XmlSlurper().parseText(response) envelope.declareNamespace('soap':'http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/') envelope.declareNamespace('tem':'http://tempuri.org/') def result2 = envelope.'soap:Body'.'tem:AddResponse'.'tem:AddResult'.text() ``` **6. Using Property Transfer to Extract Values:** ```xml declare namespace tem='http://tempuri.org/'; //tem:AddResult additionResult ``` **7. Handling Complex Response Structures:** ```xml 123 John Doe john@example.com
123 Main St New York NY 10001
1001 2024-03-01 299.99 1002 2024-03-05 149.50 ``` **8. XPath Expressions for Data Extraction:** | XPath Expression | Extracted Value | |------------------|-----------------| | `//User/ID` | 123 | | `//User/Name` | John Doe | | `//Address/City` | New York | | `count(//Order)` | 2 | | `sum(//Amount)` | 449.49 | | `//Order[1]/OrderID` | 1001 | | `//Order[Amount > 200]/OrderID` | 1001 | ```xml declare namespace ns='http://example.com/user'; //ns:User/ns:Name John Doe ``` **9. Response Validation Strategies:** ```xml false //AddResult 25 2000 ${projectDir}/schemas/response.xsd ``` **10. Handling SOAP Faults Gracefully:** ```groovy // Test script to handle SOAP faults try { def response = messageExchange.responseContent def xml = new XmlSlurper().parseText(response) // Check if this is a fault if (xml.Body.Fault.size() > 0) { def faultCode = xml.Body.Fault.faultcode.text() def faultString = xml.Body.Fault.faultstring.text() log.error "SOAP Fault: ${faultCode} - ${faultString}" // Handle specific fault types if (faultCode.contains('Client')) { testRunner.fail("Client error: ${faultString}") } else if (faultCode.contains('Server')) { log.warn "Server error occurred, might be temporary" // Could implement retry logic here } } else { // Normal response processing def result = xml.Body.AddResponse.AddResult.text() log.info "Success, result: ${result}" } } catch (Exception e) { log.error "Error parsing response: ${e.message}" testRunner.fail("Response parsing failed") } ```

content.title: Managing Complex XML Structures in SOAP
content.explanation:
**Handling Nested Elements, Arrays, and Complex Types:**

**1. Complex Type Examples:**

```xml
<!-- Complex type with nested elements -->
<soap:Envelope>
  <soap:Body>
    <PlaceOrder xmlns="http://example.com/orders">
      <Order>
        <OrderHeader>
          <OrderNumber>ORD-2024-001</OrderNumber>
          <OrderDate>2024-03-12</OrderDate>
          <Customer>
            <CustomerID>12345</CustomerID>
            <Name>John Doe</Name>
            <Email>john@example.com</Email>
            <ShippingAddress>
              <Street>123 Main St</Street>
              <City>New York</City>
              <State>NY</State>
              <ZipCode>10001</ZipCode>
              <Country>USA</Country>
            </ShippingAddress>
          </Customer>
        </OrderHeader>
        <OrderItems>
          <Item>
            <ProductID>P-1001</ProductID>
            <ProductName>Laptop</ProductName>
            <Quantity>1</Quantity>
            <UnitPrice>999.99</UnitPrice>
            <Discount>0</Discount>
          </Item>
          <Item>
            <ProductID>P-1002</ProductID>
            <ProductName>Mouse</ProductName>
            <Quantity>2</Quantity>
            <UnitPrice>29.99</UnitPrice>
            <Discount>0.1</Discount>
          </Item>
        </OrderItems>
        <PaymentInfo>
          <PaymentMethod>CreditCard</PaymentMethod>
          <CardType>Visa</CardType>
          <CardNumber>************1234</CardNumber>
          <ExpiryDate>12/25</ExpiryDate>
        </PaymentInfo>
        <OrderTotal>
          <Subtotal>1059.97</Subtotal>
          <Tax>84.80</Tax>
          <Shipping>0</Shipping>
          <Total>1144.77</Total>
        </OrderTotal>
      </Order>
    </PlaceOrder>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**2. XML Arrays (Repeating Elements):**

```xml
<!-- Multiple repeating elements (array) -->
<soap:Body>
  <GetOrderHistoryResponse>
    <Orders>
      <Order>
        <OrderID>1001</OrderID>
        <Date>2024-01-15</Date>
        <Total>299.99</Total>
      </Order>
      <Order>
        <OrderID>1002</OrderID>
        <Date>2024-02-20</Date>
        <Total>149.50</Total>
      </Order>
      <Order>
        <OrderID>1003</OrderID>
        <Date>2024-03-10</Date>
        <Total>89.99</Total>
      </Order>
    </Orders>
  </GetOrderHistoryResponse>
</soap:Body>
```

**3. Working with Attributes in XML:**

```xml
<!-- Elements with attributes -->
<soap:Body>
  <Product xmlns="http://example.com/products">
    <Product id="P1001" status="active">
      <Name language="en">Laptop</Name>
      <Description language="en">High-performance laptop</Description>
      <Price currency="USD">999.99</Price>
    </Product>
  </Product>
</soap:Body>
```

**4. XPath for Complex Data Extraction:**

```xpath
// Extract all order IDs
//Order/OrderID

// Extract order IDs for orders over $200
//Order[Total > 200]/OrderID

// Extract customer name
//Customer/Name

// Extract all items
//OrderItems/Item

// Extract quantity for a specific product
//Item[ProductID='P-1002']/Quantity

// Extract attribute values
//Product/@id
//Price/@currency

// Count elements
count(//Item)

// Sum values
sum(//Order/Total)

// Check if element exists
boolean(//Order[OrderID='1004'])
```

**5. Using XPath in SoapUI Assertions:**

```xml
<assertion type="XPath Match">
  <xpath>declare namespace ns='http://example.com/orders'; count(//ns:Item)</xpath>
  <expected>2</expected>
</assertion>

<assertion type="XPath Match">
  <xpath>declare namespace ns='http://example.com/orders'; //ns:Order/ns:Total</xpath>
  <expected>1144.77</expected>
</assertion>

<assertion type="XPath Match">
  <xpath>declare namespace ns='http://example.com/orders'; //ns:Item[1]/ns:ProductName</xpath>
  <expected>Laptop</expected>
</assertion>
```

**6. Groovy Script for Complex XML Processing:**

```groovy
import groovy.xml.XmlSlurper

def response = messageExchange.responseContent
def xml = new XmlSlurper().parseText(response)

// Handle namespaces
xml.declareNamespace('ns':'http://example.com/orders')

// Extract order summary
def orderNumber = xml.'ns:Body'.'ns:PlaceOrder'.'ns:Order'.'ns:OrderHeader'.'ns:OrderNumber'.text()
log.info "Processing order: ${orderNumber}"

// Calculate total items
int itemCount = xml.'ns:Body'.'ns:PlaceOrder'.'ns:Order'.'ns:OrderItems'.'ns:Item'.size()
log.info "Number of items: ${itemCount}"

// Extract all items and calculate total
def total = 0
def items = []
xml.'ns:Body'.'ns:PlaceOrder'.'ns:Order'.'ns:OrderItems'.'ns:Item'.each { item ->
    def product = item.ProductName.text()
    def qty = item.Quantity.text().toInteger()
    def price = item.UnitPrice.text().toDouble()
    def discount = item.Discount.text().toDouble()
    
    def itemTotal = qty * price * (1 - discount)
    total += itemTotal
    
    items.add([
        product: product,
        quantity: qty,
        unitPrice: price,
        discount: discount,
        total: itemTotal
    ])
    
    log.info "Item: ${product}, Qty: ${qty}, Total: ${itemTotal}"
}

log.info "Grand Total: ${total}"

// Verify calculated total matches response total
def reportedTotal = xml.'ns:Body'.'ns:PlaceOrder'.'ns:Order'.'ns:OrderTotal'.'ns:Total'.text().toDouble()
assert Math.abs(total - reportedTotal) < 0.01 : "Total mismatch: calculated ${total}, reported ${reportedTotal}"
```

**7. XML Schema Validation:**

```xml
<!-- Schema validation assertion -->
<assertion type="Schema Compliance">
  <definition>
    <![CDATA[
    <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
    <xs:schema xmlns:xs="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"
      targetNamespace="http://example.com/orders"
      xmlns="http://example.com/orders">
      
      <xs:element name="Order">
        <xs:complexType>
          <xs:sequence>
            <xs:element name="OrderNumber" type="xs:string"/>
            <xs:element name="OrderDate" type="xs:date"/>
            <xs:element name="Customer" type="CustomerType"/>
            <xs:element name="OrderItems" type="OrderItemsType"/>
            <xs:element name="OrderTotal" type="TotalType"/>
          </xs:sequence>
        </xs:complexType>
      </xs:element>
      
      <xs:complexType name="CustomerType">
        <xs:sequence>
          <xs:element name="CustomerID" type="xs:string"/>
          <xs:element name="Name" type="xs:string"/>
          <xs:element name="Email" type="xs:string"/>
          <xs:element name="ShippingAddress" type="AddressType"/>
        </xs:sequence>
      </xs:complexType>
      
      <!-- Additional type definitions -->
    </xs:schema>
    ]]>
  </definition>
</assertion>
```

**8. Transforming XML with XSLT:**

```groovy
// Transform SOAP response to different format
import javax.xml.transform.*
import javax.xml.transform.stream.*

def response = messageExchange.responseContent
def xslt = '''
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0" xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform"
  xmlns:ns="http://example.com/orders">
  <xsl:output method="text"/>
  
  <xsl:template match="/">
    <xsl:for-each select="//ns:Item">
      <xsl:value-of select="ns:ProductName"/>,<xsl:value-of select="ns:Quantity"/>,<xsl:value-of select="ns:UnitPrice"/>
      <xsl:text>
</xsl:text>
    </xsl:for-each>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
'''

def transformer = TransformerFactory.newInstance().newTransformer(
    new StreamSource(new StringReader(xslt)))

def source = new StreamSource(new StringReader(response))
def writer = new StringWriter()
transformer.transform(source, new StreamResult(writer))

log.info "Transformed data:\n${writer.toString()}"
```

content.title: XML Namespaces in SOAP: Complete Guide
content.explanation:
**What Are Namespaces and Why They Matter:**

Namespaces in XML prevent element name conflicts when combining XML from different sources. They're essential in SOAP because messages often combine elements from multiple schemas.

**Namespace Declaration Syntax:**

```xml
<element xmlns:prefix="namespace-URI">
```

**Common Namespace Patterns:**

```xml
<!-- SOAP Envelope namespace -->
xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"

<!-- Target namespace (service-specific) -->
xmlns:tem="http://tempuri.org/"

<!-- XML Schema namespaces -->
xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"

<!-- WS-Security namespace -->
xmlns:wsse="http://docs.oasis-open.org/wss/2004/01/oasis-200401-wss-wssecurity-secext-1.0.xsd"

<!-- Default namespace (no prefix) -->
xmlns="http://example.com/default"
```

**Namespace Scope:**

```xml
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  <!-- soap: prefix applies within this scope -->
  <soap:Header>
    <auth:Authentication xmlns:auth="http://example.com/auth">
      <!-- auth: prefix applies here and in children -->
      <auth:Username>user</auth:Username>
    </auth:Authentication>
  </soap:Header>
  <soap:Body>
    <tem:Add xmlns:tem="http://tempuri.org/">
      <!-- tem: prefix applies here -->
      <tem:intA>15</tem:intA>
      <tem:intB>10</tem:intB>
    </tem:Add>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**Default Namespace (No Prefix):**

```xml
<!-- Elements without prefix belong to default namespace -->
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"
               xmlns="http://tempuri.org/">
  <soap:Body>
    <Add>
      <!-- These are in default namespace (http://tempuri.org/) -->
      <intA>15</intA>
      <intB>10</intB>
    </Add>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**XPath with Namespaces:**

```xpath
// Without namespace declaration, XPath won't match
//Add  <!-- This won't work if Add is in a namespace -->

// Need to declare namespaces in XPath
declare namespace tem='http://tempuri.org/';
//tem:Add

// Multiple namespace declarations
declare namespace soap='http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/';
declare namespace tem='http://tempuri.org/';
//soap:Envelope//tem:Add/tem:intA
```

**XPath with Namespaces in SoapUI:**

```xml
<!-- XPath assertion with namespace declaration -->
<assertion type="XPath Match">
  <xpath>
    declare namespace soap='http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/';
    declare namespace tem='http://tempuri.org/';
    //tem:AddResult
  </xpath>
  <expected>25</expected>
</assertion>
```

**Property Transfer with Namespaces:**

```xml
<transfer>
  <source type="response">
    <xpath>
      declare namespace soap='http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/';
      declare namespace tem='http://tempuri.org/';
      //tem:AddResult
    </xpath>
  </source>
  <target type="property">
    <name>result</name>
  </target>
</transfer>
```

**Groovy Script with Namespace Handling:**

```groovy
import groovy.xml.XmlSlurper

def response = messageExchange.responseContent
def xml = new XmlSlurper().parseText(response)

// Method 1: Declare namespaces in the slurper
xml.declareNamespace(
    'soap': 'http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/',
    'tem': 'http://tempuri.org/'
)

def result = xml.'soap:Body'.'tem:AddResponse'.'tem:AddResult'.text()
log.info "Result: ${result}"

// Method 2: Use GPath with namespaces
def result2 = xml.Body.AddResponse.AddResult.text()
// This works if namespaces are properly declared

// Method 3: Handle default namespaces
if (xml.Body.AddResponse.AddResult.@namespaceURI() == 'http://tempuri.org/') {
    log.info "In correct namespace"
}
```

**Common Namespace Issues and Solutions:**

| Issue | Symptom | Solution |
|-------|---------|----------|
| **XPath not matching** | Assertion fails even though value exists | Declare namespaces in XPath |
| **Default namespace** | Elements have no prefix, XPath fails | Use `*[local-name()='Add']` or declare default namespace |
| **Multiple namespaces** | Wrong values extracted | Be specific with namespace prefixes |
| **Namespace changes** | Tests break after WSDL update | Update namespace declarations in XPath |

**Namespace-Agnostic XPath:**

```xpath
/*[local-name()='Envelope']/*[local-name()='Body']/*[local-name()='AddResponse']/*[local-name()='AddResult']

//*[local-name()='AddResult']

//*[namespace-uri()='http://tempuri.org/' and local-name()='AddResult']
```

**When to Use Which Approach:**

- **Declared namespaces:** Most readable, use when namespaces are stable
- **Local-name:** Use when namespaces might change but element names stay same
- **Namespace-uri:** Use when element names might be reused across namespaces

content.title: XPath Mastery for SOAP Testing
content.explanation:
**Complete XPath Reference for SOAP Message Processing:**

**XPath Syntax Basics:**

| Expression | Description | Example | Result |
|------------|-------------|---------|--------|
| `/` | Root element | `/soap:Envelope` | Root element |
| `//` | Any descendant | `//AddResult` | All AddResult elements |
| `.` | Current node | `.//Item` | Items under current node |
| `..` | Parent node | `..` | Parent of current node |
| `@` | Attribute | `//Product/@id` | id attributes |
| `*` | Any element | `//*` | All elements |
| `|` | Union | `//Add | //Subtract` | Add or Subtract elements |

**XPath Predicates (Filters):**

```xpath
//Order[1]                    // First Order
//Order[last()]               // Last Order
//Order[position() < 3]        // First two orders
//Order[Total > 100]           // Orders with Total > 100
//Item[Quantity >= 2]          // Items with quantity 2 or more
//Product[@status='active']    // Products with active status
//Order[OrderID='1001']        // Order with specific ID
//Item[contains(ProductName,'Laptop')]  // Items containing 'Laptop'
//Item[starts-with(ProductID,'P-')]     // Items with ID starting 'P-'
```

**XPath Functions:**

| Function | Description | Example |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| `text()` | Element text content | `//Name/text()` |
| `count()` | Count nodes | `count(//Item)` |
| `sum()` | Sum values | `sum(//Total)` |
| `avg()` | Average | `avg(//Price)` |
| `min()` | Minimum | `min(//Price)` |
| `max()` | Maximum | `max(//Price)` |
| `contains()` | Contains text | `//Name[contains(text(),'John')]` |
| `starts-with()` | Starts with text | `//Product[starts-with(@id,'P-')]` |
| `ends-with()` | Ends with text | `//Product[ends-with(@id,'US')]` |
| `not()` | Negation | `//Item[not(Quantity)]` |
| `normalize-space()` | Remove whitespace | `//Name[normalize-space()='John']` |

**XPath for Common SOAP Scenarios:**

```xpath
// Extract operation result
//AddResult
//SubtractResult
//MultiplyResult
//DivideResult

// Extract with namespace
declare namespace tem='http://tempuri.org/';
//tem:AddResult

// Extract from SOAP envelope
declare namespace soap='http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/';
//soap:Body//tem:AddResult

// Check if SOAP fault exists
count(//soap:Fault) > 0

// Extract fault information
//faultcode
//faultstring
//detail//error/message

// Extract multiple values
//Order/OrderID | //Order/Total

// Extract with conditions
//Order[Total > 1000]/OrderID

// Count items in order
count(//OrderItems/Item)

// Sum of all orders
sum(//Total)

// Check element exists
boolean(//Order[OrderID='1001'])
```

**XPath in SoapUI Assertions:**

```xml
<!-- Match exact value -->
<assertion type="XPath Match">
  <xpath>declare namespace tem='http://tempuri.org/'; //tem:AddResult</xpath>
  <expected>25</expected>
</assertion>

<!-- Match using wildcard -->
<assertion type="XPath Match">
  <xpath>declare namespace tem='http://tempuri.org/'; //tem:AddResult</xpath>
  <expected>*</expected>  <!-- Any non-empty value -->
  <allowWildcards>true</allowWildcards>
</assertion>

<!-- Check existence -->
<assertion type="XPath Match">
  <xpath>declare namespace tem='http://tempuri.org/'; exists(//tem:AddResult)</xpath>
  <expected>true</expected>
</assertion>
```

**XPath in Property Transfer:**

```xml
<!-- Extract single value -->
<transfer>
  <source type="response">
    <xpath>declare namespace tem='http://tempuri.org/'; //tem:AddResult</xpath>
  </source>
  <target type="property">
    <name>addResult</name>
  </target>
</transfer>

<!-- Extract multiple values (to list) -->
<transfer>
  <source type="response">
    <xpath>declare namespace ord='http://example.com/orders'; //ord:OrderID</xpath>
  </source>
  <target type="property">
    <name>orderIds</name>
  </target>
</transfer>
```

**XPath in Groovy Scripts:**

```groovy
import javax.xml.xpath.*
import org.xml.sax.InputSource

def response = messageExchange.responseContent
def xpath = XPathFactory.newInstance().newXPath()

// Set namespace context
xpath.namespaceContext = new NamespaceContext() {
    def namespaces = [
        'soap': 'http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/',
        'tem': 'http://tempuri.org/'
    ]
    
    String getNamespaceURI(String prefix) {
        return namespaces[prefix]
    }
}

// Evaluate XPath
def expression = "//tem:AddResult"
def result = xpath.evaluate(expression, new InputSource(new StringReader(response)))
log.info "Result: ${result}"

// Evaluate XPath that returns nodeset
def nodes = xpath.evaluateExpression("//Order", new InputSource(new StringReader(response)))
nodes.each { node ->
    log.info "Order node: ${node}"
}
```

**XPath Testing Tips:**

✅ **Test XPath in SoapUI:** Use the XPath tester in the assertion dialog
✅ **Start Simple:** Begin with simple paths and add complexity gradually
✅ **Use Namespaces:** Always declare namespaces when elements have them
✅ **Test with Sample Data:** Verify XPath works with actual responses
✅ **Consider Performance:** Complex XPath can be slow on large responses
✅ **Handle Missing Elements:** Use existence checks before extracting values

**XPath Cheat Sheet:**

```
Path Expressions:
  /root/child           - Absolute path
  //element            - Any element anywhere
  .//element           - Any element under current node
  parent/child         - Child under parent
  element[@attr]       - Element with attribute
  element[@attr='val'] - Element with specific attribute

Predicates:
  [1]                  - First element
  [last()]             - Last element
  [position()<3]       - First two elements
  [value>10]           - Elements with value > 10
  [contains(text(),'x')] - Elements containing 'x'

Functions:
  text()               - Element text
  count(node-set)      - Number of nodes
  sum(node-set)        - Sum of values
  name()               - Element name
  namespace-uri()      - Namespace URI
  local-name()         - Local name (without prefix)
  contains(s1,s2)      - String contains
  starts-with(s1,s2)   - String starts with
  ends-with(s1,s2)     - String ends with
  normalize-space()    - Remove whitespace
```

content.title: SOAP with Attachments: Complete Guide
content.explanation:
**Sending Binary Data with SOAP Messages:**

SOAP services can handle binary attachments using two main approaches:

1. **SwA (SOAP with Attachments)** - Traditional multipart MIME attachments
2. **MTOM (Message Transmission Optimization Mechanism)** - Optimized binary transmission

**SwA - SOAP with Attachments:**

SwA uses multipart MIME messages where the SOAP message is one part and attachments are additional parts.

```http
POST /upload HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary="MIME_boundary"; type="text/xml"
Content-Length: 12345

--MIME_boundary
Content-Type: text/xml; charset=UTF-8
Content-ID: <soap-part@example.com>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  <soap:Body>
    <UploadDocument xmlns="http://example.com/document">
      <fileName>contract.pdf</fileName>
      <document>
        <xop:Include xmlns:xop="http://www.w3.org/2004/08/xop/include" href="cid:contract123@example.com"/>
      </document>
    </UploadDocument>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>

--MIME_boundary
Content-Type: application/pdf
Content-ID: <contract123@example.com>
Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64


--MIME_boundary--
```

**MTOM (Message Transmission Optimization Mechanism):**

MTOM is a more efficient standard that optimizes binary data transmission.

```xml
<!-- MTOM-enabled SOAP request -->
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"
               xmlns:xop="http://www.w3.org/2004/08/xop/include">
  <soap:Header>
    <wsoma:Using xmlns:wsoma="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2004/09/mtom"
                 soap:mustUnderstand="1">
       application/xop+xml
    </wsoma:Using>
  </soap:Header>
  <soap:Body>
    <UploadDocument xmlns="http://example.com/document">
      <fileName>contract.pdf</fileName>
      <document>
        <xop:Include href="cid:contract123@example.com"/>
      </document>
    </UploadDocument>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**Configuring Attachments in SoapUI:**

**Step 1: Add Attachment to Request:**

```xml
<!-- In SoapUI request editor -->
<soapui:request>
  <attachments>
    <attachment>
      <filePath>${projectDir}/data/sample.pdf</filePath>
      <contentType>application/pdf</contentType>
      <contentId>document123</contentId>
    </attachment>
  </attachments>
</soapui:request>
```

**Step 2: Reference Attachment in SOAP Body:**

```xml
<soap:Body>
  <UploadDocument>
    <fileName>sample.pdf</fileName>
    <document>
      <xop:Include xmlns:xop="http://www.w3.org/2004/08/xop/include" 
                   href="cid:document123"/>
    </document>
  </UploadDocument>
</soap:Body>
```

**Step 3: Configure MTOM (if required):**

```xml
<!-- Enable MTOM in request properties -->
<soapui:request>
  <properties>
    <property name="mtomEnabled" value="true"/>
    <property name="mtomThreshold" value="1024"/> <!-- 1KB threshold -->
  </properties>
</soapui:request>
```

**Groovy Script for Attachment Handling:**

```groovy
// Add attachment programmatically
def request = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("UploadDocument")
request.attachments.clear()

// Add file attachment
def file = new File(context.expand('${projectDir}') + '/data/sample.pdf')
request.attachFile(file, 'application/pdf', 'document123')

// Add byte array attachment
byte[] data = "Sample content".bytes
request.attachBytes(data, 'text/plain', 'textfile123')

// Access attachments in response
def responseStep = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("UploadResponse")
def attachments = responseStep.getAttachments()
attachments.each { attachment ->
    log.info "Attachment: ${attachment.contentType}, Size: ${attachment.size}"
    def content = attachment.getContent()
    // Process attachment content
}
```

**Handling Attachments in Responses:**

```groovy
// Extract attachment from response
def response = messageExchange.getResponseContent()
def attachments = messageExchange.getResponseAttachments()

attachments.each { attachment ->
    log.info "Received attachment:"
    log.info "  Content-ID: ${attachment.contentId}"
    log.info "  Content-Type: ${attachment.contentType}"
    log.info "  Size: ${attachment.size} bytes"
    
    // Save attachment to file
    def filename = "downloaded_${System.currentTimeMillis()}.bin"
    def file = new File(filename)
    file.bytes = attachment.getContent()
    log.info "Saved to: ${file.absolutePath}"
}
```

**Testing File Upload Scenarios:**

```xml
<testCase name="File Upload Test">
  <testStep name="Upload PDF" type="soaprequest">
    <config>
      <attachments>
        <attachment>
          <filePath>${projectDir}/data/test.pdf</filePath>
          <contentId>pdf123</contentId>
        </attachment>
      </attachments>
      <request>
        <![CDATA[
        <soap:Envelope>
          <soap:Body>
            <UploadDocument>
              <fileName>test.pdf</fileName>
              <fileSize>${#Project#getFileSize('data/test.pdf')}</fileSize>
              <document>
                <xop:Include href="cid:pdf123"/>
              </document>
            </UploadDocument>
          </soap:Body>
        </soap:Envelope>
        ]]>
      </request>
    </config>
    <assertions>
      <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>200</codes></assertion>
      <assertion type="XPath Match">
        <xpath>//UploadResult/Status</xpath>
        <expected>success</expected>
      </assertion>
    </assertions>
  </testStep>
</testCase>
```

**File Upload Helper Functions:**

```groovy
// Helper script for file operations
def getFileSize(filename) {
    def file = new File(context.expand('${projectDir}') + '/' + filename)
    return file.length()
}

def getFileChecksum(filename, algorithm = 'MD5') {
    def file = new File(context.expand('${projectDir}') + '/' + filename)
    def digest = java.security.MessageDigest.getInstance(algorithm)
    file.withInputStream { is ->
        byte[] buffer = new byte[8192]
        int read
        while ((read = is.read(buffer)) != -1) {
            digest.update(buffer, 0, read)
        }
    }
    return digest.digest().encodeHex().toString()
}

// Add to test case properties
testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('testFileSize', getFileSize('data/test.pdf').toString())
testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('testFileMD5', getFileChecksum('data/test.pdf'))
```

**Best Practices for Attachment Testing:**

✅ **File Size Limits:** Test with various file sizes
✅ **Content Types:** Test different MIME types
✅ **Correlation:** Verify uploaded file matches downloaded
✅ **Error Cases:** Test with invalid files, missing attachments
✅ **Performance:** Test with large files (10MB, 100MB, 1GB)
✅ **Security:** Test with malicious content, viruses
✅ **Validation:** Verify server properly validates file content

**Common Attachment Testing Scenarios:**

| Scenario | Test Approach | Expected Result |
|----------|---------------|-----------------|
| **Small file** | Upload 1KB text file | Success, verify content |
| **Large file** | Upload 100MB file | Success, verify checksum |
| **Invalid type** | Upload .exe file | Should be rejected |
| **Empty file** | Upload 0-byte file | Should be handled appropriately |
| **Multiple files** | Upload 5 files at once | All accepted and processed |
| **Corrupt file** | Upload damaged PDF | Should report corruption |
| **Missing attachment** | Reference non-existent CID | Should return error |

**Performance Testing for Attachments:**

```groovy
// Measure upload/download times
def testFileSizes = [1024, 10240, 102400, 1048576, 10485760] // 1KB to 10MB

testFileSizes.each { size ->
    // Generate test file
    def file = new File("test_${size}.bin")
    file.bytes = new byte[size]
    
    def start = System.currentTimeMillis()
    // Perform upload
    uploadFile(file)
    def uploadTime = System.currentTimeMillis() - start
    
    log.info "Size: ${size} bytes, Upload time: ${uploadTime}ms, Speed: ${size/uploadTime} KB/s"
    
    file.delete()
}
```

**MTOM vs SwA Comparison:**

| Aspect | SwA | MTOM |
|--------|-----|------|
| **Standard** | Older, less common | W3C Recommendation |
| **Efficiency** | Base64 encoding overhead | Optimized binary |
| **Parsing** | Requires MIME parser | Integrated with XML |
| **Tool Support** | Widely supported | Modern tools support |
| **Use Case** | Legacy systems | New development |

**SoapUI Attachment Configuration Summary:**

```xml
<!-- Complete attachment configuration -->
<soapui:request>
  <mtomEnabled>true</mtomEnabled>
  <mtomThreshold>1024</mtomThreshold>
  <attachments>
    <attachment>
      <filePath>${projectDir}/data/document.pdf</filePath>
      <contentType>application/pdf</contentType>
      <contentId>doc123</contentId>
      <inline>false</inline>
    </attachment>
    <attachment>
      <filePath>${projectDir}/data/image.jpg</filePath>
      <contentType>image/jpeg</contentType>
      <contentId>img456</contentId>
    </attachment>
  </attachments>
</soapui:request>
```

content.title: SOAP Testing Best Practices and Patterns
content.explanation:
**Proven Strategies for Effective SOAP API Testing:**

**1. Test Organization:**

```xml
<testSuite name="Calculator SOAP Tests">
  <!-- Smoke tests - quick validation -->
  <testSuite name="Smoke Tests">
    <testCase name="Add - Positive Numbers"/>
    <testCase name="Subtract - Positive Numbers"/>
  </testSuite>
  
  <!-- Functional tests - comprehensive coverage -->
  <testSuite name="Functional Tests">
    <testCase name="Add - All Combinations">
      <dataSource>
        <type>CSV</type>
        <file>data/add-test-data.csv</file>
      </dataSource>
    </testCase>
    <testCase name="Divide - Edge Cases">
      <dataSource>
        <type>Grid</type>
        <columns>
          <column name="intA" values="10,10,10"/>
          <column name="intB" values="2,1,0"/>
          <column name="expectedFault" values="false,false,true"/>
        </columns>
      </dataSource>
    </testCase>
  </testSuite>
  
  <!-- Error handling tests -->
  <testSuite name="Error Tests">
    <testCase name="Invalid Input"/>
    <testCase name="Missing Parameters"/>
    <testCase name="Authentication Failure"/>
  </testSuite>
</testSuite>
```

**2. Comprehensive Assertion Strategy:**

```xml
<testStep name="Add Operation">
  <assertions>
    <!-- Protocol level -->
    <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>200</codes></assertion>
    
    <!-- Schema compliance -->
    <assertion type="Schema Compliance">
      <definition>${projectDir}/schemas/calculator.xsd</definition>
    </assertion>
    
    <!-- SOAP-specific -->
    <assertion type="SOAP Fault">
      <faultShouldExist>false</faultShouldExist>
    </assertion>
    
    <!-- Content validation -->
    <assertion type="XPath Match">
      <xpath>declare namespace tem='http://tempuri.org/'; //tem:AddResult</xpath>
      <expected>${expectedResult}</expected>
    </assertion>
    
    <!-- Performance -->
    <assertion type="Response SLA">
      <time>2000</time>
    </assertion>
    
    <!-- Response size -->
    <assertion type="Size Assertion">
      <min>100</min>
      <max>5000</max>
    </assertion>
  </assertions>
</testStep>
```

**3. Data-Driven Testing with CSV:**

```csv
intA,intB,expectedResult,expectedFault
15,10,25,false
20,7,27,false
-5,3,-2,false
10,0,,true  # Division by zero
```

**4. Property Management:**

```xml
<!-- Project-level properties -->
<project>
  <properties>
    <property name="calculator.endpoint" value="http://www.dneonline.com/calculator.asmx"/>
    <property name="soap.version" value="1.1"/>
    <property name="default.timeout" value="30000"/>
  </properties>
</project>

<!-- TestSuite-level properties -->
<testSuite>
  <properties>
    <property name="testDataDir" value="${projectDir}/data"/>
    <property name="testIterations" value="10"/>
  </properties>
</testSuite>
```

**5. Reusable Script Library:**

```groovy
// SOAPHelper.groovy - Reusable functions
class SOAPHelper {
    
    static def extractValue(String response, String xpath, Map namespaces) {
        def xml = new XmlSlurper().parseText(response)
        namespaces.each { prefix, uri ->
            xml.declareNamespace(prefix, uri)
        }
        return xml.'**'.find { node ->
            node.name() == xpath.tokenize('/').last()
        }?.text()
    }
    
    static def hasFault(String response) {
        def xml = new XmlSlurper().parseText(response)
        return xml.Body.Fault.size() > 0
    }
    
    static def getFaultDetails(String response) {
        def xml = new XmlSlurper().parseText(response)
        if (xml.Body.Fault.size() > 0) {
            return [
                code: xml.Body.Fault.faultcode.text(),
                string: xml.Body.Fault.faultstring.text(),
                detail: xml.Body.Fault.detail.toString()
            ]
        }
        return null
    }
    
    static def validateAgainstSchema(String response, String schemaFile) {
        // Implementation of schema validation
    }
}

// Usage in test case
def helper = new SOAPHelper()
def result = helper.extractValue(context.response,
    '//AddResult',
    ['tem':'http://tempuri.org/'])
```

**6. Error Handling Patterns:**

```groovy
try {
    // Execute SOAP request
    def response = testRunner.runTestStepByName("Add Operation")
    
    // Check for SOAP fault
    if (SOAPHelper.hasFault(response)) {
        def fault = SOAPHelper.getFaultDetails(response)
        log.warn "SOAP Fault: ${fault.code} - ${fault.string}"
        
        // Handle specific fault types
        if (fault.code.contains('Client')) {
            testRunner.fail("Client error: ${fault.string}")
        } else if (fault.code.contains('Server')) {
            // Retry for server errors
            testRunner.runTestStepByName("Add Operation - Retry")
        }
    }
} catch (Exception e) {
    log.error "Test failed: ${e.message}"
    testRunner.fail(e.message)
} finally {
    // Cleanup if needed
    log.info "Test completed"
}
```

**7. Performance Testing Pattern:**

```xml
<loadTest name="Calculator Load Test">
  <threads>
    <min>10</min>
    <max>100</max>
    <increment>10</increment>
  </threads>
  <duration>
    <rampUp>60</rampUp>
    <steady>300</steady>
    <rampDown>60</rampDown>
  </duration>
  <testSteps>
    <testStep name="Add" weight="4"/>
    <testStep name="Subtract" weight="3"/>
    <testStep name="Multiply" weight="2"/>
    <testStep name="Divide" weight="1"/>
  </testSteps>
</loadTest>
```

**8. SOAP Version Handling:**

```xml
<!-- SOAP 1.1 request -->
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  ...
</soap:Envelope>

<!-- SOAP 1.2 request -->
<soap12:Envelope xmlns:soap12="http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope">
  ...
</soap12:Envelope>

<!-- Dynamic version selection -->
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="${#Project#soapNamespace}">
```

**9. WS-Security Implementation:**

```xml
<soap:Header>
  <wsse:Security xmlns:wsse="http://docs.oasis-open.org/wss/2004/01/oasis-200401-wss-wssecurity-secext-1.0.xsd">
    <wsse:UsernameToken>
      <wsse:Username>${username}</wsse:Username>
      <wsse:Password Type="http://docs.oasis-open.org/wss/2004/01/oasis-200401-wss-username-token-profile-1.0#PasswordDigest">${passwordDigest}</wsse:Password>
      <wsse:Nonce>${nonce}</wsse:Nonce>
      <wsu:Created xmlns:wsu="http://docs.oasis-open.org/wss/2004/01/oasis-200401-wss-wssecurity-utility-1.0.xsd">${timestamp}</wsu:Created>
    </wsse:UsernameToken>
  </wsse:Security>
</soap:Header>
```

**10. Continuous Integration Setup:**

```yaml
# GitHub Actions for SOAP tests
name: SOAP API Tests
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Run SOAP tests
        run: |
          testrunner.sh -s "Calculator SOAP Tests" \
            -f reports \
            -j -r \
            -Pendpoint=${CALCULATOR_URL} \
            calculator-soap-project.xml
      - name: Publish test results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v2
        with:
          name: test-reports
          path: reports/
```

**11. Common SOAP Testing Pitfalls:**

| Pitfall | Symptom | Solution |
|---------|---------|----------|
| **Namespace mismatch** | XPath assertions fail | Verify namespace URIs and prefixes |
| **SOAPAction header missing** | 500 Internal Server Error | Add correct SOAPAction header |
| **Wrong SOAP version** | Service returns fault | Check WSDL for expected version |
| **Missing WS-Security** | Authentication fails | Add required security headers |
| **Invalid XML structure** | Parser errors | Validate against schema |
| **Attachment issues** | Files not received | Check content-id references |

**12. SOAP Testing Checklist:**

✅ **WSDL Validation:** Ensure WSDL is accessible and valid
✅ **Schema Compliance:** Validate requests/responses against schema
✅ **Positive Tests:** All operations with valid inputs
✅ **Negative Tests:** Invalid inputs, missing parameters
✅ **Edge Cases:** Boundaries, empty values, special characters
✅ **Error Handling:** SOAP faults, HTTP errors
✅ **Performance:** Response times under load
✅ **Security:** Authentication, authorization
✅ **Attachments:** File uploads and downloads
✅ **Interoperability:** Test with different SOAP versions

**13. Advanced SOAP Testing Tools in SoapUI:**

| Feature | Purpose | How to Use |
|---------|---------|------------|
| **WS-Security Editor** | Configure security headers | In request editor, WS-Security tab |
| **Schema Compliance** | Validate against XSD | Add Schema Compliance assertion |
| **XPath Assertion** | Validate specific elements | Add XPath Match assertion |
| **Property Transfer** | Extract values between steps | Add Property Transfer test step |
| **Data Source** | Data-driven testing | Add DataSource and DataSourceLoop |
| **Mock Services** | Simulate SOAP services | Create MockService from WSDL |

**14. SOAP Testing Metrics to Track:**

| Metric | Target | How to Measure |
|--------|--------|----------------|
| **Response Time** | < 2s | Response SLA assertion |
| **Success Rate** | > 99% | Pass/fail statistics |
| **Schema Compliance** | 100% | Schema Compliance assertions |
| **Coverage** | > 90% | Test all operations and parameters |
| **SOAP Fault Rate** | < 1% | Count of fault responses |

**15. Conclusion: SOAP Testing Excellence**

Mastering SOAP testing in SoapUI requires understanding:
- SOAP message structure and namespaces
- WSDL interpretation and usage
- XPath for precise data extraction
- Attachment handling for binary data
- WS-Security for secure services
- Data-driven testing for comprehensive coverage
- Performance testing for scalability

With these skills, you can effectively test any SOAP web service, from simple calculator APIs to complex enterprise services with security, attachments, and complex data structures.

content.title: Understanding API Security Testing
content.explanation:
**Why Security Testing Matters for APIs:**

APIs are prime targets for attackers because they expose application logic and data directly. Security testing helps identify vulnerabilities before they can be exploited.

**The OWASP API Security Top 10:**

| Rank | Vulnerability | Description |
|------|---------------|-------------|
| **API1** | Broken Object Level Authorization | Users can access objects they shouldn't |
| **API2** | Broken Authentication | Flaws in authentication mechanisms |
| **API3** | Excessive Data Exposure | APIs return more data than needed |
| **API4** | Lack of Resources & Rate Limiting | No limits on request rates |
| **API5** | Broken Function Level Authorization | Users can perform unauthorized functions |
| **API6** | Mass Assignment | Users can modify object properties |
| **API7** | Security Misconfiguration | Insecure default configurations |
| **API8** | Injection | SQL, NoSQL, command injection |
| **API9** | Improper Assets Management | Old API versions still accessible |
| **API10** | Insufficient Logging & Monitoring | Attacks go undetected |

**Security Testing Types:**

```
Security Testing
├── Static Analysis (SAST)
│   ├── Code review
│   ├── WSDL/Swagger analysis
│   └── Configuration review
├── Dynamic Analysis (DAST)
│   ├── Vulnerability scanning
│   ├── Fuzzing
│   ├── Injection testing
│   └── Authentication testing
├── Penetration Testing
│   ├── Manual exploitation
│   ├── Business logic flaws
│   └── Chained attacks
└── Compliance Testing
    ├── PCI-DSS
    ├── HIPAA
    └── GDPR
```

**SoapUI Security Testing Features:**

SoapUI Pro provides comprehensive security testing capabilities:

1. **Automated Security Scans:** Pre-configured scans for common vulnerabilities
2. **Custom Security Tests:** Create custom security test cases
3. **Fuzzing:** Generate malicious payloads automatically
4. **Authentication Testing:** Test various auth mechanisms
5. **SSL/TLS Testing:** Validate certificate handling
6. **Comprehensive Reports:** Detailed vulnerability reports

**Security Testing Workflow:**

```
1. Discovery → 2. Scanning → 3. Exploitation → 4. Verification → 5. Reporting
     ↓              ↓              ↓                ↓               ↓
Map endpoints   Run scans     Attempt exploit   Verify fix      Document findings
```

**Setting Up Security Tests in SoapUI:**

```xml
<soapui-project name="Security Test Project">
  <!-- Create a SecurityTest under a TestCase -->
  <testSuite name="Security Tests">
    <testCase name="API Security Scan">
      <securityTest name="Full Security Scan">
        <strategy>Full</strategy>
        <scans>
          <scan type="SQLInjection"/>
          <scan type="XSS"/>
          <scan type="MalformedXML"/>
          <scan type="Fuzzing"/>
        </scans>
      </securityTest>
    </testCase>
  </testSuite>
</soapui-project>
```

content.title: Common API Vulnerabilities and SoapUI Security Tests
Testing Authentication Mechanisms
content.explanation:
**Validating API Security Through Authentication Testing:**

Authentication is the first line of defense. Testing it thoroughly is crucial.

**Authentication Attack Vectors:**

```
Authentication Attacks
├── Credential-based
│   ├── Brute force
│   ├── Dictionary attacks
│   ├── Credential stuffing
│   └── Default credentials
├── Token-based
│   ├── Token tampering
│   ├── Token expiration
│   ├── Token replay
│   └── JWT vulnerabilities
├── Session-based
│   ├── Session fixation
│   ├── Session hijacking
│   └── Session timeout issues
└── OAuth flows
    ├── Authorization code interception
    ├── CSRF in OAuth
    └── Scope escalation
```

**Setting Up Authentication Tests in SoapUI:**

```xml
<securityTest name="Authentication Security Scan">
  <targets>
    <target name="Login Endpoint">
      <endpoint>${#Project#apiUrl}/auth/login</endpoint>
      <method>POST</method>
    </target>
  </targets>
  
  <scans>
    <!-- Brute Force Testing -->
    <scan type="BruteForce">
      <usernameField>username</usernameField>
      <passwordField>password</passwordField>
      <usernames>
        <value>admin</value>
        <value>administrator</value>
        <value>root</value>
        <file>data/common-usernames.txt</file>
      </usernames>
      <passwords>
        <file>data/common-passwords.txt</file>
      </passwords>
      <delay>1000</delay> <!-- ms between attempts -->
      <stopOnSuccess>true</stopOnSuccess>
    </scan>
    
    <!-- Token Manipulation -->
    <scan type="TokenManipulation">
      <tokenLocation>header:Authorization</tokenLocation>
      <tokenFormat>Bearer .*</tokenFormat>
      <manipulations>
        <manipulation type="remove"/>
        <manipulation type="empty"/>
        <manipulation type="expired">
          <value>eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4gRG9lIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyLCJleHAiOjE1MTYyMzkwMjJ9.SflKxwRJSMeKKF2QT4fwpMeJf36POk6yJV_adQssw5c</value>
        </manipulation>
        <manipulation type="invalid">
          <value>invalid.token.here</value>
        </manipulation>
        <manipulation type="tampered">
          <value>eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwicm9sZSI6ImFkbWluIn0.tampered</value>
        </manipulation>
      </manipulations>
    </scan>
    
    <!-- Session Testing -->
    <scan type="SessionTesting">
      <checks>
        <check>sessionFixation</check>
        <check>sessionTimeout</check>
        <check>concurrentSessions</check>
      </checks>
      <timeout>1800</timeout> <!-- 30 minutes -->
    </scan>
  </scans>
</securityTest>
```

**Groovy Script for Custom Authentication Testing:**

```groovy
// Custom authentication test script
import groovy.json.JsonSlurper

def testAuthentication(username, password) {
    def request = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("Login")
    request.setPropertyValue("username", username)
    request.setPropertyValue("password", password)
    
    request.run(testRunner, context)
    
    def status = request.getPropertyValue("httpResponseCode")
    def response = request.getPropertyValue("response")
    
    return [
        status: status,
        response: response,
        success: (status == "200")
    ]
}

// Test common credentials
def credentials = [
    [username: "admin", password: "admin"],
    [username: "admin", password: "password"],
    [username: "admin", password: "123456"],
    [username: "administrator", password: "admin"],
    [username: "root", password: "root"],
    [username: "test", password: "test"]
]

credentials.each { cred ->
    def result = testAuthentication(cred.username, cred.password)
    log.info "Testing ${cred.username}:${cred.password} → Status: ${result.status}"
    
    if (result.success) {
        log.warn "⚠️ SUCCESSFUL LOGIN with weak credentials: ${cred.username}:${cred.password}"
    }
}
```

**JWT Token Testing:**

```groovy
// JWT vulnerability testing
import java.util.Base64

def analyzeJWT(token) {
    def parts = token.split('\.')
    if (parts.length != 3) {
        return [error: "Invalid JWT format"]
    }
    
    def header = new String(Base64.decoder.decode(parts[0]))
    def payload = new String(Base64.decoder.decode(parts[1]))
    def signature = parts[2]
    
    log.info "JWT Analysis:"
    log.info "Header: ${header}"
    log.info "Payload: ${payload}"
    
    def json = new JsonSlurper().parseText(payload)
    
    // Check for common issues
    def issues = []
    if (!json.exp) {
        issues.add("No expiration")
    }
    if (json.alg == "none") {
        issues.add("Algorithm set to 'none'")
    }
    if (json.role == "admin" || json.admin) {
        issues.add("Contains privileged role")
    }
    
    return issues
}

def token = context.expand('${#TestCase#authToken}')
def issues = analyzeJWT(token)
if (issues.size() > 0) {
    log.warn "JWT Issues found: ${issues}"
}
```

**Authentication Test Cases:**

| Test Case | Description | Expected Result |
|-----------|-------------|-----------------|
| **No Credentials** | Request without auth | 401 Unauthorized |
| **Invalid Credentials** | Wrong username/password | 401 Unauthorized |
| **Empty Password** | Valid username, empty password | 400 Bad Request |
| **SQL Injection** | Username: ' OR '1'='1 | 401 Unauthorized |
| **Long Input** | 10,000 character password | 400/413 or timeout |
| **Special Characters** | Username: !@#$%^&*() | 400 or sanitized |
| **Token Tampering** | Modified JWT token | 401 Unauthorized |
| **Expired Token** | Token past expiration | 401 Unauthorized |
| **Wrong Signature** | Token with invalid signature | 401 Unauthorized |
| **Rate Limiting** | 100 requests in 1 second | 429 Too Many Requests |

content.title: SSL/TLS Certificate Management in SoapUI
content.explanation:
**Ensuring Secure Communication:**

SSL/TLS certificates are crucial for encrypted communication. Testing certificate handling helps identify security misconfigurations.

**Common SSL/TLS Issues:**

```
SSL/TLS Vulnerabilities
├── Certificate Validation
│   ├── Self-signed certificates
│   ├── Expired certificates
│   ├── Wrong hostname
│   └── Untrusted CA
├── Protocol Issues
│   ├── SSLv3 (POODLE)
│   ├── TLS 1.0 (deprecated)
│   └── Weak cipher suites
├── Certificate Content
│   ├── Weak key size (<2048 bits)
│   ├── SHA-1 signatures
│   └── Missing subject alternative names
└── Implementation
    ├── Certificate pinning bypass
    ├── Hostname verification disabled
    └── Certificate revocation checking
```

**Configuring SSL in SoapUI:**

```xml
<!-- SSL Settings in SoapUI Preferences -->
<soapui-settings>
  <ssl>
    <!-- KeyStore for client certificates -->
    <keyStore>
      <location>${projectDir}/certs/client.jks</location>
      <password>${#Project#keystorePassword}</password>
      <type>JKS</type>
    </keyStore>
    
    <!-- TrustStore for server certificates -->
    <trustStore>
      <location>${projectDir}/certs/truststore.jks</location>
      <password>${#Project#truststorePassword}</password>
    </trustStore>
    
    <!-- SSL Protocols -->
    <enabledProtocols>
      <protocol>TLSv1.2</protocol>
      <protocol>TLSv1.3</protocol>
    </enabledProtocols>
    
    <!-- Cipher Suites -->
    <enabledCipherSuites>
      <suite>TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384</suite>
      <suite>TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256</suite>
    </enabledCipherSuites>
  </ssl>
</soapui-settings>
```

**Testing SSL/TLS Configuration:**

```xml
<securityTest name="SSL Security Scan">
  <targets>
    <target name="HTTPS Endpoint">
      <endpoint>https://api.example.com/secure</endpoint>
    </target>
  </targets>
  
  <scans>
    <!-- Certificate Validation -->
    <scan type="CertificateValidation">
      <checks>
        <check>expiration</check>
        <check>hostname</check>
        <check>chain</check>
        <check>revocation</check>
      </checks>
    </scan>
    
    <!-- Protocol Downgrade -->
    <scan type="ProtocolDowngrade">
      <protocols>
        <protocol>SSLv3</protocol>
        <protocol>TLSv1</protocol>
        <protocol>TLSv1.1</protocol>
      </protocols>
    </scan>
    
    <!-- Weak Cipher Suites -->
    <scan type="CipherScan">
      <excludeWeak>true</excludeWeak>
      <cipherSuites>
        <suite>SSL_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_MD5</suite>
        <suite>SSL_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_SHA</suite>
        <suite>TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA</suite>
      </cipherSuites>
    </scan>
  </scans>
</securityTest>
```

**Groovy Script for SSL Testing:**

```groovy
import javax.net.ssl.*
import java.security.cert.X509Certificate

// Custom SSL context for testing
def testSSLConnection(url) {
    def results = [:]
    
    // Test with strict validation
    try {
        def connection = new URL(url).openConnection()
        connection.connect()
        results.strictValidation = [
            success: true,
            message: "Connection successful with strict validation"
        ]
    } catch (Exception e) {
        results.strictValidation = [
            success: false,
            error: e.message
        ]
    }
    
    // Test with disabled hostname verification
    def trustAllCerts = [
        new X509TrustManager() {
            X509Certificate[] getAcceptedIssuers() { return null }
            void checkClientTrusted(X509Certificate[] certs, String authType) { }
            void checkServerTrusted(X509Certificate[] certs, String authType) { }
        }
    ]
    
    def allHostsValid = [
        verify: { String hostname, SSLSession session -> true }
    ] as HostnameVerifier
    
    def sc = SSLContext.getInstance("TLS")
    sc.init(null, trustAllCerts, new java.security.SecureRandom())
    HttpsURLConnection.setDefaultSSLSocketFactory(sc.getSocketFactory())
    HttpsURLConnection.setDefaultHostnameVerifier(allHostsValid)
    
    try {
        def connection = new URL(url).openConnection()
        connection.connect()
        results.weakValidation = [
            success: true,
            message: "Connection successful with weak validation (VULNERABLE!)"
        ]
    } catch (Exception e) {
        results.weakValidation = [
            success: false,
            error: e.message
        ]
    }
    
    return results
}

// Test endpoint
def url = context.expand('${#Project#secureEndpoint}')
def results = testSSLConnection(url)

if (results.weakValidation.success) {
    log.warn "⚠️ Server accepts connections with disabled certificate validation"
}

if (!results.strictValidation.success) {
    log.error "Certificate validation failed: ${results.strictValidation.error}"
}
```

**Certificate Information Extraction:**

```groovy
// Extract certificate details from response
def connection = new URL(context.expand('${#Project#secureEndpoint}')).openConnection()
connection.connect()

if (connection instanceof HttpsURLConnection) {
    def certs = connection.getServerCertificates()
    
    certs.eachWithIndex { cert, index ->
        log.info "Certificate ${index + 1}:"
        log.info "  Subject: ${cert.getSubjectDN()}"
        log.info "  Issuer: ${cert.getIssuerDN()}"
        log.info "  Serial: ${cert.getSerialNumber()}"
        log.info "  Valid From: ${cert.getNotBefore()}"
        log.info "  Valid To: ${cert.getNotAfter()}"
        log.info "  Algorithm: ${cert.getSigAlgName()}"
        log.info "  Version: ${cert.getVersion()}"
        
        // Check expiration
        def now = new Date()
        if (now.after(cert.getNotAfter())) {
            log.warn "  ⚠️ Certificate EXPIRED"
        }
        if (now.before(cert.getNotBefore())) {
            log.warn "  ⚠️ Certificate not yet valid"
        }
    }
}
```

**SSL Testing Checklist:**

✅ **Certificate Validity:** Check expiration dates
✅ **Chain of Trust:** Verify complete certificate chain
✅ **Hostname Verification:** Ensure certificate matches hostname
✅ **Protocol Support:** Test for weak protocols (SSLv3, TLSv1.0)
✅ **Cipher Strength:** Check for weak ciphers (RC4, DES)
✅ **Key Size:** Verify key length >= 2048 bits
✅ **Signature Algorithm:** Ensure not using SHA-1
✅ **Revocation:** Check CRL/OCSP support
✅ **Certificate Pinning:** Test pinning implementation
✅ **Renegotiation:** Test secure renegotiation

content.title: SQL Injection Testing in SoapUI
content.explanation:
**Identifying Database Injection Flaws:**

SQL injection occurs when untrusted data is sent to an interpreter as part of a command or query.

**SQL Injection Attack Types:**

```
SQL Injection
├── In-band (Classic)
│   ├── Union-based
│   ├── Error-based
│   └── Boolean-based
├── Inferential (Blind)
│   ├── Time-based
│   └── Boolean-based
└── Out-of-band
    ├── DNS exfiltration
    └── HTTP exfiltration
```

**SQL Injection Payload Examples:**

```sql
-- Basic authentication bypass
' OR '1'='1
' OR 1=1--
admin' --

-- Union-based extraction
' UNION SELECT username,password FROM users--
' UNION SELECT @@version,2,3--

-- Blind/time-based
' AND SLEEP(5)--
' AND (SELECT * FROM (SELECT(SLEEP(5)))a)--

-- Error-based
' AND extractvalue(1,concat(0x7e,database()))--

-- Database fingerprinting
' AND '1'='1
' AND '1'='2

-- Stacked queries
'; DROP TABLE users--
'; EXEC xp_cmdshell('dir')--
```

**SoapUI SQL Injection Security Scan:**

```xml
<securityTest name="SQL Injection Scan">
  <targets>
    <target name="User Login">
      <endpoint>${#Project#apiUrl}/auth/login</endpoint>
      <method>POST</method>
      <parameters>
        <parameter name="username"/>
        <parameter name="password"/>
        <parameter name="email"/>
      </parameters>
    </target>
  </targets>
  
  <scans>
    <scan type="SQLInjection">
      <!-- Database types to test for -->
      <databases>
        <database>MySQL</database>
        <database>Oracle</database>
        <database>PostgreSQL</database>
        <database>MSSQL</database>
      </databases>
      
      <!-- Injection points -->
      <parameters>
        <parameter name="username">
          <payloads>
            <payload>' OR '1'='1</payload>
            <payload>admin' --</payload>
            <payload>' UNION SELECT * FROM users--</payload>
            <payload>' AND SLEEP(5)--</payload>
          </payloads>
        </parameter>
        <parameter name="email">
          <payloads>
            <payload>' OR '1'='1'--</payload>
            <payload>' UNION SELECT null,username,null FROM users--</payload>
          </payloads>
        </parameter>
      </parameters>
      
      <!-- Detection patterns -->
      <detection>
        <errorPatterns>
          <!-- MySQL -->
          <pattern>SQL syntax.*MySQL</pattern>
          <pattern>You have an error in your SQL syntax</pattern>
          
          <!-- Oracle -->
          <pattern>ORA-[0-9]{5}</pattern>
          <pattern>Oracle.*Driver</pattern>
          
          <!-- PostgreSQL -->
          <pattern>PostgreSQL.*ERROR</pattern>
          <pattern>unterminated quoted string</pattern>
          
          <!-- MSSQL -->
          <pattern>Microsoft OLE DB.*SQL Server</pattern>
          <pattern>Unclosed quotation mark</pattern>
        </errorPatterns>
        
        <!-- Time-based detection threshold -->
        <timeThreshold>5000</timeThreshold>
      </detection>
    </scan>
  </scans>
</securityTest>
```

**Groovy Script for Advanced SQL Injection Testing:**

```groovy
// Custom SQL injection tester
def testSQLInjection(endpoint, parameter, payload) {
    def request = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("SQLTestRequest")
    request.setPropertyValue(parameter, payload)
    
    def startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
    request.run(testRunner, context)
    def responseTime = System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime
    
    def status = request.getPropertyValue("httpResponseCode")
    def response = request.getPropertyValue("response")
    
    return [
        status: status,
        response: response,
        responseTime: responseTime
    ]
}

// Database fingerprinting
def fingerprintDatabase() {
    def payloads = [
        "' AND '1'='1",
        "' AND '1'='2",
        "' AND 1=1--",
        "' AND 1=2--"
    ]
    
    def results = []
    payloads.each { payload ->
        def result = testSQLInjection("username", payload)
        results.add([payload: payload, result: result])
    }
    
    // Analyze behavior
    if (results[0].result.response.contains("MySQL")) {
        log.info "Detected MySQL database"
    }
    if (results[0].result.response.contains("ORA-")) {
        log.info "Detected Oracle database"
    }
}

// Time-based blind detection
def testTimeBased() {
    def baseline = testSQLInjection("username", "' AND '1'='1").responseTime
    def sleepPayload = "' AND SLEEP(5)--"
    def sleepResult = testSQLInjection("username", sleepPayload)
    
    if (sleepResult.responseTime > baseline + 4000) {
        log.warn "⚠️ Time-based SQL injection detected"
    }
}

// Union-based extraction
def testUnionExtraction() {
    def payloads = [
        "' UNION SELECT null--",
        "' UNION SELECT null,null--",
        "' UNION SELECT null,null,null--",
        "' UNION SELECT @@version,2,3--",
        "' UNION SELECT table_name,null,null FROM information_schema.tables--"
    ]
    
    payloads.each { payload ->
        def result = testSQLInjection("username", payload)
        if (result.response.contains("version") || 
            result.response.contains("table")) {
            log.warn "⚠️ Union-based extraction possible with payload: ${payload}"
        }
    }
}
```

**SQL Injection Testing Checklist:**

| Test Type | Payload | Success Indicator |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|
| **Authentication Bypass** | ' OR '1'='1 | Login successful |
| **Error-based** | ' | Database error message |
| **Union-based** | ' UNION SELECT null-- | Column count mismatch |
| **Boolean Blind** | ' AND '1'='1 vs '1'='2 | Different responses |
| **Time Blind** | ' AND SLEEP(5)-- | Response delay |
| **Stacked Queries** | '; DROP TABLE users-- | 500 error |
| **Out-of-band** | '; EXEC xp_dirtree | External interaction |

**Prevention Recommendations:**

✅ Use parameterized queries/prepared statements
✅ Apply strict input validation
✅ Use stored procedures
✅ Escape special characters
✅ Apply least privilege principle
✅ Use WAF for additional protection
✅ Regular security audits

content.title: Fuzzing and Buffer Overflow Testing
content.explanation:
**Finding Memory Corruption Vulnerabilities:**

Fuzzing involves sending unexpected, malformed, or random data to an API to cause crashes or unexpected behavior. Buffer overflows occur when more data is written to a buffer than it can hold.

**Fuzzing Strategies:**

```
Fuzzing Types
├── Mutation-based
│   ├── Bit flips
│   ├── Byte flips
│   ├── Arithmetic
│   └── Boundaries
├── Generation-based
│   ├── Protocol-aware
│   ├── Schema-based
│   └── Grammar-based
└── Evolutionary
    ├── Genetic algorithms
    └── Coverage-guided
```

**SoapUI Fuzzing Configuration:**

```xml
<securityTest name="Fuzzing Scan">
  <targets>
    <target name="User Input Fields">
      <parameters>
        <parameter name="id"/>
        <parameter name="name"/>
        <parameter name="email"/>
        <parameter name="age"/>
      </parameters>
    </target>
  </targets>
  
  <scans>
    <scan type="Fuzzing">
      <!-- Fuzzing strategies -->
      <strategies>
        <!-- Boundary values -->
        <strategy name="Boundary">
          <values>
            <value>0</value>
            <value>1</value>
            <value>-1</value>
            <value>2147483647</value>
            <value>-2147483648</value>
            <value>999999999999</value>
          </values>
        </strategy>
        
        <!-- Long strings -->
        <strategy name="LongString">
          <lengths>
            <length>100</length>
            <length>1000</length>
            <length>10000</length>
            <length>100000</length>
            <length>1000000</length>
          </lengths>
          <character>A</character>
        </strategy>
        
        <!-- Special characters -->
        <strategy name="SpecialChars">
          <chars>!@#$%^&*()_+{}|:"<>?~`-=[]\;',./</chars>
        </strategy>
        
        <!-- Unicode -->
        <strategy name="Unicode">
          <values>
            <value>\u0000</value>
            <value>\uFFFF</value>
            <value>\u202E</value>
            <value>\u1F4A9</value>
          </values>
        </strategy>
        
        <!-- Format string attacks -->
        <strategy name="FormatString">
          <values>
            <value>%s%s%s%s%s</value>
            <value>%n%n%n%n</value>
            <value>%x%x%x%x</value>
          </values>
        </strategy>
        
        <!-- Integer overflows -->
        <strategy name="IntegerOverflow">
          <values>
            <value>2147483648</value>
            <value>4294967296</value>
            <value>-2147483649</value>
          </values>
        </strategy>
      </strategies>
    </scan>
  </scans>
</securityTest>
```

**Buffer Overflow Testing:**

```groovy
// Buffer overflow testing script
def testBufferOverflow(parameterName, sizes) {
    def request = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("BufferOverflowTest")
    
    sizes.each { size ->
        // Generate payload of specified size
        def payload = "A" * size
        
        log.info "Testing ${parameterName} with ${size} bytes"
        
        request.setPropertyValue(parameterName, payload)
        
        def startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
        request.run(testRunner, context)
        def responseTime = System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime
        
        def status = request.getPropertyValue("httpResponseCode")
        
        // Check for crash indicators
        if (status == null || status == "" || status == "500") {
            log.warn "⚠️ Possible crash at ${size} bytes (status: ${status})"
        }
        
        if (responseTime > 30000) { // 30 seconds
            log.warn "⚠️ Timeout at ${size} bytes - possible DoS"
        }
        
        // Record result
        context.setProperty("test.${parameterName}.${size}", [
            status: status,
            time: responseTime
        ])
    }
}

// Test incremental sizes
def sizes = [
    10, 100, 1000, 5000, 10000, 50000,
    100000, 500000, 1000000, 5000000, 10000000
]

testBufferOverflow("name", sizes)
testBufferOverflow("description", sizes)
testBufferOverflow("data", sizes)

// Analyze results for patterns
sizes.each { size ->
    def result = context.getProperty("test.name.${size}")
    if (result?.status != "200") {
        log.warn "Non-200 response at ${size}: ${result?.status}"
    }
}
```

**Malformed XML/JSON Fuzzing:**

```xml
<!-- Malformed XML payloads -->
<fuzzing>
  <xml>
    <!-- Missing closing tag -->
    <payload><root><element>value</root></payload>
    
    <!-- Invalid characters -->
    <payload><root>� invalid �</root></payload>
    
    <!-- Deep nesting -->
    <payload><root><root><root><root><root><root><root><root><root><root>value</root></root></root></root></root></root></root></root></root></root></payload>
    
    <!-- XML bomb -->
    <payload>
      <!DOCTYPE bomb [
        <!ENTITY a "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa">
        <!ENTITY b "&a;&a;&a;&a;&a;&a;&a;&a;&a;&a;">
      ]>
      <bomb>&b;&b;&b;&b;&b;&b;&b;&b;&b;&b;</bomb>
    </payload>
    
    <!-- XXE attack -->
    <payload>
      <!DOCTYPE foo [
        <!ELEMENT foo ANY>
        <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">
      ]>
      <foo>&xxe;</foo>
    </payload>
  </xml>
  
  <json>
    <!-- Malformed JSON -->
    <payload>{key: "value"}</payload>
    <payload>{"key": value}</payload>
    
    <!-- Duplicate keys -->
    <payload>{"key":"value","key":"duplicate"}</payload>
    
    <!-- Deep nesting -->
    <payload>{"a":{"b":{"c":{"d":{"e":{"f":{"g":"value"}}}}}}}</payload>
    
    <!-- Type confusion -->
    <payload>{"age":"not-a-number"}</payload>
    <payload>{"active":"true"}</payload>
    
    <!-- Very large payload -->
    <payload>{"data":"${'A' * 1000000}"}</payload>
  </json>
</fuzzing>
```

**Fuzzing Detection and Analysis:**

```groovy
// Analyze fuzzing results
def analyzeFuzzingResults() {
    def findings = []
    
    // Check for crashes
    testRunner.results.each { result ->
        if (result.status.toString() == "FAILED" && 
            result.error?.message?.contains("Connection refused")) {
            findings.add([
                type: "CRASH",
                step: result.testStep.name,
                payload: result.testStep.getPropertyValue("request")
            ])
        }
    }
    
    // Check for error disclosures
    def errorPatterns = [
        /Stack trace:/,
        /at [a-zA-Z0-9\.]+\([a-zA-Z0-9\.]+:[0-9]+\)/,
        /SQLException/,
        /NullPointerException/,
        /ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException/,
        /BufferOverflowException/
    ]
    
    testRunner.results.each { result ->
        def response = result.testStep.getPropertyValue("response")
        errorPatterns.each { pattern ->
            if (response =~ pattern) {
                findings.add([
                    type: "INFORMATION_DISCLOSURE",
                    pattern: pattern.toString(),
                    step: result.testStep.name
                ])
            }
        }
    }
    
    return findings
}

def findings = analyzeFuzzingResults()
findings.each { finding ->
    log.warn "${finding.type} found in ${finding.step}"
}
```

**Fuzzing Best Practices:**

✅ **Start Small:** Begin with shorter payloads
✅ **Monitor Resources:** Watch CPU, memory usage
✅ **Test Incrementally:** Gradually increase complexity
✅ **Log Everything:** Capture all responses and errors
✅ **Reproduce Crashes:** Verify findings with smaller payloads
✅ **Check Error Messages:** Don't leak sensitive information
✅ **Test All Inputs:** Every parameter, header, and body field
✅ **Use Multiple Strategies:** Combine different fuzzing approaches

**Security Testing Metrics:**

```groovy
// Calculate security metrics
def calculateMetrics(findings) {
    def metrics = [
        totalVulnerabilities: findings.size(),
        criticalCount: findings.count { it.severity == 'critical' },
        highCount: findings.count { it.severity == 'high' },
        mediumCount: findings.count { it.severity == 'medium' },
        lowCount: findings.count { it.severity == 'low' },
        byType: [:],
        byEndpoint: [:]
    ]
    
    findings.each { finding ->
        metrics.byType[finding.type] = metrics.byType[finding.type] ?: 0 + 1
        metrics.byEndpoint[finding.endpoint] = metrics.byEndpoint[finding.endpoint] ?: 0 + 1
    }
    
    // Calculate risk score
    metrics.riskScore = (metrics.criticalCount * 10 +
                         metrics.highCount * 7 +
                         metrics.mediumCount * 4 +
                         metrics.lowCount * 1) / metrics.totalVulnerabilities
    
    return metrics
}
```

content.title: Understanding API Mocking
content.explanation:
**What is Mocking and Why It Matters:**

Mocking is the practice of creating a simulated version of a web service that mimics the behavior of the real service. It's like having a stunt double for your API – it looks and acts like the real thing, but it's under your complete control.

**The Mocking Analogy:**

Think of mocking like a flight simulator for pilots:
- Real airplane (actual API) is expensive, dangerous to practice on
- Flight simulator (mock service) behaves like the real thing
- Pilots (developers) can practice safely, test emergencies
- Once trained, they can fly the real plane with confidence

**Why Mocking is Essential:**

```
Development Timeline Without Mocking:
Frontend Team: "We're blocked waiting for the API"
Backend Team: "We're still developing the API"
Testing Team: "Can't test until both are ready"
Result: Delays, idle time, late defect discovery

Development Timeline With Mocking:
Frontend Team: "Building against mock API"
Backend Team: "Developing real API"
Testing Team: "Testing with controlled mocks"
Result: Parallel work, early feedback, faster delivery
```

**Key Benefits of Mocking:**

| Benefit | Description | Impact |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| **Parallel Development** | Frontend and backend work simultaneously | 30-50% faster time-to-market |
| **Isolated Testing** | Test components independently | Earlier defect detection |
| **Cost Reduction** | No need for expensive third-party APIs | Lower testing costs |
| **Reliability** | No dependencies on external services | Consistent test results |
| **Edge Cases** | Simulate rare or error conditions | Better test coverage |
| **Performance** | Fast, predictable responses | Faster test execution |
| **Offline Development** | Work without internet connection | Developer productivity |
| **Demos** | Safe environment for presentations | Professional demonstrations |

**Mocking vs Stubbing vs Virtualization:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      Test Double Hierarchy                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │
│  Stub:     Returns hardcoded responses, minimal logic           │
│            Example: Always returns {"status": "ok"}             │
│                                                                 │
│  Mock:     Simulates behavior, can verify interactions          │
│            Example: Returns different responses based on input  │
│                                                                 │
│  Virtual Service: Full simulation with state and logic          │
│            Example: Complete payment gateway simulation         │
│                                                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**When to Use Mocking:**

✅ **During Development:**
- Backend API not ready
- Third-party API expensive or rate-limited
- Need to agree on API contract first

✅ **During Testing:**
- Unit testing components in isolation
- Integration testing with controlled responses
- Testing error scenarios and edge cases
- Performance testing without real backend

✅ **During Demos:**
- Product demonstrations
- Training sessions
- Sales pitches

✅ **In CI/CD:**
- Automated testing pipelines
- Contract testing
- Parallel build processes

**SoapUI Mocking Capabilities:**

SoapUI provides comprehensive mocking features:

1. **SOAP Mock Services:** Create mocks from WSDL
2. **REST Mock Services:** Define REST endpoints and responses
3. **Dynamic Responses:** Use scripting for complex behavior
4. **Response Delays:** Simulate network latency
5. **Fault Injection:** Test error handling
6. **Stateful Mocks:** Maintain state between requests
7. **Request Logging:** Debug and monitor interactions

**Mocking Use Case Examples:**

```
Scenario 1: Payment Gateway Integration
┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐
│   Your App  │────▶│  Mock       │────▶│  Not Ready  │
│   (in dev)  │     │  Payment    │     │  Real API   │
└─────────────┘     │  Gateway    │     └─────────────┘
                    └─────────────┘
✓ App development continues
✓ Mock returns: success, failure, timeout
✓ Switch to real API when ready

Scenario 2: Testing Error Handling
┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐
│   Test      │────▶│  Mock       │
│   Suite     │     │  Service    │
└─────────────┘     └─────────────┘
                          │
           ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
           ▼              ▼              ▼
    ┌───────────┐  ┌───────────┐  ┌───────────┐
    │ HTTP 200  │  │ HTTP 404  │  │ HTTP 500  │
    │ Success   │  │ Not Found │  │ Error     │
    └───────────┘  └───────────┘  └───────────┘
✓ All scenarios tested
✓ No real API needed
✓ Consistent results
```
