content.title: What You Need Before Installing LoadRunner
content.explanation:
**Planning Your LoadRunner Installation**

Before installing LoadRunner, it's crucial to understand the system requirements and prepare your environment. Proper planning prevents installation failures and ensures optimal performance.

**Minimum vs Recommended Requirements:**

| Component | Minimum Requirements | Recommended Requirements |
|-----------|---------------------|--------------------------|
| **Processor** | 2 GHz dual-core | 3 GHz quad-core or higher |
| **RAM** | 4 GB | 16 GB for Controller, 8 GB for VuGen |
| **Hard Disk** | 10 GB free space | 50 GB SSD for results storage |
| **Operating System** | Windows 10/11, Server 2016+ | Windows Server 2019/2022 |
| **Display** | 1024×768 resolution | 1920×1080 or higher |
| **Network** | 100 Mbps | 1 Gbps dedicated |
| **Browser** | Internet Explorer 11+ | Chrome/Firefox latest |

**Detailed Requirements by Component:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Component-Specific Requirements               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  VuGen (Script Development):                                     │
│  ├── OS: Windows 10/11 Pro/Enterprise, Windows Server 2016+    │
│  ├── RAM: 8 GB minimum, 16 GB recommended                       │
│  ├── Disk: 5 GB for installation, SSD recommended              │
│  ├── Browser: Chrome, Firefox, Edge (latest versions)          │
│  └── Additional: .NET Framework 4.8+, Visual C++ Redistributable│
│                                                                  │
│  Controller (Test Execution):                                    │
│  ├── OS: Windows Server 2016/2019/2022 (preferred)             │
│  ├── RAM: 8 GB minimum, 32 GB for large tests                  │
│  ├── Disk: 10 GB for installation, 100+ GB for results         │
│  ├── Network: 1 Gbps dedicated connection                      │
│  └── Additional: Database access for result storage            │
│                                                                  │
│  Load Generator (Load Generation):                               │
│  ├── OS: Windows or Linux (Red Hat, SUSE, Ubuntu)              │
│  ├── RAM: 4 GB + 2-5 MB per Vuser                              │
│  ├── Disk: 2 GB for installation, logging space                │
│  ├── Network: Bandwidth dependent on protocol                  │
│  └── Additional: Same network segment as target                │
│                                                                  │
│  Analysis (Results Processing):                                  │
│  ├── OS: Windows 10/11, Windows Server 2016+                   │
│  ├── RAM: 8 GB minimum, 16 GB for large results                │
│  ├── Disk: SSD recommended for fast graph generation           │
│  └── Additional: Office for report export (optional)           │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Java Requirements:**

| Component | Java Requirement | Notes |
|-----------|-----------------|-------|
| **VuGen** | Java 8, 11, or 17 | For Java Vuser protocol |
| **Controller** | Java 8 or 11 | For monitoring and reporting |
| **Load Generator** | Java 8 or 11 | For Java-based protocols |
| **Analysis** | Java 8 | For graph generation |

**Database Requirements (for Performance Center):**

| Database | Supported Versions | Notes |
|----------|-------------------|-------|
| **Microsoft SQL Server** | 2016, 2017, 2019, 2022 | Standard/Enterprise |
| **Oracle** | 12c, 18c, 19c | Standard/Enterprise |
| **PostgreSQL** | 12, 13, 14 | Community/Enterprise |

**Network Requirements:**

```
Port Requirements:
├── Controller to Load Generator: 54345 (TCP)
├── Controller to Performance Center: 443 (HTTPS)
├── Load Generator to Target: Dynamic (depending on protocol)
├── Performance Center Web Access: 8080 or 443
└── Database: 1433 (SQL Server) or 1521 (Oracle)

Bandwidth Estimates:
├── Web/HTTP: 100-500 Kbps per Vuser
├── TruClient: 500 Kbps - 2 Mbps per Vuser
├── SAP GUI: 200-400 Kbps per Vuser
├── Citrix: 1-5 Mbps per Vuser
└── Database: 100-300 Kbps per Vuser

Latency Requirements:
├── Controller to Load Generator: < 10 ms
├── Load Generator to Target: < 50 ms
└── Controller to Analysis: < 100 ms
```

**Software Prerequisites Checklist:**

```
Before Installation, Verify:
□ Windows Updates are current
□ .NET Framework 4.8 or higher installed
□ Visual C++ Redistributables (2015-2022)
□ Java JDK/JRE 8 or 11 (if needed)
□ Antivirus exceptions for LoadRunner directories
□ User has Administrator privileges
□ Firewall ports open as required
□ Sufficient disk space with SSD recommended
□ Network connectivity to license server
□ Backup of existing LoadRunner versions (if upgrading)
```

**Virtual Machine Considerations:**

| Hypervisor | Supported | Notes |
|------------|-----------|-------|

content.title: Installing LoadRunner Components
content.explanation:
**From Setup Wizard to Complete Installation**

Follow these detailed steps to install LoadRunner components correctly. Choose the appropriate installation type based on your role and requirements.

**Installation Types:**

| Installation Type | Components Installed | Best For |
|-------------------|---------------------|----------|
| **Complete** | All components (VuGen, Controller, Analysis, Load Generators) | All-in-one machine, learning |
| **VuGen Only** | Script development only | Developers, script creators |
| **Controller Only** | Test execution and monitoring | Test leads, execution managers |
| **Load Generator Only** | Load generation only | Dedicated load generators |
| **Analysis Only** | Results processing only | Report creators |
| **Custom** | Selected components | Advanced users |

**Step 1: Download LoadRunner**

```
1. Visit Micro Focus Support Portal (https://support.microfocus.com)
2. Navigate to Software Downloads → LoadRunner
3. Select LoadRunner version (e.g., LoadRunner 2025)
4. Choose installation package:
   ├── LoadRunner_2025_Windows_Full.iso (Complete, ~4GB)
   ├── LoadRunner_2025_Windows_Components.zip (Individual components)
   └── LoadRunner_2025_Linux_LoadGenerator.tar.gz (Linux LG only)
5. Download the appropriate package
6. Verify checksum (SHA256)

Alternative: Download from Micro Focus License & Download Portal
- Access through your company's license agreement
- Download with provided credentials
```

**Step 2: Prepare for Installation**

```
1. Extract or mount the ISO file:
   Windows: Right-click → Mount
   Command: powershell Mount-DiskImage -ImagePath "C:\Downloads\LoadRunner.iso"

2. Run as Administrator:
   Right-click on Setup.exe → Run as Administrator

3. Temporarily disable antivirus:
   - Windows Defender: Turn off real-time protection
   - Third-party: Disable or add exceptions

4. Close all unnecessary applications:
   - Browser windows
   - Office applications
   - Other development tools

5. Verify prerequisites:
   Run \LoadRunner\Prerequisites\CheckPrerequisites.exe
```

**Step 3: Installation Wizard**

```

│                    LoadRunner Installation Wizard                │

**Step 4: Silent Installation (for Automation)**

```
# Silent installation command
Setup.exe /silent /v"INSTALLDIR=\"C:\LoadRunner\" ADDLOCAL=VuGen,Controller,Analysis"

# Parameters:
# /silent - No UI display
# /v - Pass parameters to MSI
# INSTALLDIR - Installation directory
# ADDLOCAL - Components to install (comma-separated)
# REMOVE - Components to exclude
# LICENSE_SERVER - License server address

# Example: Install VuGen only silently
Setup.exe /silent /v"INSTALLDIR=\"C:\LoadRunner\" ADDLOCAL=VuGen"

# Example: Complete installation with license server
Setup.exe /silent /v"INSTALLDIR=\"C:\LoadRunner\" ADDLOCAL=ALL LICENSE_SERVER=192.168.1.100"
```

**Step 5: Linux Load Generator Installation**

```bash
# 1. Download Linux Load Generator package
# LoadRunner_2025_Linux_LoadGenerator.tar.gz

# 2. Extract package
tar -xzf LoadRunner_2025_Linux_LoadGenerator.tar.gz
cd LoadRunner_2025_Linux_LoadGenerator

# 3. Install prerequisites (as root)
./install_prerequisites.sh

# 4. Run installation
./install.sh

# 5. Follow prompts
Installation Directory [/opt/HP/HP_LoadGenerator]:

# 6. Set environment
source /opt/HP/HP_LoadGenerator/env.sh

# 7. Start Load Generator service
/opt/HP/HP_LoadGenerator/bin/lg_agent_start

# 8. Verify installation
/opt/HP/HP_LoadGenerator/bin/lg_agent_status
```

**Step 6: Post-Installation Steps**

```
1. Restart computer (if prompted)

2. Verify installation:
   Start Menu → Micro Focus LoadRunner →
   ├── Virtual User Generator
   ├── Controller
   └── Analysis

3. Create desktop shortcuts (optional)
   Right-click on executables → Send to → Desktop

4. Check Windows services:
   Services.msc → Look for:
   ├── LoadRunner Controller Service
   ├── LoadRunner Agent Service
   └── LoadRunner License Service

5. Verify environment variables:
   System Properties → Advanced → Environment Variables
   M_HOME should point to LoadRunner installation

6. Test basic functionality:
   - Open VuGen → Create new script → Record a simple web page
   - Open Controller → Create simple scenario → Run test
   - Open Analysis → Open results → Generate graph
```

content.title: Post-Installation Configuration for Optimal Performance
content.explanation:
**Fine-Tuning Your LoadRunner Installation**

After installation, proper configuration ensures LoadRunner performs optimally and integrates with your environment.

**1. License Configuration**

```
License Types:
├── Evaluation License (30 days, 50 Vusers)
│   └── Automatically activated after installation
├── Permanent License (Perpetual or term)
│   └── Enter license key in License Utility
├── Network License (Floating licenses)
│   └── Configure license server connection

Configuring Network License:
1. Start Menu → LoadRunner → License Utility
2. Select "Network License"
3. Enter license server: license.company.com
4. Test connection
5. Verify available licenses

License Commands:
# Check license status
lmstat -a -c @license-server

# View licenses in LoadRunner
lr_license_manager -list

# Add license key
lr_license_manager -add XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX
```

**2. Load Generator Configuration**

```
Windows Load Generator Configuration:
1. LoadRunner → Controller → Load Generators tab
2. Add new generator:
   - Name: LG1
   - Platform: Windows
   - IP/Hostname: 192.168.1.101
3. Test connection
4. Set status to Ready

Configuration File (lr_agent.cfg):
# C:\Program Files\Micro Focus\LoadRunner\config\lr_agent.cfg
[general]
agent_port=54345
max_vusers=2000
log_level=ERROR
enable_ssl=0

[performance]
thread_pool_size=50
socket_buffer_size=65536

[security]
require_authentication=0
trusted_hosts=192.168.1.100

Linux Load Generator Configuration:
# /opt/HP/HP_LoadGenerator/conf/lg.cfg
AGENT_PORT=54345
MAX_VUSERS=1500
LOG_LEVEL=ERROR
```

**3. Runtime Settings Configuration**

```
VuGen Runtime Settings (Default):
├── Run Logic: Run (3 iterations)
├── Pacing: As soon as the previous iteration ends
├── Log: Standard log
├── Think Time: Replay as recorded
├── General: Disable script step debugger
├── Network: Use system proxy settings
├── Browser: Internet Explorer 11 emulation

Recommended Runtime Settings for Load Tests:
├── Run Logic: Run (with duration, not iterations)
├── Pacing: After the previous iteration ends
├── Log: Send messages only when error occurs
├── Think Time: Ignore or multiply by 0.5-0.7
├── General: Enable multithreading
├── Network: Simulate browser cache
├── Browser: Use browser cache
├── ContentCheck: Define warnings as errors
```

**4. Firewall and Port Configuration**

```
Windows Firewall Rules:
# Add inbound rules for LoadRunner
netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="LoadRunner Controller" dir=in action=allow protocol=TCP localport=54345
netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="LoadRunner Agent" dir=in action=allow protocol=TCP localport=54345
netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="LoadRunner License" dir=in action=allow protocol=TCP localport=27000

Linux Firewall (iptables):
# Add rules for Load Generator
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 54345 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --sport 54345 -j ACCEPT
service iptables save

Linux Firewall (firewalld):
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=54345/tcp
firewall-cmd --reload
```

**5. Memory and Performance Tuning**

```
Windows System Tuning:
# Increase system limits
[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters]
"MaxUserPort"=dword:0000fffe (65534)
"TcpTimedWaitDelay"=dword:0000001e (30)
"TcpNumConnections"=dword:00fffffe (16777214)

# Increase virtual memory
System Properties → Advanced → Performance → Settings → Advanced → Virtual memory
Initial size: 1.5 × RAM
Maximum size: 2 × RAM

# LoadRunner memory settings
# Edit lr_agent.cfg
max_memory_mb=4096

Linux System Tuning:
# /etc/sysctl.conf
net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 1024 65535
net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse = 1
net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout = 30
net.core.somaxconn = 1024
fs.file-max = 1000000

# Apply changes
sysctl -p

# User limits (/etc/security/limits.conf)
* soft nofile 1000000
* hard nofile 1000000
* soft nproc unlimited
* hard nproc unlimited
```

**6. Database Configuration (for Performance Center)**

```
SQL Server Configuration:
1. Create database: CREATE DATABASE LoadRunnerDB;
2. Create login: CREATE LOGIN lruser WITH PASSWORD = 'strongpassword';
3. Grant permissions: EXEC sp_addrolemember 'db_owner', 'lruser';
4. Configure connection string in Performance Center

Oracle Configuration:
1. Create tablespace
2. Create user: CREATE USER lruser IDENTIFIED BY password;
3. Grant permissions: GRANT CONNECT, RESOURCE, DBA TO lruser;
4. Configure TNSNAMES.ORA
```

**7. Protocol Configuration**

```
Web Protocol Settings:
# Enable advanced web features
web_set_sockets_option("SSL_VERSION", "TLSv1.2");
web_set_option("MaxRedirectionDepth", 5);
web_set_option("SupportFrames", 1);

Database Protocol Settings:
# Set database connection properties
lr_db_connect("Server={db_server}",
    "User={db_user}",
    "Password={db_password}",
    "Database={db_name}",
    "Driver=SQL Server Native Client 11.0",
    LAST);

SAP GUI Protocol Configuration:
# sapgui.cfg
sapgui_session_pool_size = 10
sapgui_connection_timeout = 60
sapgui_keepalive = 1
```

**8. Integration Configuration**

```
ALM/Quality Center Integration:
1. Tools → ALM/Quality Center Connection
2. Enter ALM Server URL
3. Enter credentials
4. Select domain/project
5. Test connection

Jenkins Integration:
# Jenkins plugin configuration
1. Install LoadRunner Jenkins plugin
2. Configure LoadRunner installation path
3. Set license server
4. Configure result storage

SiteScope Integration:
1. Tools → SiteScope Connection
2. Enter SiteScope server URL
3. Enter credentials
4. Select monitors to display
```

**9. Environment Variables Configuration**

```
System Environment Variables:
M_HOME = C:\Program Files\Micro Focus\LoadRunner
PATH = %PATH%;%M_HOME%\bin;%M_HOME%\bin\runtime
LR_PATH = %M_HOME%
LR_AGENT_PORT = 54345
LR_LICENSE_SERVER = @license-server

User Environment Variables:
TEMP = D:\Temp (redirect to fast drive)
TMP = D:\Temp
LR_RESULTS_DIR = D:\LoadRunnerResults
```

**10. Security Configuration**

```
SSL/TLS Configuration:
# Enable SSL for Controller-Agent communication
lr_agent.cfg:
[security]
enable_ssl=1
certificate_file=C:\LoadRunner\certificates\agent.crt
private_key_file=C:\LoadRunner\certificates\agent.key

User Authentication:
# Require authentication for load generators
lr_agent.cfg:
[security]
require_authentication=1
trusted_hosts=192.168.1.0/24

Certificate Management:
# Import certificates
certmgr.msc → Import → LoadRunner certificates
```

**11. Configuration Verification**

```
Verification Steps:
1. Check license status:
   LoadRunner → License Utility → Verify licenses

2. Test load generator connections:
   Controller → Load Generators → Select all → Connect

3. Run sample test:
   File → Open → Sample Scripts → BasicScript
   Run test with 5 users

4. Verify results:
   Analysis → Open results → Check graphs

5. Check logs:
   %M_HOME%\logs\*.log for errors

Configuration Checklist:
□ License properly configured
□ Load generators connected
□ Firewall ports open
□ Runtime settings optimized
□ Environment variables set
□ Protocol settings configured
□ Integrations tested
□ Results storage location verified
□ Backups of configuration files
```

content.title: Solving Common Installation and Configuration Problems
content.explanation:
**When Things Go Wrong: Diagnosis and Resolution**

Even with careful planning, installation issues can occur. Here's how to diagnose and resolve common problems.

**1. Installation Failures**

| Problem | Symptoms | Solution |
|---------|----------|----------|
| **Prerequisites missing** | Setup fails with error code 1603 | Run PrerequisitesChecker, install missing components |
| **Insufficient disk space** | Installation stops, disk full error | Free space, move TEMP to another drive |
| **Antivirus interference** | Files not copied, access denied | Disable antivirus during installation |
| **Windows Update required** | Setup fails, compatibility warning | Run Windows Update, restart, retry |
| **Corrupted installer** | CRC errors, extraction fails | Redownload, verify checksum |
| **Permission denied** | Cannot write to Program Files | Run as Administrator |

**Installation Log Analysis:**
```
# Find installation logs
%TEMP%\LoadRunner_Install.log
%TEMP%\MSI*.log

# Check for errors
findstr /i "error fail" %TEMP%\LoadRunner_Install.log

# Common error codes:
# 1603 - Fatal error during installation
# 1605 - Product uninstalled
# 1618 - Another installation in progress
# 1638 - Newer version already installed
```

**2. License Issues**

| Problem | Symptoms | Solution |
|---------|----------|----------|
| **No licenses available** | "No licenses available" error | Check license server, available counts |
| **License expired** | Warning at startup | Renew license or request extension |
| **License server unreachable** | Connection timeout | Check network, firewall, server status |
| **Wrong license type** | Features disabled | Install correct license type |
| **License count insufficient** | Cannot start enough Vusers | Purchase additional licenses |

**License Troubleshooting Commands:**
```
# Check license server status
lmstat -a -c @license-server

# Test license server connection
telnet license-server 27000

# Verify license file
lr_license_manager -verify license_file.lic

# Force license refresh
lr_license_manager -refresh
```

**3. Load Generator Connection Issues**

| Problem | Symptoms | Solution |
|---------|----------|----------|
| **Connection refused** | "Failed to connect to load generator" | Check if agent running, firewall |
| **Authentication failed** | Access denied | Check credentials, trust settings |
| **Timeout** | Connection attempt times out | Network latency, increase timeout |
| **Version mismatch** | Incompatible version error | Match LoadRunner versions |
| **Resource exhausted** | Cannot start new Vusers | Check generator capacity |

**Load Generator Diagnostics:**
```
# Windows: Check agent service
sc query lr_agent
net start lr_agent

# Linux: Check process
ps aux | grep lr_agent

# Test connectivity
ping load-generator

# Check port
Test-NetConnection load-generator -Port 54345  # PowerShell
nc -zv load-generator 54345  # Linux

# View agent log
Windows: %M_HOME%\logs\agent_log.txt
Linux: /opt/HP/HP_LoadGenerator/logs/agent.log
```

**4. Component Launch Issues**

| Problem | Symptoms | Solution |
|---------|----------|----------|
| **VuGen won't start** | Crashes on launch | Check Java version, reinstall VC++ redist |
| **Controller freezes** | Unresponsive when opening | Check results directory permissions |
| **Analysis errors** | Cannot open results | Check results file integrity |
| **DLL not found** | Missing DLL error | Reinstall, copy from another machine |
| **COM registration failed** | Class not registered | Run regsvr32 on required DLLs |

**Component Repair:**
```
# Repair installation
Control Panel → Programs → LoadRunner → Change → Repair

# Re-register COM components
cd %M_HOME%\bin
regsvr32 lr_vugen.dll
regsvr32 lr_controller.dll
regsvr32 lr_analysis.dll

# Reset user settings
%APPDATA%\Micro Focus\LoadRunner → Rename folder
```

**5. Performance Issues After Installation**

| Problem | Symptoms | Solution |
|---------|----------|----------|
| **Slow script execution** | Replay takes too long | Check think time settings, logging level |
| **Controller lag** | Slow response in UI | Reduce active monitors, increase memory |
| **High CPU usage** | 100% CPU in LoadRunner | Check for infinite loops, reduce threads |
| **Out of memory** | Crashes with OOM error | Increase heap, reduce result logging |
| **Network bottleneck** | Slow result transfer | Upgrade network, compress results |

**Performance Optimization:**
```
# Increase Java heap for Analysis
%M_HOME%\bin\Analysis.ini
-Xmx2048m → -Xmx4096m

# Reduce logging in load tests
Runtime Settings → Log → Send messages only when error occurs

# Disable unnecessary services
services.msc → Disable unused LoadRunner services
```

**6. Protocol-Specific Issues**

| Protocol | Common Issue | Solution |
|----------|--------------|----------|
| **Web/HTTP** | SSL/TLS errors | Update Java, configure certificates |
| **TruClient** | Browser compatibility | Install correct browser version |
| **SAP GUI** | Connection fails | Check SAP GUI client version |
| **Citrix** | ICA channel errors | Verify Citrix receiver version |
| **Database** | Driver not found | Install database client drivers |

**7. Uninstallation Issues**

| Problem | Symptoms | Solution |
|---------|----------|----------|
| **Incomplete uninstall** | Components remain | Run uninstaller as Administrator |
| **Cannot uninstall** | MSI error | Use Microsoft Program Install and Uninstall troubleshooter |
| **Registry leftovers** | Reinstall fails | Clean registry manually |
| **Service won't stop** | Service in use | Stop service before uninstall |

**Clean Uninstallation Process:**
```
1. Control Panel → Programs → Uninstall LoadRunner
2. Restart computer
3. Delete installation directory
4. Clean registry:
   regedit → Delete HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Mercury Interactive
   regedit → Delete HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Mercury Interactive
5. Delete temporary files: %TEMP%\*LoadRunner*
6. Reboot again
```

**8. Installation Troubleshooting Toolkit**

```
# Diagnostic Commands
# Check system info
msinfo32

# Check Windows Installer version
msiexec /?

# Check .NET Framework versions
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\NET Framework Setup\NDP" /s

# Check Visual C++ Redistributables
wmic product where "name like 'Microsoft Visual C++%'" get name,version

# Check environment variables
set | findstr LR

# Check disk space
fsutil volume diskfree C:

# Check memory
wmic memorychip get capacity

# Check OS version
ver

# Useful Tools
Process Explorer - Check running processes
TCPView - Check network connections
DebugView - View debug output
ProcMon - Monitor registry and file access
```

**9. Installation Verification Checklist**

```
□ All components launch without errors
□ License shows correct Vuser count
□ Load generators connect successfully
□ Sample script records and replays
□ Controller can run a simple scenario
□ Analysis can open and display results
□ Logs show no critical errors
□ Firewall ports are properly configured
□ Performance meets expectations
□ Backups of configuration are saved
□ Documentation of setup is complete
```

content.title: Specialized Installations for Enterprise Environments
content.explanation:
**Beyond Basic Installation: Complex Deployments**

Enterprise environments often require specialized installation scenarios: distributed setups, upgrades, cloud deployments, and integration with other tools.

**1. Distributed Installation Architecture**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Distributed LoadRunner Architecture                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  Development Workstations (Multiple)                            │
│  ┌─────────────────────┐                                        │
│  │ VuGen                │                                        │
│  │ - Script development │                                        │
│  └─────────────────────┘                                        │
│           │                                                     │
│           ▼                                                     │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ Controller Server (Windows Server)                         │ │
│  │ - Central test management                                  │ │
│  │ - Scenario design                                          │ │
│  │ - Test execution control                                   │ │
│  │ - Result collection                                        │ │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│           │                    │                               │
│  ┌────────┴────────┐  ┌────────┴────────┐                     │
│  │ Load Generator 1│  │ Load Generator N│                     │
│  │ (Windows/Linux) │  │ (Windows/Linux) │                     │
│  │ - 1000 Vusers   │  │ - 1000 Vusers   │                     │
│  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘                     │
│           │                    │                               │
│           └────────┬───────────┘                               │
│                    ▼                                            │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ Analysis Workstation (Windows)                             │ │
│  │ - Results analysis                                         │ │
│  │ - Report generation                                        │ │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Installation Steps for Distributed Setup:**

```
Step 1: Install Controller on dedicated server
- Windows Server 2019/2022
- 16+ GB RAM, 4+ cores
- Install "Controller Only"

Step 2: Install Load Generators on multiple machines
- Windows or Linux
- 8+ GB RAM per generator
- Install "Load Generator Only"

Step 3: Configure network
- Open firewall ports (54345)
- Ensure low latency (<10ms) between Controller and generators
- Dedicated network segment recommended

Step 4: Add generators in Controller
- Controller → Load Generators → Add
- Enter hostname/IP of each generator
- Test connection → Set to Ready

Step 5: Install VuGen on developer workstations
- Windows 10/11
- Install "VuGen Only"
- Connect to same network

Step 6: Install Analysis on reporting workstation
- Windows 10/11
- Install "Analysis Only"
- Access to result storage
```

**2. Upgrading from Previous Versions**

```
Pre-Upgrade Checklist:
□ Backup all scripts and scenarios
□ Backup configuration files
□ Document current license information
□ Check compatibility of custom code
□ Verify system requirements for new version
□ Plan maintenance window
□ Notify all users of downtime

Upgrade Paths:
├── LoadRunner 12.x → 2023: Direct upgrade
├── LoadRunner 2023 → 2025: Direct upgrade

├── New runtime settings
└── Browser compatibility changes

Automated Script Upgrade:

%M_HOME%\bin\MigrateScripts.exe /source="C:\Scripts" /target="C:\Scripts_2025"
```

content.title: The Virtual User Generator: Your Script Development Environment
content.explanation:
**Where Performance Tests Are Born**

VuGen (Virtual User Generator) is LoadRunner's script development environment. It captures user actions, converts them into executable scripts, and provides tools for enhancement, debugging, and validation.

**What VuGen Does:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    VuGen Core Functions                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  1. Protocol Selection & Recording                              │
│     • Protocol Advisor recommends best protocol                 │
│     • Multi-protocol recording for complex applications         │
│     • Record using proxy, network-level, or browser extension   │
│                                                                  │
│  2. Script Generation                                           │
│     • Convert user actions to code (C, Java, JavaScript, VB)   │
│     • Tree View for visual representation                       │
│     • Script View for manual coding                             │
│                                                                  │
│  3. Script Enhancement                                          │
│     • Parameterization with test data                           │
│     • Correlation of dynamic values                             │
│     • Transactions for measuring response times                 │
│     • Checkpoints for validation                                │
│     • Think time for realism                                    │
│     • Comments for documentation                                │
│                                                                  │
│  4. Debugging & Validation                                      │
│     • Single-step debugging with breakpoints                    │
│     • Replay log analysis                                       │
│     • Snapshot comparison (recorded vs replayed)                │
│     • Output window for messages                                │
│                                                                  │
│  5. Runtime Settings                                            │
│     • Think time configuration                                  │
│     • Logging levels                                            │
│     • Browser emulation                                         │
│     • Proxy settings                                            │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**VuGen Interface Overview:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    VuGen Interface                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  Menu Bar: File, Edit, View, Script, Tools, Help                │
│                                                                  │
│  Toolbar: Record, Replay, Stop, Step Into, Step Over, Run       │
│                                                                  │
│  ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ Solution Explorer                                          │  │
│  │ ├── Script                                                 │  │
│  │ │   ├── vuser_init.c                                       │  │
│  │ │   ├── Action.c                                           │  │
│  │ │   └── vuser_end.c                                        │  │
│  │ ├── Parameters                                             │  │
│  │ ├── Run-Time Settings                                      │  │
│  │ └── Extra Files                                            │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                  │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ Script View / Tree View                                    │  │
│  │                                                             │  │
│  │ web_url("home",                                            │  │
│  │     "URL=https://example.com/",                           │  │
│  │     LAST);                                                  │  │
│  │                                                             │  │
│  │ web_submit_data("login",                                   │  │
│  │     "Action=https://example.com/login",                   │  │
│  │     "Method=POST",                                         │  │
│  │     ITEMDATA,                                               │  │
│  │     "Name=username", "Value={username}", ENDITEM,        │  │
│  │     "Name=password", "Value={password}", ENDITEM,        │  │
│  │     LAST);                                                  │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                  │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ Output / Replay Log / Correlation Results                  │  │
│  │ [2025-03-15 10:30:45] Starting replay                     │  │
│  │ [2025-03-15 10:30:46] Action.c(5): web_url successful     │  │
│  │ [2025-03-15 10:30:47] Action.c(12): web_submit_data OK    │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Script Structure:**

```c
// vuser_init.c - Runs once per Vuser at start
vuser_init()
{
    // Initialize connection, login, etc.
    web_url("home", "URL=https://example.com/", LAST);
    
    lr_output_message("vuser_init completed");
    return 0;
}

// Action.c - Runs repeatedly during test
Action()
{
    // Main business transactions
    
    // Start transaction for measurement
    lr_start_transaction("Search");
    
    web_submit_data("search",
        "Action=https://example.com/search",
        "Method=POST",
        ITEMDATA,
        "Name=query", "Value={searchTerm}", ENDITEM,
        LAST);
    
    // Check for expected content
    web_reg_find("Text=Results found", LAST);
    
    // End transaction
    lr_end_transaction("Search", LR_AUTO);
    
    // Think time between actions
    lr_think_time(5);
    
    return 0;
}

// vuser_end.c - Runs once at end
vuser_end()
{
    // Cleanup, logout
    web_url("logout", "URL=https://example.com/logout", LAST);
    
    lr_output_message("vuser_end completed");
    return 0;
}
```

**Key Concepts:**

| Concept | Description | Importance |
|---------|-------------|------------|
| **Vuser** | Virtual User - simulated user | Core unit of load |
| **Action** | Logical section of script (init, action, end) | Organizes script flow |
| **Transaction** | Measurable unit of work | Response time measurement |
| **Parameter** | Variable that changes per iteration | Data-driven testing |
| **Correlation** | Dynamic value capture | Handles session data |
| **Checkpoint** | Verification of expected content | Validates responses |
| **Think Time** | Delay between user actions | Simulates real users |

content.title: Capturing Real User Behavior: Recording Techniques
content.explanation:
**From User Actions to Test Scripts**

Recording is the first step in script creation. VuGen captures the communication between the client and server, converting it into script code.

**Protocol Selection:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Protocol Selection Guide                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  Application Type              │ Recommended Protocol           │
│─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│
│  Web Application (HTML)        │ Web - HTTP/HTML                │
│  Single Page App (React/Angular)│ Web - HTTP/HTML + TruClient   │
│  REST/SOAP APIs                │ Web Services                   │
│  SAP GUI Client                │ SAP GUI                        │
│  Oracle Forms                  │ Oracle NCA                     │
│  Citrix Virtual Apps           │ Citrix ICA                     │
│  Database (SQL)                │ MS SQL / Oracle (DB)           │
│  Java Application              │ Java Vuser                     │
│  .NET Application              │ .NET Vuser                     │
│  Mobile App                    │ Mobile App (iOS/Android)       │
│  Mainframe 3270                │ Terminal Emulation (RTE)       │
│  Mixed Technologies            │ Multi-Protocol                 │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Using Protocol Advisor:**

```
Protocol Advisor helps choose the right protocol automatically:

1. VuGen → File → New Script → Protocol Advisor
2. Enter application URL or path
3. Click "Start Recording"
4. Perform typical user actions
5. Stop recording
6. Advisor analyzes traffic and recommends:

Recommended Protocols:
├── Primary: Web - HTTP/HTML (100%)
├── Secondary: Web Services (45%)
├── Detected: AJAX calls - Consider TruClient
└── Detected: HTTPS - SSL/TLS will be handled
```

**Recording Methods:**

| Method | How It Works | Best For | Advantages | Limitations |
|--------|--------------|----------|------------|-------------|
| **Proxy Recording** | VuGen acts as proxy between browser and server | Most web applications | Clean script, no browser dependency | May miss some client-side events |
| **Network-Level** | Captures packets at network level | Applications that can't use proxy | No application modification needed | Captures all traffic, may need filtering |
| **Browser Extension** | Extension records browser events | AJAX-heavy applications | Captures client-side events | Browser-specific, may miss low-level details |
| **Citrix ICA** | Captures screen and keyboard events | Citrix virtualized apps | Works with any published app | Higher resource usage |
| **Cross-Platform** | Records on remote machines | Mobile, non-Windows apps | Platform independent | Network overhead |

**Step-by-Step Recording Process:**

```
Step 1: Create New Script
File → New Script → Select Protocol → Create

Step 2: Configure Recording Options
├── Recording mode: HTML-based (recommended for web)
├── Script type: C (or Java/JavaScript)
├── Target URL: https://example.com
├── Working directory: Default
├── Recording into Action: Action
└── Advanced options:
    ├── Support charset: UTF-8
    ├── Recording scheme: HTTP/HTTPS
    └── Correlation during recording: Enabled

Step 3: Start Recording
Click Record button → Browser opens automatically

Step 4: Perform User Actions
├── Navigate to login page
├── Enter username and password
├── Click login button
├── Navigate to search page
├── Enter search term
├── Click search
├── View results
└── Logout

Step 5: Stop Recording
Click Stop Recording in VuGen toolbar

Step 6: Review Generated Script
VuGen displays recorded steps in Tree View or Script View
```

**Recording Options Configuration:**

```
Recording Options Dialog:

General Tab:
├── Recording mode:
│   ○ HTML-based (better readability)
│   ○ URL-based (more detailed)
├── Script type:
│   ○ C (standard, best performance)
│   ○ Java (for Java Vusers)
│   ○ JavaScript (for TruClient)
├── Recording into:
│   ○ vuser_init (for login)
│   ○ Action (for main flow)
│   ○ vuser_end (for logout)

Advanced Tab:
├── Support charset: UTF-8
├── Recording scheme: HTTP/HTTPS
├── Correlation during recording: Enable
├── Add comments: Enable
├── Save snapshots: Enable
├── Think time: Record as lr_think_time
└── Header handling: Record all headers

HTTP Properties Tab:
├── User-Agent: Internet Explorer 11
├── Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml
├── Accept-Language: en-US
├── Keep-Alive: Enabled
└── Authentication: Handle automatically
```

**Generated Script Example:**

```c
// After recording a simple login-search-logout flow

vuser_init()
{
    // Home page
    web_url("example.com",
        "URL=https://example.com/",
        "Resource=0",
        "RecContentType=text/html",
        "Referer=",
        "Snapshot=t1.inf",
        "Mode=HTML",
        LAST);
    
    return 0;
}

Action()
{
    // Login page
    web_url("login",
        "URL=https://example.com/login",
        "Resource=0",
        "RecContentType=text/html",
        "Referer=https://example.com/",
        "Snapshot=t2.inf",
        "Mode=HTML",
        LAST);
    
    // Login submission
    web_submit_data("authenticate",
        "Action=https://example.com/login",
        "Method=POST",
        "RecContentType=text/html",
        "Referer=https://example.com/login",
        "Snapshot=t3.inf",
        "Mode=HTML",
        ITEMDATA,
        "Name=username", "Value=johndoe", ENDITEM,
        "Name=password", "Value=secret123", ENDITEM,
        "Name=submit", "Value=Login", ENDITEM,
        LAST);
    
    // Search page
    web_url("search",
        "URL=https://example.com/search?q=laptop",
        "Resource=0",
        "RecContentType=text/html",
        "Referer=https://example.com/dashboard",
        "Snapshot=t4.inf",
        "Mode=HTML",
        LAST);
    
    // Logout
    web_url("logout",
        "URL=https://example.com/logout",
        "Resource=0",
        "RecContentType=text/html",
        "Referer=https://example.com/search",
        "Snapshot=t5.inf",
        "Mode=HTML",
        LAST);
    
    return 0;
}

vuser_end()
{
    return 0;
}
```

**Recording Best Practices:**

```
✅ DO:
- Plan your recording session before starting
- Record clean, predictable user flows
- Include think time between actions
- Use meaningful names for steps
- Record both happy path and edge cases
- Stop recording when finished
- Review script immediately after recording
- Add comments during recording if possible

❌ DON'T:
- Record unnecessary navigation
- Include personal information in recorded values
- Perform random actions during recording
- Forget to log out
- Record during system maintenance
- Include sensitive data in clear text
- Record with browser extensions that may interfere
```

**Recording Troubleshooting:**

| Problem | Cause | Solution |
|---------|-------|----------|
| **Browser doesn't open** | Proxy settings | Check VuGen proxy configuration |
| **No script generated** | Wrong protocol | Use Protocol Advisor to select correct protocol |
| **Too many steps** | Recording unnecessary actions | Clean recording, stop when done |
| **Missing steps** | AJAX calls not captured | Use TruClient or URL-based recording |
| **HTTPS errors** | SSL certificate | Install certificate, disable SSL validation |
| **Application not responding** | Firewall | Check firewall settings |
| **Script too large** | Too many steps | Split into multiple scripts |

content.title: Making Scripts Dynamic with Test Data
content.explanation:
**From Hardcoded to Data-Driven Testing**

Parameterization replaces hardcoded values with variables that get different values each iteration, simulating real users with unique data.

**Why Parameterization Matters:**

```
Without Parameterization:
web_submit_data("login",
    "Name=username", "Value=johndoe", ENDITEM,
    "Name=password", "Value=secret123", ENDITEM);
// Every Vuser uses the same credentials
// Server caching hides performance issues
// Can't test multiple users

With Parameterization:
web_submit_data("login",
    "Name=username", "Value={username}", ENDITEM,
    "Name=password", "Value={password}", ENDITEM);
// Each Vuser gets unique credentials
// Realistic load simulation
// Better performance measurement
```

**What Can Be Parameterized:**

| Element | Example | Why Parameterize |
|---------|---------|------------------|
| **User credentials** | username, password | Each user needs unique login |
| **Search terms** | query | Different searches per user |
| **Form data** | firstname, lastname, email | Unique user profiles |
| **Dates** | check-in, check-out | Date variations |
| **Product IDs** | productId | Different products per user |
| **Payment info** | credit card, CVV | Avoid duplicate transactions |
| **File names** | uploadFile | Different files per user |
| **URL parameters** | sessionId | Dynamic session handling |

**Parameter Types:**

| Parameter Type | Description | Use Case |
|----------------|-------------|----------|
| **File** | Data from external files (CSV, TXT, Excel) | Large datasets, test data management |
| **Table** | Data from database queries | Dynamic data from DB |
| **User-Defined** | Manually entered values | Small, fixed datasets |
| **Random Number** | Generated random numbers | Unique IDs, quantities |
| **Unique Number** | Guaranteed unique values | Order numbers, transaction IDs |
| **Date/Time** | Current date/time in various formats | Timestamps, future dates |
| **Vuser ID** | Unique Vuser identifier | Per-user tracking |
| **Group Name** | Vuser group name | Group-specific data |
| **Iteration Number** | Current iteration count | Loop control |

**Creating a File Parameter:**

```
Step 1: Prepare Data File (users.dat)
username,password,email
john,pass123,john@test.com
jane,secure456,jane@test.com
bob,test789,bob@test.com

Step 2: Create Parameter in VuGen
1. In script, select value to parameterize (e.g., "johndoe")
2. Right-click → Replace with a parameter
3. Click "New Parameter"
4. Name: username
5. Parameter type: File
6. File path: C:\LoadRunner\Data\users.dat
7. Column: username (by name or number)
8. Select data selection method:
   ○ Sequential: Take values in order
   ○ Random: Random selection
   ○ Unique: Each Vuser gets unique values
9. Click OK

Step 3: Configure Parameter Properties
├── Select next row: Sequential, Random, Unique
├── Update value on: Each iteration, Once
└── When out of values: Cycle, Abort, Continue with last
```

**Parameter Configuration Options:**

```
Data Selection Methods:
├── Sequential: Takes values in order from the file
│   Vuser1: row1, row2, row3
│   Vuser2: row4, row5, row6
│
├── Random: Randomly selects values
│   Each Vuser gets random rows
│   Can repeat values
│
└── Unique: Guarantees unique values across Vusers
    Requires enough data for all Vusers
    Fails if not enough data

Update Value On:
├── Each iteration: New value per loop
├── Once: Same value for all iterations
└── Each occurrence: New value per parameter occurrence

When Out of Values:
├── Cycle: Start over from beginning
├── Abort Vuser: Stop Vuser execution
└── Continue with last: Keep using last value
```

**Advanced Parameter Examples:**

```c
// 1. Multiple parameters from same file
// users.dat: username,password,email,role

web_submit_data("register",
    ITEMDATA,
    "Name=username", "Value={username}", ENDITEM,
    "Name=password", "Value={password}", ENDITEM,
    "Name=email", "Value={email}", ENDITEM,
    "Name=role", "Value={role}", ENDITEM,
    LAST);

// 2. Random number parameter
// Generate random quantity between 1 and 10
[Parameter: quantity]
Type: Random Number
Range: 1-10
Format: %d

web_submit_data("addtocart",
    ITEMDATA,
    "Name=productId", "Value={productId}", ENDITEM,
    "Name=quantity", "Value={quantity}", ENDITEM,
    LAST);

// 3. Date/Time parameter
[Parameter: checkin_date]
Type: Date/Time
Format: %Y-%m-%d
Offset: +7 days

[Parameter: checkout_date]
Type: Date/Time
Format: %Y-%m-%d
Offset: +14 days

web_submit_data("booking",
    ITEMDATA,
    "Name=checkin", "Value={checkin_date}", ENDITEM,
    "Name=checkout", "Value={checkout_date}", ENDITEM,
    LAST);

// 4. Unique number parameter
[Parameter: order_id]
Type: Unique Number
Start: 1000000
Block size: 1000
Format: %d

web_submit_data("order",
    ITEMDATA,
    "Name=orderId", "Value={order_id}", ENDITEM,
    LAST);

// 5. Combined Vuser ID and iteration
lr_output_message("Vuser ID: %s", lr_eval_string("{VuserId}"));
lr_output_message("Iteration: %s", lr_eval_string("{IterationNum}"));
lr_output_message("Username: %s", lr_eval_string("{username}"));
```

**Parameter Functions:**

```c
// lr_eval_string - Get parameter value
char *username = lr_eval_string("{username}");
lr_output_message("Current user: %s", username);

// lr_save_string - Create runtime parameter
char newValue[50];
sprintf(newValue, "user_%d", atoi(lr_eval_string("{VuserId}")));
lr_save_string(newValue, "runtime_username");

// lr_save_int - Save integer as parameter
int count = 42;
lr_save_int(count, "item_count");

// lr_save_datetime - Save formatted date/time
lr_save_datetime("%Y-%m-%d", DATE_NOW, "today");
lr_save_datetime("%Y-%m-%d", DATE_NOW + ONE_DAY, "tomorrow");

// lr_param_sprintf - Formatted parameter creation
lr_param_sprintf("message", "User %s logged in at %s", 
    lr_eval_string("{username}"), lr_eval_string("{timestamp}"));

// lr_param_increment - Increment numeric parameter
lr_param_increment("counter", 1);
```

**Parameterization Strategies:**

| Strategy | Configuration | Use Case |
|----------|--------------|----------|
| **Unique users per Vuser** | File: Sequential, Update: Once | Each Vuser gets one set of credentials for entire test |
| **Rotating users** | File: Sequential, Update: Each iteration | Vuser changes identity each loop |
| **Random selection** | File: Random, Update: Each iteration | Unpredictable user behavior |
| **Data pool sharing** | File: Unique, All Vusers share | All Vusers share one data pool, unique values |
| **Date progression** | Date/Time with offset | Future dates, booking scenarios |

**Parameterization Best Practices:**

```
✅ DO:
- Use meaningful parameter names (username, not param1)
- Ensure enough data for all Vusers and iterations
- Match parameter types to data format
- Test with small dataset first
- Use CSV format for portability
- Handle out-of-values gracefully
- Document data sources
- Parameterize all dynamic values

❌ DON'T:
- Hardcode values that will change
- Use sequential with insufficient data
- Ignore data format mismatches
- Parameterize static values
- Use sensitive data in plain text
- Mix parameter types inconsistently
- Forget to update runtime settings
```

**Parameterization Troubleshooting:**

| Problem | Cause | Solution |
|---------|-------|----------|
| **Parameter not replaced** | Name mismatch | Check {paramName} syntax |
| **Wrong values used** | Column mapping | Verify column name/number |
| **Out of data** | Insufficient rows | Add more data or enable cycling |
| **Format errors** | Data format mismatch | Check quotes, delimiters |
| **Date format wrong** | Format string incorrect | Use correct format specifiers |
| **Random not working** | Seed issue | Use unique for critical data |
| **File not found** | Path incorrect | Use absolute path |

content.title: Handling Dynamic Data: The Art of Correlation
content.explanation:
**Capturing Server-Generated Values for Reuse**

Correlation is the process of capturing dynamic values from server responses and using them in subsequent requests. It's essential for handling session IDs, tokens, and other server-generated data.

**Why Correlation Matters:**

```
Without Correlation:
Request 1: Login
Server Response: Set-Cookie: JSESSIONID=ABC123XYZ
Request 2: Get Profile
Script uses: Hardcoded JSESSIONID=XYZ789ABC
Result: 401 Unauthorized (Session invalid)

With Correlation:
Request 1: Login
Server Response: Set-Cookie: JSESSIONID=ABC123XYZ
Correlation: Capture JSESSIONID=ABC123XYZ
Request 2: Get Profile
Script uses: JSESSIONID={JSESSIONID}=ABC123XYZ
Result: 200 OK (Valid session)
```

**What Needs Correlation:**

| Dynamic Value | Example | Where Found |
|---------------|---------|-------------|
| **Session IDs** | JSESSIONID, PHPSESSID, ASP.NET_SessionId | Cookies, URLs |
| **CSRF Tokens** | csrf_token, authenticity_token | Hidden form fields |
| **Auth Tokens** | JWT, access_token, bearer token | JSON responses, headers |
| **View State** | __VIEWSTATE, __EVENTVALIDATION | ASP.NET hidden fields |
| **Timestamps** | t=1234567890 | URLs, parameters |
| **Sequence Numbers** | reqId=12345 | Request parameters |
| **Transaction IDs** | orderId=ORD-12345 | Order confirmations |

**Automatic Correlation in VuGen:**

```
VuGen's Auto-Correlation Feature:

1. After recording, go to Script → Scan for Correlations
2. VuGen analyzes recorded vs replayed responses
3. Identifies values that differ between runs
4. Suggests correlation rules
5. Automatically adds web_reg_save_param functions

Correlation Scan Results:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Correlation Results                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│ Found 3 dynamic values:                                         │
│                                                                  │
│ 1. JSESSIONID - Session cookie                                  │
│    Location: Response Header → Set-Cookie                       │
│    Pattern: JSESSIONID=([^;]+)                                  │
│    [✓] Correlate                                                 │
│                                                                  │
│ 2. csrf_token - Hidden form field                               │
│    Location: Response Body → Login Page                         │
│    Pattern: name="csrf_token" value="([^"]+)"                │
│    [✓] Correlate                                                 │
│                                                                  │
│ 3. timestamp - URL parameter                                    │
│    Location: Request URL → search.jsp                           │
│    Pattern: t=(\d+)                                             │
│    [✗] Ignore (optional)                                        │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Manual Correlation with web_reg_save_param:**

```c
// Basic correlation function
web_reg_save_param("ParameterName",
    "LB=Left Boundary",
    "RB=Right Boundary",
    "Search=Body",  // Options: Body, Headers, Cookies, All
    "RelFrameId=1", // Optional frame ID
    "Ordinal=1",    // Which occurrence to capture
    LAST);

// Example: Capturing session ID from cookie
web_reg_save_param("JSESSIONID",
    "LB=JSESSIONID=",
    "RB=;",
    "Search=Headers",
    LAST);

web_url("login", "URL=https://example.com/login", LAST);

// Use captured value
web_add_cookie("JSESSIONID={JSESSIONID}; domain=example.com");

// Example: Capturing CSRF token from HTML
web_reg_save_param("csrf_token",
    "LB=name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"",
    "RB=\"",
    "Search=Body",
    LAST);

web_url("login_page", "URL=https://example.com/login", LAST);

web_submit_data("authenticate",
    "Action=https://example.com/login",
    "Method=POST",
    ITEMDATA,
    "Name=username", "Value={username}", ENDITEM,
    "Name=password", "Value={password}", ENDITEM,
    "Name=csrf_token", "Value={csrf_token}", ENDITEM,
    LAST);
```

**Advanced Correlation Functions:**

```c
// web_reg_save_param_ex - Extended with filters
web_reg_save_param_ex(
    "ParamName=sessionId",
    "LB=session=",
    "RB=&",
    SEARCH_FILTERS,
    "Scope=Body",
    "IgnoreRedirections=Yes",
    "RequestUrl=*/login*",
    LAST);

// web_reg_save_param_json - JSON path extraction
web_reg_save_param_json(
    "ParamName=accessToken",
    "QueryString=$.data.token",
    SEARCH_FILTERS,
    "Scope=Body",
    LAST);

// web_reg_save_param_regexp - Regular expression
web_reg_save_param_regexp(
    "ParamName=orderId",
    "Regexp=orderId=(\\d+)",
    SEARCH_FILTERS,
    LAST);

// web_reg_save_param_xpath - XPath extraction
web_reg_save_param_xpath(
    "ParamName=productId",
    "Query=//div[@class='product']/@data-id",
    SEARCH_FILTERS,
    LAST);
```

**Correlation Techniques by Content Type:**

| Content Type | Recommended Method | Example |
|--------------|-------------------|---------|
| **HTML Form Fields** | web_reg_save_param with HTML boundaries | name="csrf_token" value="([^"]+)" |
| **JSON Responses** | web_reg_save_param_json | $.data.sessionId |
| **XML/SOAP** | web_reg_save_param_xpath | //sessionId/text() |
| **HTTP Headers** | web_reg_save_param with Search=Headers | Set-Cookie: JSESSIONID=([^;]+) |
| **URL Parameters** | web_reg_save_param with LB/RB | session=([^&]+) |
| **JavaScript Variables** | web_reg_save_param with regex | var token = '([^']+)' |

**Correlation Examples by Application Type:**

```c
// Example 1: ASP.NET ViewState
web_reg_save_param("ViewState",
    "LB=id=\"__VIEWSTATE\" value=\"",
    "RB=\"",
    "Search=Body",
    LAST);

web_reg_save_param("EventValidation",
    "LB=id=\"__EVENTVALIDATION\" value=\"",
    "RB=\"",
    "Search=Body",
    LAST);

web_submit_data("search",
    ITEMDATA,
    "Name=__VIEWSTATE", "Value={ViewState}", ENDITEM,
    "Name=__EVENTVALIDATION", "Value={EventValidation}", ENDITEM,
    "Name=searchTerm", "Value={searchTerm}", ENDITEM,
    LAST);

// Example 2: JWT Token from JSON
web_reg_save_param_json(
    "ParamName=jwt_token",
    "QueryString=$.token",
    LAST);

web_reg_save_param_json(
    "ParamName=expires_in",
    "QueryString=$.expiresIn",
    LAST);

web_submit_data("login", ...);

web_add_header("Authorization", "Bearer {jwt_token}");

// Example 3: OAuth2 Authorization Code
web_reg_save_param("auth_code",
    "LB=code=",
    "RB=&",
    "Search=Headers",
    LAST);

web_url("oauth_redirect",
    "URL=https://example.com/oauth/callback",
    LAST);

web_submit_data("token_exchange",
    "Action=https://example.com/oauth/token",
    "Method=POST",
    ITEMDATA,
    "Name=code", "Value={auth_code}", ENDITEM,
    "Name=grant_type", "Value=authorization_code", ENDITEM,
    LAST);
```

**Correlation Functions Reference:**

| Function | Purpose | Parameters |
|----------|---------|------------|
| **web_reg_save_param** | Save parameter from response | LB, RB, Search, Ordinal, SaveOffset, SaveLen |
| **web_reg_save_param_ex** | Extended version with filters | Same as above + SEARCH_FILTERS |
| **web_reg_save_param_json** | Extract from JSON | QueryString |
| **web_reg_save_param_xpath** | Extract from XML/HTML | Query |
| **web_reg_save_param_regexp** | Extract with regex | Regexp |
| **web_set_sockets_option** | Socket-level settings | SSL_VERSION, etc. |

**Correlation Best Practices:**

```
✅ DO:
- Always correlate session IDs and tokens
- Test correlation with multiple runs
- Use specific boundaries (LB/RB)
- Add error handling for missing values
- Document correlated values
- Verify captured values before use
- Use ordinal for multiple matches
- Set default values for robustness

❌ DON'T:
- Correlate static values
- Use too broad boundaries
- Ignore correlation warnings
- Assume values always present
- Hardcode dynamic values
- Forget to check correlation in replay
```

**Correlation Troubleshooting:**

| Problem | Cause | Solution |
|---------|-------|----------|
| **Parameter empty** | LB/RB incorrect | Check response, adjust boundaries |
| **Wrong value captured** | Multiple matches, wrong ordinal | Use Ordinal parameter |
| **Script fails after correlation** | Missing required value | Add default value, error handling |
| **Correlation works once then fails** | Value changes format | Check if value format changes |
| **JSON path not found** | Path incorrect | Validate JSON path |
| **Value in headers not found** | Search scope wrong | Use Search=Headers |
| **Special characters in value** | Escape issues | Use web_save_param_unescape |

**Debugging Correlation:**

```c
// Add logging to verify correlation
web_reg_save_param("sessionId",
    "LB=JSESSIONID=",
    "RB=;",
    LAST);

web_url("login", ...);

// Check if parameter was set
if (strlen(lr_eval_string("{sessionId}")) == 0) {
    lr_error_message("Failed to capture sessionId!");
    lr_output_message("Response: %s", lr_eval_string("{Response}"));
}

// Log captured value
lr_output_message("Captured sessionId: %s", lr_eval_string("{sessionId}"));

// Save entire response for analysis
lr_save_string(lr_eval_string("{Response}"), "FullResponse");
```

**Advanced Correlation Techniques:**

```c
// 1. Dynamic boundaries with wildcards
web_reg_save_param("authToken",
    "LB=accessToken: ",
    "RB=\n",
    LAST);

// 2. Capturing multiple values
web_reg_save_param("userIds",
    "LB=<userId>",
    "RB=</userId>",
    "Ordinal=All",
    LAST);

// Then iterate through matches
for (i=1; i<=atoi(lr_eval_string("{userIds_count}")); i++) {
    lr_param_sprintf("currentUserId", "{userIds_%d}", i);
    lr_output_message("User %d: %s", i, lr_eval_string("{currentUserId}"));
}

// 3. Conditional correlation based on response
web_reg_save_param("errorCode",
    "LB=<error>",
    "RB=</error>",
    LAST);

web_reg_save_param("successToken",
    "LB=<token>",
    "RB=</token>",
    LAST);

web_submit_data("process", ...);

if (strlen(lr_eval_string("{errorCode}")) > 0) {
    lr_error_message("Error: %s", lr_eval_string("{errorCode}"));
}
```

**Correlation Strategy Decision Tree:**

```
Is the value dynamic?
├── No → Leave as hardcoded
└── Yes → Is it in the response?
    ├── No → Check other sources (cookies, headers)
    └── Yes → What format?
        ├── HTML/Text → web_reg_save_param with LB/RB
        ├── JSON → web_reg_save_param_json
        ├── XML → web_reg_save_param_xpath
        ├── Header → web_reg_save_param with Search=Headers
        └── Cookie → web_reg_save_param with Search=Cookies
```

content.title: The Command Center of LoadRunner
content.explanation:
**Where Load Tests Are Designed and Controlled**

The Controller is LoadRunner's test management hub. It's where you design load scenarios, assign scripts to Vusers, control test execution, and monitor performance in real-time.

**What the Controller Does:**

├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │

│     • Assign scripts to Vuser groups                           │
│     • Configure load generators                                │
│     • Set schedule (ramp-up, steady, ramp-down)                │
│                                                                  │
│  2. Load Generator Management                                   │
│     • Add/remove load generators                               │
│     • Monitor generator health                                 │
│     • Distribute Vusers across generators                      │
│     • Configure generator settings                             │
│                                                                  │
│  3. Real-Time Monitoring                                        │
│     • Transaction response times                               │
│     • Vuser status (running, ready, finished, error)          │
│     • System resources (CPU, memory, disk, network)           │
│     • Server monitoring via SiteScope                          │
│     • APM integration (Dynatrace, AppDynamics)                 │
│                                                                  │
│  4. SLA Definition                                              │
│     • Set performance goals per transaction                    │
│     • Define thresholds for warnings and failures              │
│     • Real-time SLA alerts                                     │
│                                                                  │
│  5. Test Execution Control                                      │
│     • Start, stop, pause tests                                 │

content.title: Building Your Test Scenario: Groups, Scripts, and Generators
content.explanation:
**The Foundation of Every Load Test**

Configuring a test scenario involves defining Vuser groups, assigning scripts, selecting load generators, and setting runtime configurations.

**Step-by-Step Scenario Configuration:**

```
Step 1: Create New Scenario
1. Open Controller
2. File → New → Scenario
3. Select script(s) to include
4. Choose scenario type (Manual or Goal-Oriented)
5. Click OK

Step 2: Configure Vuser Groups
1. In Design tab, you'll see your script as a group
2. Rename group (e.g., "Browsers", "Buyers", "Admins")
3. Set quantity for each group
4. Assign load generators
5. Configure runtime settings per group

Step 3: Add Multiple Groups (if needed)
1. Right-click in Groups section → Add Group
2. Select script for new group
3. Configure group settings
4. Repeat for each user type

Step 4: Configure Load Generators
1. Click Load Generators tab
2. Add new generators if needed
3. Test connection
4. Assign generators to groups

Step 5: Save Scenario
File → Save As → scenario_name.lrs
```

**Vuser Group Configuration:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Vuser Group Configuration                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  Group: Browsers (50 Vusers)                                    │
│  ├── Script: browse_script.usr                                  │
│  ├── Load Generators: LG1 (30), LG2 (20)                        │
│  ├── Runtime Settings: Standard                                 │
│  ├── Initialize: Before running                                 │

content.title: Setting Performance Goals and Tracking Compliance
content.explanation:
**Defining Success Before You Test**

SLA (Service Level Agreement) configuration allows you to define performance goals and monitor compliance in real-time during test execution.

**SLA Definition:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    SLA Configuration                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  SLA Rule: Transaction Response Time                            │
│  ├── Transaction: Checkout                                      │
│  ├── Condition: Percentile                                      │
│  ├── Threshold: 90% of samples < 2 seconds                     │
│  ├── Measurement interval: 30 seconds                          │
│  ├── Evaluation period: Full test duration                     │
│  └── Actions:                                                   │
│      ├── Log warning when threshold approached                 │
│      ├── Mark SLA as failed when exceeded                      │
│      └── Send alert to monitoring console                      │
│                                                                  │
│  SLA Rule: Average Response Time                                │
│  ├── Transaction: Search                                        │
│  ├── Condition: Average                                         │
│  ├── Threshold: < 500 ms                                       │
│  ├── Measurement interval: 1 minute                            │
│  └── Actions:                                                   │
│      ├── Update graph color                                    │
│      └── Log to results                                        │
│                                                                  │
│  SLA Rule: Error Rate                                           │
│  ├── Transaction: All                                           │
│  ├── Condition: Percentage                                      │
│  ├── Threshold: < 1%                                           │
│  ├── Measurement interval: 1 minute                            │
│  └── Actions:                                                   │
│      ├── Stop test if exceeded                                 │
│      └── Send email alert                                      │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Real-Time SLA Monitoring:**

```
During Test Execution:

SLA Status Dashboard:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    SLA Status (Real-Time)                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│ Transaction  │ Target       │ Current  │ Status │ Trend        │
